story:
Once upon a time, a little Bulbasaur lived at the edge of a sunny meadow. It had a green seed on its back, and every morning it lay in the sunshine so the seed could drink up the light. "Grow, seed, grow," it whispered.

One day a tiny Pidgey couldn't reach the berries at the top of a bush. Bulbasaur stretched out two long vines, snip, snip, and passed the berries down. Then the two friends shared lunch in the sun, and the seed on Bulbasaur's back felt just a little bit bigger.

Ivysaur used to be a little Bulbasaur. Now the seed on its back had opened into a big pink bud, and the bud was getting heavier every day. Ivysaur's legs grew strong from carrying it around. Stomp, stomp, stomp.

One warm afternoon, a sweet smell drifted out of the bud, like honey and rain. Butterflies came to see, and so did all of Ivysaur's friends. "Is it going to bloom?" they asked. "Soon," said Ivysaur, smiling. "When the sun says so."

On a hill covered in flowers lived a big, gentle Venusaur. The flower on its back was so large that it opened like a giant umbrella whenever the sun came out.

The flower's sweet smell made everyone feel calm. When little Pokémon were grumpy or tired, they curled up in its shade, and soon they were yawning and smiling. Venusaur never minded. It liked having friends nap beside it, and the sunnier the day, the brighter its flower glowed.

Charmander had a little flame on the tip of its tail. When Charmander was happy, the flame danced high. When it was sleepy, the flame glowed soft and small, like a night-light.

One afternoon, gray clouds rolled in and rain began to fall. Plip, plop. Charmander tucked its tail close and hurried along. Then a Bulbasaur held out a big leaf. "Share my umbrella!" it said. They walked home together under the leaf, and Charmander's flame burned bright and warm all the way.

Charmeleon was always in a hurry. It wanted to be the fastest, the bravest and the strongest, and its tail flame flickered with excitement all day long.

One evening it raced up a mountain to watch the sunset, huffing and puffing. At the top, an old Charizard was already sitting quietly. "Sit with me," it said. So Charmeleon sat. The sky turned orange, then pink, then purple. "Sometimes the best things come when you slow down," said Charizard. And for once, Charmeleon agreed.

High above the clouds, Charizard spread its wide orange wings and soared. Whoosh! It could fly so high that the towns below looked like toys.

Charizard was very strong, and its fire was very hot. But it had a rule: it never showed off to anyone smaller than itself. Instead, when little Pokémon got lost in the cold mountains, Charizard landed beside them, lit a cozy fire and kept them warm until morning. Then it flew them home, one wingbeat at a time.

Squirtle lived by a sparkling pond and loved to play. When it was startled, it pulled its head and legs into its shell. Pop! When it felt brave again, out they came. Pop, pop, pop!

Squirtle's favorite game was spraying water from its mouth. Swoosh! It sprayed the thirsty flowers. Swoosh! It filled up a puddle for the Psyduck. Swoosh! It accidentally sprayed its best friend. Everyone laughed, even the friend, and they all jumped into the pond together.

Wartortle had a big fluffy tail and furry ears that looked like little wings. When it swam, it swished them to keep its balance, swish, swash, swish, and zipped through the water.

Some folks said that Wartortle's fluffy tail was a sign of a long and happy life. So the old Pokémon by the lake always smiled when Wartortle swam by. "That one will have many birthdays," they said. And Wartortle splashed them, just a little, to say thank you.

Blastoise had two big water cannons on its shell. When it aimed them at the sky, the water shot up so high that it came down like rain.

One hot, dry summer, the farmers' fields were thirsty and the flowers drooped. So Blastoise stomped out to the fields, planted its feet and fired. Fwoosh! Fwoosh! A gentle shower fell over everything. The flowers lifted their heads, the farmers cheered, and a little rainbow appeared right over Blastoise's shell.

Caterpie was a little green bug with a big appetite. Munch, munch, munch. It ate leaves for breakfast, leaves for lunch and leaves for dinner, and it was always ready for more.

On top of its head was a red feeler. When a hungry bird came too close, Caterpie wiggled it and let out a stinky smell. "Phew!" said the bird, and flew away. Caterpie went back to munching. It had important growing to do.

Metapod was very good at one thing: being still. Its shell was hard as stone, and inside, something wonderful was happening, very slowly.

The wind blew. Metapod stayed still. A Rattata ran by. Metapod stayed still. The moon came up and the stars came out, and still Metapod waited, patient as can be. "Aren't you bored?" asked a Pidgey. Metapod couldn't answer, but if it could, it would have said, "I'm busy getting ready." And one morning, it was ready.

One sunny morning, a shell on a branch went crack. Out came Butterfree, stretching its new white wings for the very first time.

Butterfree fluttered from flower to flower, sipping sweet nectar. Its wings were covered in a fine, sparkly dust, and when it flapped, the dust drifted down like glitter. Butterfree flew farther than it had ever crawled, over rivers and hills. It looked down at the leaves it used to munch and laughed. "I'm flying!"

Weedle lived in the forest and loved to eat leaves. It had a small, pointy horn on top of its head, and everyone knew to give it a little room.

Weedle had a wonderful nose. Sniff, sniff. It could tell which leaves were the tastiest just by smelling them. So whenever its friends were hungry, Weedle led the way to the best leaves in the whole forest. They called it the leaf finder, and Weedle was very proud.

Kakuna hung from a tree branch, all wrapped up in its golden shell. It could hardly move at all, but every now and then it stretched, just a tiny bit. Creak.

Inside the shell, Kakuna was busy growing. It dreamed of wings and buzzing and flying fast. The forest friends knew to tiptoe past and let it rest. "Shh," they said to each other. "Kakuna is getting ready." And Kakuna, snug in its shell, dreamed a little more.

Bzzzz! Beedrill zoomed through the forest faster than a falling leaf. It had clear wings, yellow and black stripes, and two pointy stingers on its arms.

Beedrill lived with a big family in a hollow tree. They guarded their home carefully, so visitors always said hello from far away. But when a storm knocked a baby Pidgey out of its nest, the Beedrill buzzed out together, caught the little bird gently and carried it home. Bzzz. Busy as bees, and kind ones too.

Pidgey was a small, cheerful bird who lived in the tall grass. It was gentle and didn't like a fuss, so when trouble came, it flapped its wings very fast. Flap, flap, flap! Up swirled a cloud of sand, and Pidgey hid inside it.

When the sand settled, Pidgey was gone, sitting safely on a branch nearby, giggling. It played this game with its friends every day. They never found it on the first try. Or the second. Or the third.

Pidgeotto had a big job. Every day it flew in wide circles over its forest to make sure everything was all right. Its eyes were so sharp that it could spot a tiny berry from high up in the sky.

When a little Caterpie wandered too far from home, Pidgeotto saw it right away. It swooped down, landed softly and walked the Caterpie back to its tree. "Thank you," said the Caterpie's mother. Pidgeotto just nodded, ruffled its feathers and took off to check the next part of the forest.

Pidgeot had the most beautiful feathers in the sky. When it flew, its long crest streamed behind it in red and yellow, like ribbons in the wind.

And oh, it was fast! Pidgeot could cross a whole valley before you could finish saying its name. "Pidg..." Whoosh! Gone! The little bird Pokémon loved to watch it race the clouds. Someday, they hoped, they would fly just like Pidgeot. And Pidgeot always looped back once, just to wave.

Rattata was small and quick, with a curly tail and two big front teeth. Its teeth never stopped growing, so Rattata chewed on things all day long. Nibble, nibble, nibble.

It chewed on sticks. It chewed on nuts. Once it chewed a whole row of tiny doors into a fallen log, so every little Pokémon in the forest had a house. "Rattata the builder!" they cheered. Rattata just smiled its big toothy smile and went looking for something else to nibble.

Raticate had long whiskers that helped it keep its balance, even when it scurried along the very top of a fence. Tip, tip, tip, and never a wobble.

Raticate liked to keep its home neat and cozy. It gathered soft grass and fluffy feathers and made a nest so comfy that its little Rattata friends always wanted to sleep over. Raticate tucked them in, twitched its whiskers good night and kept watch until everyone was snoring.

Spearow was a small bird with short wings. It couldn't glide like the big birds, so it flapped and flapped as fast as it could. Flappity flap!

What Spearow lacked in size, it made up for in voice. Its cry could be heard far across the fields. So whenever a storm was coming, Spearow climbed to the highest branch and shouted, "Squawk! Squawk!" and every Pokémon in the meadow knew it was time to head home. Little bird, big job.

Fearow had a long neck, a long beak and great big wings. It could fly all day and all night without stopping to rest.

When Fearow flew over the river, it watched the water closely. Then, swish! Its long beak dipped down and came back up with a snack. Fearow was proud of that beak. It used it to fix its nest, to scratch its back and once, to fish a lost hat out of a pond for a very grateful little girl.

Ekans was a long purple Pokémon who loved to curl up in the tall grass. It could coil its body into a perfect spiral, like a cinnamon roll, and take the most comfortable naps.

Ekans flicked its tongue in and out to smell the air. Flick, flick. It could smell when berries were ripe and when rain was coming. "Rain soon," it told its friends one morning. They didn't believe it. But that afternoon, splash! Everyone ran for cover, and from then on, they always listened to Ekans.

Arbok had a pattern on its chest that looked like a big face. When Arbok stretched up tall, the face looked even bigger. Some Pokémon thought it looked fierce. But Arbok had a better idea for it.

Whenever the baby Pokémon in the forest were sad, Arbok stretched up, wiggled and made the face go silly. Wobble, wobble! The babies giggled and giggled. Arbok learned that a face that could look fierce could also make everyone laugh, and that was much more fun.

Once upon a time, in a forest of tall green trees, there lived a little yellow Pikachu with a tail shaped like a lightning bolt. Whenever Pikachu felt happy, its red cheeks went fizz, fizz, pop with tiny sparks.

One stormy night, all of Pikachu's friends were scared of the thunder. So Pikachu climbed the tallest tree, caught a little bit of the storm in its cheeks, and made the whole forest glow like a lamp. And nobody was scared anymore.

When Pikachu touched a shiny Thunder Stone, it grew into Raichu, a bigger, rounder Pokémon with a long, thin tail. Raichu could hold lots and lots of electricity.

Sometimes Raichu held so much that its fur stood on end and its whiskers crackled. Bzzt! Then Raichu pressed the tip of its tail to the ground and let the extra sparks go, zip, into the earth. "Ahh," said Raichu, nice and calm again. Then it went back to its favorite thing: glowing softly in the dark so its friends could find their way.

Sandshrew lived in a dry, sandy place where it hardly ever rained. Its skin was tough and dry, perfect for the desert sun. And whenever it felt shy, it curled up into a tight little ball.

One day Sandshrew was curled up at the top of a sand dune when, oops, it started to roll. Down, down, down it went, bumpity bump, faster and faster, all the way to the bottom. It uncurled, blinked and laughed. Then it climbed right back up to do it again.

Sandslash had a back covered in sharp spikes and long claws for digging. When it curled up, it became a spiky ball that nobody wanted to poke.

But Sandslash's favorite thing was climbing. It dug its claws into tree bark and climbed all the way to the top, scritch, scratch, scritch, to look out over the desert. From up there, it could see where the cactus flowers bloomed and where the cool shade was. Then it climbed down and told all its friends.

Nidoran♀ was a small blue Pokémon with big ears and a little pointed horn. She was gentle and quiet and liked to stay close to her friends.

Her big ears could hear the tiniest sounds: a leaf falling, a Caterpie munching, a raindrop landing on a flower. So when her friends played hide-and-seek, Nidoran♀ always won. "How did you find me?" they asked. She just wiggled her ears and smiled.

Nidorina was a kind Pokémon who looked after the little ones. She had spikes on her back, but when she was with her friends and family, she folded them down flat so nobody would get poked.

At bedtime, all the baby Nidoran snuggled up against her soft blue side. Nidorina hummed a quiet tune and kept them warm. Outside, the wind howled, but inside the burrow everyone was cozy, safe and fast asleep.

Nidoqueen was big and strong, with tough scales like armor. But the most important thing about Nidoqueen was her big, warm heart.

She dug a deep burrow under the hill and made it the safest place in the whole forest. Whenever a storm came, the little Pokémon ran to Nidoqueen's burrow, and she stood in the doorway like a wall while the rain poured down. Not a single drop got in. "Thank you, Nidoqueen," they whispered. "Anytime," she said.

Nidoran♂ was a small purple Pokémon with big ears that stuck straight up. He could turn them this way and that to listen for anything nearby.

Nidoran♂ was brave for his size. When a strange noise came from the bushes, he marched right over, ears up, horn ready. Rustle, rustle... and out hopped a tiny, lost Pidgey. "Oh," said Nidoran♂. "You're just little, like me." So he walked the Pidgey home, ears up all the way.

Nidorino had a hard horn on its head and big ears that could hear far away. It was proud and a little bit bossy, and it liked to stand on the tallest rock and look around.

One day Nidorino's friends needed to cross a stream, but the stepping stones were too far apart. Nidorino pushed a log with its horn, heave, heave, until it made a bridge. Everyone crossed safely. "Not bad for a bossy one," teased a friend. Nidorino laughed. Maybe being strong was best when it helped somebody.

Nidoking was one of the strongest Pokémon around. It had a thick tail, a mighty horn and feet that went STOMP so loudly the whole forest heard.

But Nidoking had a secret: it loved little things. Tiny flowers, tiny bugs, tiny Nidoran who rode on its tail. Every afternoon it gave them rides around the meadow. Stomp, stomp, swish! The little ones squealed with joy. The strongest Pokémon in the forest was also the gentlest.

High on a mountain, when the moon was full and round, the Clefairy came out to dance. They held hands in a circle and twirled, and their soft pink bodies glowed in the moonlight.

Nobody knew exactly why they danced. Some said they were saying hello to the moon. Some said the moon was saying hello back. One little Clefairy was too shy to join in, so it watched from behind a rock. Then the circle opened, a hand reached out, and soon it was dancing too.

Clefable was very shy. It lived in a quiet valley and almost never let anyone see it. But it had the best ears in the world. It could hear a pin drop on the other side of the hill.

At night, Clefable listened to the whole world: crickets chirping, rivers running, Pokémon snoring. And when it was sure nobody was looking, it skipped across the meadow so lightly that it almost flew, hop, float, hop, under the bright full moon.

When Vulpix was born, it had just one fluffy white tail. But as it grew, the tail split, and split again, until Vulpix had six beautiful curly red tails.

Vulpix loved its tails. It counted them every morning. "One, two, three, four, five, six!" When it was cold, it curled them around itself like a blanket. Inside, Vulpix kept a little warm flame. On chilly nights, its friends snuggled close, and Vulpix shared its warmth with everyone.

Ninetales had nine golden tails and soft, shining fur. It was very old and very wise, and it had lived in the forest longer than anyone could remember.

The young Pokémon came to Ninetales with questions. "Why is the sky blue?" "Where does the wind go?" "Will I grow nine tails too?" Ninetales listened to every question, swished its tails and answered each one patiently. And to the little Vulpix who asked about tails, it said, "With a Fire Stone and a brave heart, maybe someday."

Jigglypuff was a round, pink Pokémon who loved to sing. When it took a big breath, its body puffed up like a balloon. Then it sang the softest, sweetest lullaby.

"Jiggly-puff, jiggly-puff..." Everyone who heard it began to yawn. The Pidgey yawned. The Rattata yawned. Even the moon looked sleepy. One by one, every Pokémon in the meadow fell fast asleep. Jigglypuff smiled and kept singing, quietly, just for you. Are you yawning yet?

Wigglytuff was the softest Pokémon you could ever imagine. Its fur was fine and fluffy, like a cloud, and its body was bouncy and stretchy, like a balloon.

When Wigglytuff took a deep breath, it puffed up bigger and bigger. Boing! It bounced across the meadow, and its friends lined up for turns. They jumped on its soft round tummy and boinged into the air, giggling. At the end of the day, everyone curled up on Wigglytuff like the world's comfiest pillow.

Zubat lived in a deep, dark cave. It didn't have any eyes, but that was okay, because Zubat had a trick. It sent out tiny squeaks, eep, eep, and listened to them bounce back off the walls.

That way, Zubat always knew where everything was. It zipped around rocks and swooped under ledges without ever bumping into anything. When a Geodude got lost in the dark, Zubat squeaked the way out. "Follow my voice!" it called. And the Geodude rolled safely out into the sunshine.

When Zubat grew up, it became Golbat, with big wings and an even bigger mouth. Golbat could open its mouth so wide that it looked like it was always yawning.

Golbat used its big mouth for the loudest, happiest "Good night!" in the whole cave. Every evening, when the sun went down, it flew out into the starry sky with its friends, swooping and twirling. And every morning, before the sun came up, it flew back home to sleep upside down. Shh. Golbat is sleeping now.

During the day, Oddish buried itself in the cool soil, with only its leafy head poking out. Wiggle, wiggle. It soaked up water from the earth and took a long, quiet rest.

But at night, when the moon came up, Oddish popped out of the ground and went for a walk. Tiptoe, tiptoe. It wandered through the fields, scattering tiny seeds as it went. In the morning, nobody knew who had done it. They only knew that, somehow, new little flowers had grown.

Gloom had a big flower on its head and a little problem. The flower made a very, very strong smell. Some Pokémon held their noses. "Phew!" they said.

But one Pokémon didn't mind at all. A tiny Butterfree loved the smell, because it meant sweet nectar was nearby. Every morning it visited Gloom and had breakfast from its flower. Gloom was so happy to have a friend that it didn't care about the noses anymore. Smelly can be nice, if you have the right friend.

Vileplume had the biggest flower petals in the whole forest. They were so big that Vileplume had to walk very carefully so it wouldn't tip over. Wobble, wobble, wobble.

When the rain came, the little Pokémon ran under Vileplume's petals to stay dry. Pitter, patter, went the rain. Vileplume stood still and proud, holding up its giant flower like an umbrella. When the sun came out, it gave a happy shake, and a shower of golden pollen floated through the air.

Paras was a little orange bug with two tiny mushrooms growing on its back. The mushrooms grew a bit bigger every day, and Paras carried them everywhere, like a little garden.

Paras liked to dig under the roots of big trees, where it was cool and damp. It found yummy things there to eat, and the mushrooms liked the shade. "Where are you going, Paras?" asked a Bulbasaur. "Somewhere shady," said Paras, "to keep my garden happy." And off it went, scuttle, scuttle.

Parasect had a great big red mushroom on its back, bigger than the rest of its body. It liked dark, damp places best, deep in the forest where the sunlight couldn't reach.

When Parasect walked, little puffs of mushroom dust floated out behind it. Poof, poof. Wherever the dust landed, tiny new mushrooms grew. Over the years, Parasect turned a dark corner of the forest into a magical mushroom garden, where little Pokémon came to play hide-and-seek among the caps.

Venonat was a fuzzy purple bug with big round red eyes. Those eyes could see in the dark, so Venonat liked to come out at night.

There was one thing Venonat couldn't resist: lights. When it saw a glowing porch lamp, it scuttled right over and stared, as if it were the most wonderful thing in the world. "Ooooh." The family inside waved hello, and Venonat waved back with its little feet. Every night after that, they left the light on, just for Venonat.

When Venonat grew up, it became Venomoth, with big purple wings covered in shimmering dust. At night, it fluttered out under the stars.

Venomoth loved the lights of the town. It danced around the lamps, and every flap of its wings sprinkled a tiny cloud of dust that glittered in the lamplight. The children in town looked out their windows and whispered, "Look, it's the night dancer!" Then they went to sleep, dreaming of glittering wings.

Diglett lived underground, and nobody ever saw more than its little brown head. Pop! Up it came from the dirt. Pop! Back down it went.

Diglett loved to dig, and wherever it went, it left the soil soft and fluffy. One spring, an old farmer noticed that Diglett had been digging in her garden all night. She planted her seeds in the fluffy soil, and that summer she grew the biggest carrots she had ever seen. After that, she left a little snack out for Diglett every evening.

Dugtrio was three Diglett who did everything together. Three little heads popped up from the ground, side by side, and three little heads popped back down. Pop, pop, pop!

Because there were three of them, Dugtrio could dig three times as fast. When the Rattata wanted a tunnel to their favorite berry bush, Dugtrio dug it before lunch. When the Sandshrew wanted a slide, Dugtrio dug that too. "How do you work so well together?" asked a friend. "Easy," said all three heads at once. "We take turns."

Meowth had a shiny gold coin on its forehead, and it loved shiny things more than anything. Glittery buttons, sparkly marbles, a lost silver spoon: Meowth collected them all in a little box.

One evening, Meowth found a shiny key on the path. It was the best shiny thing yet! But then Meowth saw a little boy searching and searching, looking very worried. Meowth looked at the key. It looked at the boy. Then it padded over and dropped the key in his hand. The boy's smile was the shiniest thing Meowth had ever seen.

Persian was a sleek, elegant Pokémon with a red jewel on its forehead. It walked with its nose in the air and its long tail swaying, as if it were the queen of the whole town.

Persian didn't like to be bothered. But one rainy day, a tiny Meowth followed it home, shivering and soggy. Persian sighed. Then it curled its long body around the little one and licked its fur dry. "Just this once," Persian said. But it said that every day after, too.

Psyduck always had a headache. It held its head in its hands and tilted it this way and that. "Psy-y-y?" It never quite remembered what it was doing.

But when its headache got really strong, something surprising happened. One day, a ball rolled into the deep part of the pond, and Psyduck's friend started to cry. Psyduck held its head, blinked hard and, whoosh! The ball floated up out of the water and landed right in its friend's arms. Psyduck blinked again. It didn't remember doing it. But it was very happy anyway.

Golduck was the best swimmer in the whole lake. It had long webbed hands and feet, and it zoomed through the water like a blue arrow. Swish, swish, swoosh!

In the middle of its forehead was a red gem. When Golduck was thinking very hard, the gem glowed. The little Psyduck at the lake looked up at Golduck with big eyes. "Will we swim that fast someday?" they asked. "Practice every day," said Golduck, and its gem twinkled. So the Psyduck practiced, and they got a little faster every week.

Mankey was a small, fluffy Pokémon who lived in the treetops. It was full of energy, swinging from branch to branch, and it got cross very easily. If a berry was too sour, Mankey stomped. If the wind messed up its fur, Mankey huffed.

One day a wise old Pokémon taught Mankey a trick. "When you feel cross, count to ten." So the next time a branch snapped, Mankey took a deep breath. "One, two, three..." By the time it reached ten, it was laughing at itself. Mankey still gets cross sometimes. But now it counts.

Primeape was a fiery Pokémon with a big temper and even bigger energy. It liked to run, jump and shout, and it never, ever gave up.

When the river flooded and washed away the little bridge, everyone else said, "Oh no!" But Primeape said, "Let's fix it!" It ran back and forth all day, carrying logs and stones, huffing and puffing and not stopping once. By sunset the new bridge was finished. Primeape was still a little grumpy. But it was grumpy and proud.

Growlithe was a loyal, friendly Pokémon with a fluffy orange coat. It had a wonderful nose and could follow a smell for miles. Sniff, sniff, sniff!

Growlithe lived with a family in a little house by the woods. Every morning, it walked the children to the end of the path, and every afternoon it was waiting there when they came home, wagging its tail. When the littlest one dropped her mitten in the snow, Growlithe sniffed it out in no time. "Good Growlithe!" she said, and gave it the biggest hug.

Arcanine was big and beautiful, with a shaggy mane and stripes like flames. It could run so fast and so far that it crossed a whole country in a single day.

People told old stories about Arcanine, the swift and kind. In the stories, it always came running when someone needed help. One snowy night, when a little village ran out of firewood, a warm wind swept down from the hills, and there was Arcanine, glowing like a campfire. It lay down in the village square, and everyone gathered close until morning.

Poliwag had a swirl on its round belly and a tail for swimming. In the water, it was quick and graceful. But Poliwag had only just grown legs, and on land it was still learning to walk. Wobble, wobble, flop!

Every day, Poliwag practiced. It took one step and fell. It took two steps and fell. Its friends cheered from the pond. "You can do it, Poliwag!" And one day, it took ten whole steps in a row, all the way to the berry bush. Poliwag was so proud that it did a little dance. Then it fell over again. That's okay.

Poliwhirl had a big swirl in the middle of its tummy. When it moved, the swirl seemed to spin round and round and round.

The little Pokémon at the pond loved to watch it at bedtime. "Spin the swirl, Poliwhirl!" they said. So Poliwhirl wiggled, and the swirl went round and round, and their eyes went round and round, and their heads went nod, nod, nod. Before long, they were all fast asleep. Try it: imagine the swirl going round and round...

Poliwrath was a strong swimmer with big muscles. It could swim across a whole lake without taking a break, and even across the sea.

One day, a message in a bottle needed to reach an island far, far away. "I'll take it," said Poliwrath. It tucked the bottle under its arm and swam. Stroke, stroke, stroke. Waves splashed and the wind blew, but Poliwrath kept going. At sunset it reached the island and handed over the bottle. Then it floated on its back and watched the stars before swimming home.

Abra slept eighteen hours a day. Morning, noon and night, it was usually snoozing, curled up with its eyes closed. Zzz.

But even when it was asleep, Abra could tell when something was about to happen. Once, a big pinecone fell from a tree right toward Abra's nap spot. Pop! Abra vanished and reappeared on a soft patch of moss nearby, still fast asleep. The pinecone bounced harmlessly. Abra didn't even wake up. It just smiled in its dreams and kept on snoozing.

Kadabra always carried a silver spoon. It used the spoon to help its mind do amazing things, like lifting stones without touching them or making a leaf float in the air.

One evening, Kadabra was helping its friends make soup. The pot was too heavy to stir. So Kadabra held up its spoon and concentrated. Hmmm. The big wooden spoon in the pot began to stir all by itself. Round and round, round and round. The soup was delicious, and everyone agreed that Kadabra was the best cook in the forest.

Alakazam was the smartest Pokémon anyone knew. It held a spoon in each hand, and its brain remembered everything that had ever happened to it, from the day it was born.

Alakazam lived in an old library, and children came from far away to visit. "Tell us a story!" they said. So Alakazam closed its eyes and told them a story it had heard a long time ago, every word just right. Then another, and another. The children never ran out of questions, and Alakazam never ran out of stories.

Machop was small, but it was very, very strong. It practiced lifting things every single day. Rocks, logs, buckets of water. Hup, hup, hup!

One morning, a big boulder rolled onto the path to the village, and nobody could move it. Then Machop marched up, rubbed its hands together, took a deep breath and pushed. Hnnnnngh! The boulder rolled away with a THUD. The villagers clapped and cheered. Machop flexed its little arms and grinned. All that practice had paid off.

Machoke was so strong that it wore a special belt to help keep its power under control. It loved to help people with heavy work.

When the town built a new playground, Machoke carried the slide, the swings and the big wooden climbing frame, all by itself. Heave-ho! It set everything in place, gently, gently, so nothing broke. When the children ran in to play, Machoke sat on a bench and watched them, smiling. Being strong was nice, but helping was even nicer.

Machamp had four strong arms, and it was always busy. With four arms, it could do four things at once!

It could carry a basket, open a door, wave hello and scratch its nose, all at the same time. When moving day came for the family down the road, Machamp carried the bed, the table, the chairs and the Meowth's basket in one trip. But the best thing about four arms? Machamp gave the biggest, warmest, four-arm hugs in the whole world.

Bellsprout was thin as a stick, with a yellow bell-shaped head and two little leaves. When the wind blew, Bellsprout swayed this way and that. Sway, sway, sway.

Bellsprout loved to dance. It wiggled its roots and bobbed its head to the rhythm of the rain. Plip, plop, sway. The other Pokémon thought it looked so funny that they joined in, and soon the whole garden was dancing. When the rain stopped, Bellsprout took a little bow, and everyone clapped.

Weepinbell looked just like a big yellow bell. It liked to hang from a tree branch by the hook on its back, swinging gently in the breeze. Ding, dong, ding.

Well, it didn't really ring. But the little Pokémon pretended it did. Whenever they saw Weepinbell swinging, they shouted, "Ding! Dong! Time to play!" And Weepinbell swung higher, giggling, while everyone gathered underneath. It liked being the forest's bell. It brought everybody together.

Victreebel was a big, bell-shaped Pokémon with a sweet, sweet smell, like honey and flowers mixed together. When the breeze carried its smell across the garden, every nose went sniff, sniff.

One evening, Victreebel planned a surprise party for its friends. It didn't send any invitations. It just stood in the middle of the clearing and let its sweet smell drift away on the wind. One by one, the Pokémon followed their noses, and soon everyone had arrived. "How did we all know to come?" they asked. Victreebel just smiled its big wide smile.

Tentacool floated in the warm sea, and its body was so clear that the sunlight shone right through it. From above, it looked like a piece of glass bobbing on the waves.

When the sun hit Tentacool just right, the red gems on its head sparkled. The fish Pokémon swam up to look. "You're like a little window," said a Goldeen. Tentacool liked that. It floated on the waves all afternoon, sparkling in the sun, while its friends swam circles around it.

Tentacruel had lots and lots of long tentacles. When it wanted to, it could stretch them all out, and they floated around it in the water like ribbons.

One day, a little Shellder lost its way among the rocks. Tentacruel stretched out its tentacles in every direction, feeling gently between the stones, until one of them found the Shellder. It scooped it up and carried it back home. "How did you find me?" asked the Shellder. "I looked everywhere at once," said Tentacruel.

Geodude looked a lot like a round gray rock, except that it had two strong arms. It lived beside a mountain path, where it liked to sit very still and watch the world go by.

Because it looked so much like a rock, hikers sometimes sat down on it for a rest. "What a nice comfy rock," they would say. Geodude didn't mind. It sat very still and listened to their stories. But once, a hiker sneezed so loudly that Geodude jumped, and the hiker jumped, and they both laughed until their sides hurt.

Graveler loved to roll. At the top of the mountain, it tucked in its arms and legs and, rumble, rumble, rumble, rolled all the way down the slope.

Graveler wasn't fussy about food, either. It munched on pebbles and rocks, crunch, crunch, and thought they were delicious. Its favorite game was racing the other Graveler down the mountain. They rolled and bounced and tumbled together, and at the bottom, they always lay in a happy, dusty pile, catching their breath.

Golem had a hard shell like a big, round boulder. Its body was so tough that it hardly noticed bumps at all. Bonk! "Was that a bump?" Golem would ask.

Once a year, Golem did something special. It wriggled and stretched until its old shell came loose, and out it came with a shiny new one, smooth and clean. The old shell stayed behind on the mountain, and the little Geodude loved to climb inside it and use it as a clubhouse. Golem was very proud of that.

When Ponyta was born, its legs were wobbly and weak. It couldn't run at all. But it watched the grown-ups race across the fields with their fiery manes streaming, and it wanted to run too.

So every day, Ponyta practiced. It tripped and it tumbled, but it got back up. Its legs grew stronger and stronger. And one morning, it raced across the meadow with its own little mane flickering behind it. Here's a secret: Ponyta's fiery mane doesn't feel hot to friends it trusts. So its friends could ride on its back, warm and safe.

Rapidash was one of the fastest Pokémon in the land. When it ran, its hooves barely touched the ground, and its blazing mane streamed behind it like a comet.

Every morning, Rapidash raced the sunrise. It galloped across the fields as the sky turned from purple to pink to gold. Clip-clop, clip-clop, faster, faster! And every morning it reached the top of the hill just as the sun peeked over the edge. Rapidash tossed its fiery mane as if to say, "Good morning, sun. I won again."

Slowpoke was very, very slow. It took a long time to walk, a long time to think and a long, long time to notice anything at all.

Slowpoke liked to sit by the river and dangle its tail in the water, as if it were fishing. It sat there all day, waiting. Hours went by. The sun moved across the sky. A Krabby walked by, then walked back. "Are you catching anything?" asked the Krabby. Slowpoke thought about it for a very long time. "Not yet," it said happily. It had all the time in the world.

Slowbro was once a Slowpoke who went fishing and got a surprise: a Shellder clamped onto its tail and wouldn't let go. Slowpoke didn't mind. It stood up on two legs and kept on walking, with Shellder along for the ride.

Now Slowbro and Shellder go everywhere together. Slowbro is still slow and still dreamy, and Shellder holds on tight. When Slowbro forgets where it's going, Shellder reminds it with a little nip. "Oh yes," says Slowbro. "The river." They make a very good team.

Magnemite was a small, round metal Pokémon with one big eye and a magnet on each side. It didn't have wings, but it floated in the air anyway, humming quietly. Mmmmm.

Magnemite loved electricity. Whenever it found a power line, it floated along beside it, humming happily. Once, it floated into a kitchen by mistake and stuck to the fridge. Clank! The family laughed and laughed. They pulled it off gently and let it rest by a warm lamp, and after that, Magnemite visited every afternoon.

Magneton was three Magnemite stuck together in a little triangle. They floated everywhere as a team, humming a three-part song. Mmm, mmm, mmm.

Being stuck together wasn't always easy. One Magnemite wanted to go left, one wanted to go right and one wanted to take a nap. They wobbled around in a circle until they all started laughing. Then they made a rule: take turns choosing. Today it's left. Tomorrow it's right. And on Sundays, everyone naps.

Farfetch’d was a small brown duck Pokémon who always carried a green leek. It used the leek for everything: to point the way, to stir its soup, to scratch an itch and to wave hello.

Farfetch’d would never, ever let go of its leek. But one windy day, a gust blew so hard that the leek flew out of its wing and landed in a tree. Farfetch’d hopped and flapped and hopped until a kind Bulbasaur reached up with its vines and brought it down. Farfetch’d hugged its leek tight, then waved it at Bulbasaur to say thank you.

Doduo was a bird Pokémon with two heads and two long, quick legs. It couldn't fly very well, but it could run very fast. Zoom!

The two heads usually agreed on everything. But one day, they came to a fork in the road. "Left!" said one head. "Right!" said the other. They stood there for a long time, arguing. Then they both had the same idea at the same time: "Let's go straight!" And off they ran, straight through the meadow, both heads laughing.

Dodrio had three heads, and each head had its own feelings. One head was usually happy, one was usually a little sad and one was usually grumpy.

When something good happened, the happy head cheered. When something sad happened, the sad head sighed. And the grumpy head grumbled about almost everything. But one day, a friend brought Dodrio three slices of berry pie. All three heads tasted at once, and for the very first time, all three heads smiled. "Mmmm!"

Seel lived in the cold, icy sea, and it loved the cold more than anything. The colder the water, the happier Seel was. Splish, splash!

On top of its head was a little horn, and Seel used it to break through the ice. Crack! Up came Seel, popping out of a hole in the frozen sea to say hello. Its favorite game was sliding across the ice on its smooth, round tummy. Wheee! It slid and slid until it splashed right back into the water.

Dewgong was a beautiful white Pokémon who lived in the icy sea. It loved to nap on floating icebergs, curled up in the cold sunshine.

Long ago, sailors saw Dewgong sleeping on the ice from far away, and they told stories about a mysterious sea maiden. They didn't know it was just a sleepy Dewgong! Dewgong didn't mind the stories. It liked to swim beside the ships as they passed, and it waved its flippers at the sailors, who always waved back.

Grimer was a gooey, gloopy, purple Pokémon. It squished and squelched wherever it went. Squish, squelch, squish!

Most Pokémon wrinkled their noses at Grimer, because it liked yucky things. Muddy puddles. Old sludge. Sticky goo. But one day, the town's drain got all clogged with gunk, and nobody knew what to do. Then Grimer squelched in and slurped it all up. Gloop! The drain was clean, and the whole town cheered. Sometimes the best helpers are the gooiest ones.

Muk was a big, big blob of goo. It was soft and squishy and very, very sticky. When it moved, it went glorp, glorp, glorp, and left a shiny trail behind it.

Muk loved to help keep the town tidy. Every night, it oozed through the streets and gobbled up the litter that people had left behind. Crumpled papers, broken toys, old banana peels. Glorp! By morning, the streets were sparkling clean. The people never saw Muk at work. But they always wondered who the nighttime cleaner was.

Shellder lived inside a hard, shiny shell, and it was very shy. When anything came close, it snapped the shell shut. Clack!

But Shellder was curious, too. When things were quiet, it opened its shell just a little and stuck out its long tongue to see what was going on. Peek. If it was a friend, Shellder opened all the way and said hello. If it wasn't sure, clack, shut again. Its friends learned to say hello very softly, and then Shellder always came out to play.

Cloyster had a big spiky shell that was harder than almost anything. It could swim deep, deep down to the bottom of the sea, where hardly anyone else could go.

Down there, in the dark, quiet water, Cloyster found treasures: shiny pebbles, pretty shells and once, a beautiful round pearl. It carried the pearl all the way back up and left it on the sand for the little girl who always sang to the waves. When she found it, she sang her very best song, and Cloyster listened from the water.

Gastly was a Pokémon made of purple, misty gas, with big eyes and a big grin. It could float through walls and slip under doors like a little cloud.

Gastly loved to play peekaboo. It hid inside the walls of an old house, then popped out and said, "Boo!" At first the Pokémon who lived there jumped. But then they started to laugh, because Gastly was giggling so hard that it puffed up twice its size. After that, they played peekaboo every night, and Gastly always let them win.

Haunter had two floating hands that weren't attached to anything. They waved, they pointed and they tickled. Tickle, tickle!

Haunter loved to sneak up on its friends and tickle them from behind. They spun around, but nobody was there! Then Haunter appeared out of the wall, laughing and waving its floating hands. Haunter was a bit of a trickster, but a friendly one. When the little Gastly were scared of the dark, Haunter held their hands and floated them home.

Gengar liked to hide in shadows. It could slip into a dark corner or under a bed and wait there, grinning its big wide grin. When it was nearby, the air felt a tiny bit chilly.

But Gengar was a playful shadow, not a scary one. Its favorite game was copying people. When a girl walked down the street at sunset, her long shadow wiggled its ears. She stopped. The shadow stopped. She waved. The shadow waved, and then it winked. She laughed and laughed, and Gengar giggled too, right there in her shadow.

Onix was a giant snake made of rocks, as long as a train. It lived deep underground and dug tunnels through the earth, faster than anyone could imagine. Rumble, rumble!

Inside Onix's head was a special sense that always told it which way to go, like a compass. So Onix never got lost. When the Diglett got turned around in the dark, Onix let them ride on its back and took them home. "How do you always know the way?" they asked. "I just do," said Onix, and rumbled on.

Drowzee had a long nose and droopy eyes, and it had a very special job. At night, it tiptoed from house to house and sniffed the air. Sniff, sniff. Drowzee could smell dreams.

If it found a bad dream, Drowzee gobbled it right up. Gulp! The sleeper turned over and smiled, and a happy dream drifted in instead. Drowzee liked the taste of funny dreams best, but it always ate the bad ones first. So if you sleep well tonight, maybe a Drowzee came by to help.

Hypno carried a shiny pendulum on a string. When it swung the pendulum, back and forth, back and forth, anyone watching began to feel very, very sleepy.

One night, a little Rattata couldn't fall asleep. It tossed and it turned. So Hypno sat beside it and swung the pendulum. Back and forth. Back and forth. "Watch the pendulum," Hypno whispered. Back and forth... The little Rattata's eyes grew heavy. Back and forth... and soon it was snoring. Zzz. Are your eyes getting heavy, too?

Krabby lived on a sandy beach, in a hole near the water. It walked sideways, click, click, click, and waved its two big pincers in the air.

When Krabby was happy, it blew bubbles from its mouth. Blub, blub, blub! The bubbles floated up and popped in the sunshine. The children on the beach loved to watch. They walked sideways next to Krabby, click, click, click, and blew bubbles too. Krabby thought they were the funniest crabs it had ever seen.

Kingler had one claw that was much, much bigger than the other. The big claw was very strong, but it was also very heavy, so Kingler sometimes tipped over. Whoops!

To talk to its friends across the beach, Kingler waved its big claw up high. Wave, wave! That was how the Krabby talked to each other: one wave for hello, two waves for "come and play" and three waves for "dinner time!" Kingler's favorite was always the third one.

Voltorb was round and red and white, and it looked a lot like a ball. It had two little eyes and no arms or legs, so it got around by rolling. Roll, roll, roll!

One day, some children at the park found Voltorb in the grass. "A ball!" they cried. Voltorb blinked. Then it bounced, all by itself. Boing! The children gasped and then laughed. They rolled it gently back and forth, and Voltorb fizzed with tiny happy sparks. It had never been part of a game before, and it loved it.

Electrode looked like a big ball, just like Voltorb, only bigger and rounder. It was one of the fastest Pokémon of all, and it zoomed around by rolling. Zoom, zoom!

Electrode stored up lots of electricity inside its round body. When it had too much, it glowed and buzzed and got a little jumpy. So Electrode found a fun way to use it up: it rolled to the town square every evening and lit up all the lamps, one by one, with tiny sparks. Fizz, fizz, glow. The town called it the lamplighter.

Exeggcute looked like six little eggs, but they were really six seeds, and they were the best of friends. They always stayed close together, rolling and bouncing as a group.

The six seeds could talk to each other without making a sound. When one wanted to go to the stream, all six went to the stream. When one felt sleepy, all six curled up together in a pile. Once, one little seed rolled a bit too far. The other five called to it with their thoughts, "Over here!" and it rolled right back home.

Exeggutor was a tall, walking palm tree with three round heads, and each head had its own ideas. It loved hot, sunny places, where it could soak up the sunshine all day.

One summer, the three heads couldn't decide where to go on holiday. "The beach!" said the first. "The beach!" said the second. "Also the beach!" said the third. They all looked at each other and laughed. Exeggutor stomped off to the seaside, and all three heads had the sunniest day of their lives.

Cubone was a small, shy Pokémon who wore a hard helmet on its head and carried a little bone club. It liked quiet places and didn't talk very much.

One evening, Cubone sat alone on a hill, watching the moon. A Clefairy came and sat beside it. "Do you like the moon too?" it asked. Cubone nodded. They sat together, not saying anything, just watching. The next night, the Clefairy came back. And the night after that. Cubone wasn't alone anymore, and its little heart felt warm.

Marowak used to be a shy Cubone. Now it was strong and brave, and it was very, very good with its bone. It could throw it like a boomerang, and the bone always came spinning back. Whirr, whirr!

The little Pokémon loved to play catch with Marowak. It tossed the bone high into the sky, whirr, and it curved all the way around the field, whirr, and back into Marowak's hand. "Again! Again!" they cried. And Marowak, who had once been so quiet and shy, laughed and threw it again.

Hitmonlee had long, bendy legs that could stretch and stretch, much farther than you'd think. Boing! It loved to jump and kick and practice its moves.

Every year, the town had a big kickball game, and everybody wanted Hitmonlee on their team. When the ball got stuck at the top of a tall tree, nobody could reach it. Then Hitmonlee stretched its leg up, up, up, and gave the ball a gentle tap. Bonk! Down it came. Everyone cheered, even the other team.

Hitmonchan practiced its punches every day. Its fists moved so fast that you could hardly see them. Pow, pow, pow! Like a little whirlwind.

But Hitmonchan's favorite job wasn't fighting. Every spring, the people in town hung their dusty rugs over the fence, and Hitmonchan came to help. Pow, pow, pow! It punched every rug until the dust flew out in big clouds. "Achoo!" sneezed the townspeople, laughing. When it was done, every rug in town was clean and fluffy.

Lickitung had the longest tongue you have ever seen. It was twice as long as its whole body! Lickitung used it to taste everything. Slurp!

It licked the berries to see if they were ripe. It licked the raindrops to see if they were cold. It even licked its friends to say hello, which made them squeal and giggle. When the juiciest apple in the orchard was too high for anyone to reach, Lickitung stuck out its tongue, longer, longer and, slurp! The apple was down, and everybody shared it.

Koffing was a round, purple Pokémon that floated through the air like a balloon. It was full of gas, and sometimes, um, a little bit of gas came out. Pfffft. "Oops," said Koffing.

The other Pokémon held their noses and giggled. Koffing went pink with embarrassment. But then a little Rattata said, "Koffing, you float so beautifully. Can you teach us to float?" Koffing puffed up proudly and showed them how it bobbed in the air. Nobody could float like Koffing. And everyone forgot all about the smell.

Weezing was two Koffing who had grown together into one Pokémon, with two heads, one big and one small. They floated along together, puffing little clouds behind them.

The big head liked to hum low songs. Hmmmm. The little head liked to hum high songs. Heeee! For a long time, they tried to hum over each other. Then one day, they tried humming together. Hmmmm-heeee. It sounded wonderful! Now Weezing floats through the valley humming two-part songs, and the clouds it puffs drift away like little notes.

Rhyhorn was big and strong, with a stony hide and a horn on its nose. When it started running, it ran straight ahead, as fast as it could. Thunder, thunder, thunder!

The trouble was, Rhyhorn wasn't very good at remembering things. Halfway through a run, it often forgot why it had started running in the first place. It would slow down, stop and look around. "Hmm. Where was I going?" Then it would spot a nice patch of grass and decide that must have been it. Munch, munch.

Rhydon stood up on its back legs, and on its nose was a horn that spun like a drill. Whirrrr! It could drill right through solid rock.

One day, a rockslide blocked the only path between the village and the mountain meadow. The little Pokémon on the other side couldn't get home. So Rhydon lowered its horn and started drilling. Whirrr, crunch, whirrr! By evening, it had made a tunnel straight through the rocks. The little ones ran through, cheering, and Rhydon stood guard at the entrance until the last one was home.

Chansey was one of the kindest Pokémon in the world. It carried a round egg in a pouch on its tummy, and it loved to help anyone who was hurt or sad.

When a little Pidgey hurt its wing, Chansey was there right away. It wrapped the wing gently and sang a soft song. When a Psyduck had a cold, Chansey brought it soup. And when somebody was just having a bad day, Chansey gave them a big, warm hug. "There, there," it said. Everyone felt better when Chansey was around.

Tangela was covered all over in blue vines, so many that nobody had ever seen its face. Only its two little eyes peeked out from the tangle, and two red feet stuck out at the bottom.

Tangela was the champion of hide-and-seek. It just sat in a bush, and nobody could tell where the bush stopped and Tangela started. Once, it sat so still that a Pidgey built a nest right on top of it. Tangela didn't move all week. When the eggs hatched, the baby Pidgey thought Tangela was the cuddliest bush in the world.

Kangaskhan was a big, strong mother Pokémon, and she carried her baby in a pouch on her tummy. The baby peeked out at the world with wide eyes and wiggly ears.

One sunny day, the baby wanted to try walking by itself. Kangaskhan set it down very gently in the grass. The baby took one step. Then two. Then it toddled all the way to a flower and sniffed it. "I did it!" Kangaskhan's heart was so full of love that she scooped her baby up and twirled it round and round, and they both laughed and laughed.

Horsea was a tiny sea Pokémon with a curly tail. It liked to wrap its tail around a piece of coral so the waves couldn't wash it away. Hold on tight!

When something startled Horsea, it squirted out a cloud of black ink, squish, and zipped away while the water was dark. Then it peeked out from behind the coral. "Oh! It's just you," it would say, when it saw its friend Staryu. And the two of them would play in the waves until the ink cloud floated away.

Seadra was a spiky sea Pokémon with sharp fins, and it was a very good dad. In Seadra families, it's the fathers who look after the eggs and the babies.

Seadra guarded its little ones in a cozy nest of seaweed. When the babies hatched, it taught them how to curl their tails around coral and how to swim in little bursts. Zip, zip! At night, it tucked them into the seaweed and swam slow circles around the nest until every little Horsea was sound asleep.

Goldeen was a beautiful fish Pokémon with long, flowing fins that waved like a ballerina's skirt. People called it the queen of the water.

Goldeen loved to dance in the river. It twirled and swirled, and its fins rippled through the water like silk. Swish, swoosh, swirl. The other fish stopped to watch. "How do you swim so beautifully?" they asked. "I just listen to the music of the water," said Goldeen, and twirled again.

Every autumn, Seaking got very busy. It used the horn on its head to dig a cozy nest in the bottom of the river, scooping away the pebbles one by one. Scoop, scoop, scoop.

When the nest was finished, Seaking laid its eggs there and guarded them all winter long. It swam back and forth, back and forth, keeping watch through the cold months. And when spring came, the river was full of tiny new Goldeen, all flapping their fins and wiggling their tails. Seaking was the proudest Pokémon in the river.

Staryu was shaped like a star, with a red jewel in the middle. Every night, when the stars came out in the sky, the jewel in Staryu's middle began to glow and twinkle too.

On summer nights, all the Staryu gathered on the beach. Their jewels twinkled together, and the sand sparkled as if the night sky had fallen down to the shore. The children in the seaside town came out to look. "Look, stars in the sand!" they whispered, and made wishes on every single one.

Starmie looked like two stars stacked together, with a shining jewel in the center. The jewel glowed in seven different colors, like a rainbow.

Starmie spun slowly through the deep, dark sea, lighting up the water wherever it went. Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet. The little fish followed it, amazed by the colors. Some people said Starmie's jewel was sending messages to the stars. Nobody knew for sure. But on clear nights, if you look at the sea, you might see a tiny rainbow twinkling back at the sky.

Mr. Mime was a mime, which means it could act out anything without saying a single word. And it had a special trick: when it moved its fingers in the air, it made invisible walls appear.

Mr. Mime loved to put on shows. It pretended to be stuck in a box, pushing on the invisible walls. It pretended to climb an invisible ladder. Once, it made an invisible wall so real that a Doduo bumped right into it. Bonk! The Doduo's two heads looked at each other. Then everyone burst out laughing, even Mr. Mime, silently, of course.

Scyther was a green bug Pokémon that moved so fast it was just a blur. Swish! On its arms were two big curved blades, and it was very, very careful with them.

Scyther was the best gardener in the whole meadow. It trimmed the tall grass into neat paths, swish, swish, and cut the hedges into shapes: a Pidgey, a Pikachu, a big round Snorlax. Every morning, the little Pokémon came to see what new shape Scyther had made overnight. Scyther never told anyone how it worked so fast. It just smiled and said, "Practice."

Jynx loved to dance. It swayed and wiggled to a rhythm only it could hear, and as it danced, it sang in a language nobody understood.

The other Pokémon didn't know what the words meant. But the songs were so cheerful that their feet started tapping on their own. Tap, tap, tap. Soon the whole snowy valley was dancing with Jynx, slipping and sliding on the ice. When the song ended, nobody knew what it had been about. But everybody felt happy, and that was enough.

Electabuzz was a yellow Pokémon with black stripes and a whole lot of energy. It loved electricity so much that it liked to hang around power plants, just to feel the buzz. Bzzzz!

One winter night, a storm knocked the power out in town. Everything went dark and quiet. Then there was a crackle and a glow. Electabuzz was standing in the middle of the square, spinning its arms round and round, making sparks. Fizz, crackle, buzz! It lit up the streetlights, one by one, until the whole town was glowing again.

Magmar was born in a volcano, and its body was always warm, warm, warm. Its skin glowed orange and yellow, like a flickering flame.

When winter came to the little village at the foot of the mountain, the snow piled up high and everyone shivered. So Magmar walked down from the volcano and wandered through the streets, glowing. Wherever it went, the snow melted into little puddles and the air turned cozy. The villagers opened their doors and invited Magmar in for tea. It was the warmest winter they had ever had.

Pinsir had two huge pincers on top of its head, and it was very, very strong. It could pick up things much bigger and heavier than itself.

When a big tree fell across the stream, the Pokémon of the forest couldn't get across. Pinsir walked up, grabbed the trunk with its pincers and lifted. Creeeak! It swung the log around and set it down neatly, so it made a perfect bridge. "Thank you, Pinsir!" said everyone, trotting across. Pinsir clicked its pincers happily. Click, click. That meant "You're welcome."

Tauros was a strong, wild Pokémon with three swishing tails. Before it ran, it whipped its tails back and forth. Swish, swish, swish! Then off it charged, kicking up dust.

Tauros lived with a big herd on the grassy plains. They loved to run together, their hooves drumming like thunder. Ba-dum, ba-dum, ba-dum. When the sun went down, the whole herd lay down in the warm grass, tails swishing gently, and watched the stars come out one by one.

Magikarp was a little orange fish Pokémon, and it wasn't very good at anything. It couldn't swim very fast. It couldn't jump very high. Mostly, it just flopped around. Splash! Splash!

The other Pokémon laughed at Magikarp, but Magikarp didn't give up. Every day it splashed and splashed, as hard as it could. "What are you doing?" they asked. "Getting ready," said Magikarp. Nobody knew what it meant. But Magikarp knew something they didn't: one day, all that splashing was going to turn into something amazing.

Once there was a little Magikarp who splashed every day, even when everyone laughed. And one day, with a great big SPLASH, it grew into Gyarados, a giant blue sea dragon, longer than a boat and as strong as a storm.

The Pokémon who had laughed at Magikarp hid behind rocks. But Gyarados just smiled. It remembered what it felt like to be small. So it became the guardian of the lake, keeping the water calm and the little fish safe. And every so often, just for old times' sake, it gave a little splash.

Lapras was a big, gentle sea Pokémon with a smooth shell on its back. It loved to carry people across the sea, from one island to another, swimming slow and steady through the waves.

On the way, Lapras sang. Its songs were soft and beautiful, and they drifted across the water like a lullaby. The children riding on its back leaned against its long neck, listening to the waves and the singing, and by the time they reached the other island, they were often fast asleep. Lapras never minded. It just swam a little slower.

Ditto was a pink, blobby Pokémon with a little dot-eyed smile. And it had an amazing talent: it could turn itself into anything it saw. Bloop!

It turned into a Pikachu. Bloop! It turned into a Bulbasaur. Bloop! It even turned into a teapot. But no matter what Ditto turned into, it kept its own little dot eyes and its funny smile. That's how its friends could always find it. "There's Ditto!" they laughed, pointing at the teapot that was smiling at them.

Eevee was a small, fluffy brown Pokémon with big ears and a bushy tail. And Eevee had a secret: it could grow up into many different kinds of Pokémon.

"Will I be a water Pokémon?" Eevee wondered, looking at the lake. "Or a fire Pokémon, warm and cozy? Or a lightning Pokémon, fast as a spark?" Eevee didn't know yet. And that was okay. "I'll find out when I find out," it decided, and went off to play. After all, there was plenty of time to grow.

When Eevee touched a sparkling Water Stone, it became Vaporeon, a sleek blue Pokémon with fins and a tail like a mermaid's. Vaporeon loved the water more than anything.

Vaporeon had a special trick. When it dove into a lake, its body seemed to melt right into the water, so you couldn't see it at all. The little Pokémon on the shore would look and look. "Where did Vaporeon go?" Then, splash! Up it popped right in front of them, spraying them with a shower of cool, sparkly water.

When Eevee touched a crackling Thunder Stone, it became Jolteon, a spiky yellow Pokémon full of electricity. When it was excited, its fur stood up in sharp little points. Zzzt!

Jolteon was very quick and a little bit jumpy. If you surprised it, its fur crackled and puffed up like a pincushion. But when it was calm and happy, its fur lay flat and soft. Jolteon's friends learned to say hello gently, and then Jolteon would curl up beside them, with only the tiniest sparkle of static. Fzzt.

When Eevee touched a glowing Fire Stone, it became Flareon, a fluffy orange Pokémon with a big puffy tail and a fiery heart. Its fur was so warm and soft that everyone wanted to cuddle it.

On the coldest winter nights, all of Flareon's friends gathered around it like a campfire. Flareon fluffed up its mane and glowed warm and toasty inside. "Ahh," said everyone, holding out their paws. Flareon was happy to share its warmth. It was the best heater in the whole forest, and it gave the coziest hugs.

Porygon wasn't born like other Pokémon. It was made by people, out of computer code, and its body was all smooth shapes and bright colors, like a toy.

Porygon could do something no other Pokémon could: it could travel inside computers. Zip! Into the screen it went, zooming through tunnels of light and numbers. Sometimes it peeked out of a phone to say hello. And when a little boy's video call kept freezing, Porygon zipped inside the computer and fixed it, beep boop, so he could see his grandma's smile again.

Omanyte was an ancient Pokémon from long, long ago, when the world was very different. For thousands of years it slept as a fossil, hidden inside a stone.

Then one day, scientists found the fossil and woke Omanyte up. It blinked its big eyes and looked around. Everything was new! It wiggled its little tentacles and twirled through the water, twisting its spiral shell. "Hello, world," said Omanyte. The world had changed a lot while it was asleep, and Omanyte couldn't wait to explore it.

Omastar had a great big spiral shell on its back, much bigger than when it was a little Omanyte. The shell was so big and heavy that Omastar moved slowly, very slowly, through the water.

But Omastar didn't mind being slow. It had been asleep for thousands of years, and it was the wisest Pokémon in the sea. The young fish came to ask it questions about the old days. "What was it like, a long, long time ago?" they asked. And Omastar told them stories about ancient seas, slowly, one bubble at a time.

Kabuto was an ancient Pokémon with a round, hard shell. Long ago, it lived on the bottom of the sea, and it hid under its shell whenever it felt shy.

Kabuto had a funny trick: it had eyes on its back, so it could peek out without moving at all. Peek! The little Krabby on the beach loved to play guessing games with Kabuto. "Can you see me now?" they asked, hiding behind a rock. And Kabuto just giggled under its shell, because of course it could.

Kabutops was a sleek, fast swimmer from ancient times, with long curved arms and a smooth, shiny shell. In the water, it zipped like an arrow. Zip!

Kabutops liked to swim in the shallow tide pools, where the little Pokémon played. It showed them how to tuck in their arms and glide, smooth and quick. Glide, glide, swoosh! When the tide went out, Kabutops climbed onto the rocks and dried off in the sun, its shell gleaming. It had seen the oceans of long ago, but it liked this one just fine.

Aerodactyl was an ancient flying Pokémon that had slept inside a piece of golden amber for a very, very long time. When scientists woke it up, it flapped its great gray wings and let out a loud cry. SKREEE!

At first, everything was strange to Aerodactyl. There were houses and roads and bicycles! But a family of Pidgey flew up to it and said, "Fly with us!" So it did. They showed Aerodactyl the best tree for resting and the warmest winds for gliding. Soon, Aerodactyl felt right at home in its brand-new world.

Snorlax was big. Really, really big. And it did two things: it ate, and it slept. Munch, munch, munch. Zzz, zzz, zzz.

One afternoon, Snorlax fell asleep right in the middle of the road. Nobody could get past! The townspeople tried calling it. They tried tickling it. Snorlax just snored. So they gave up and had a picnic instead, right there on Snorlax's big round tummy. When it finally woke up, it was covered in crumbs and very happy children. Snorlax yawned, smiled and went back to sleep.

Articuno was a legendary bird of ice, with long blue tail feathers that sparkled like frost. It lived high in the snowy mountains, where few people had ever seen it.

But there was an old story the mountain folk told. When travelers got lost in a snowstorm, a beautiful blue bird would appear in the sky above them. It would sing a clear, sweet note and fly slowly ahead, leaving a trail of glittering snowflakes. And if the travelers followed the sparkles, they would always find their way home.

Zapdos was a legendary bird of lightning, with bright yellow feathers and spiky wings that crackled. It lived inside the thunderclouds, high above the world.

When a storm rolled in, the children in town ran to their windows to look. Crash! went the thunder. Flash! went the lightning. And sometimes, just for a moment, they saw a great golden bird swooping through the clouds. "Zapdos!" they whispered. The storm didn't seem scary anymore. It just seemed like Zapdos was out flying, having fun.

Moltres was a legendary bird of fire, with wings that blazed orange and gold. Wherever it flew, the air grew warm and bright.

People said that when Moltres flew over the land, it meant spring was on its way. So at the end of every long, cold winter, the children watched the sky. One morning, there it was: a streak of fire across the blue. The snow began to melt, the first flowers poked up, and everyone ran outside, shouting, "Spring is here! Moltres came!"

Dratini was a small blue dragon Pokémon that lived in a hidden lake behind a waterfall. It was very rare, and very few people had ever seen one.

Dratini grew and grew, and as it grew, it shed its old skin, wriggling out of it like taking off a sweater. Wiggle, wiggle, pop! Then it was a little longer and a little shinier than before. It left the old skin by the lake, and the other Pokémon found it in the morning. "Dratini is growing up," they said, smiling.

Dragonair was a graceful blue dragon with crystal orbs on its neck and tail. It glided through the sky and the water like a ribbon in the wind.

People said Dragonair could change the weather. One morning, a village was getting ready for a festival, but dark rain clouds filled the sky. Everyone was sad. Then Dragonair rose up from the lake, its crystals glowing. It swirled through the clouds once, twice, three times, and the clouds parted, and the sun came out. The festival was the best one ever.

Dragonite was a big, friendly orange dragon with small wings that could carry it all the way around the world. It was gentle and kind, and it loved to help.

One foggy night, a little boat got lost at sea. The sailors couldn't see anything at all. Then, out of the fog, came a warm orange glow. It was Dragonite, flying low over the water. It flew in front of the boat, slowly, so the sailors could follow, all the way back to the harbor. By the time they turned to say thank you, Dragonite was already gone, off to help someone else.

Mewtwo was one of the most powerful Pokémon in the world. It could lift mountains with its mind. But Mewtwo wasn't born like other Pokémon. It was made, long ago, in a laboratory, and for a long time it didn't know where it belonged.

Mewtwo went to live on a quiet island, far away from everyone. At first it was lonely and a little bit angry. But slowly, the island's Pokémon got used to it. A Pidgey nested on its shoulder. A Caterpie napped by its foot. Mewtwo stayed very still so it wouldn't wake them. And somewhere along the way, it found it wasn't lonely anymore. The strongest Pokémon in the world had learned to be gentle.

Mew was a tiny pink Pokémon with big blue eyes and a long, thin tail. It was so rare that most people thought it was only a legend. But Mew was real, and it loved to play.

Mew could turn invisible whenever it wanted, so it was the best at hide-and-seek. It giggled in the trees, floated over rivers and blew bubbles at sleepy Pokémon. Some scientists said that Mew held a little piece of every Pokémon inside it. Maybe that's why it liked everyone so much. If you ever hear a tiny giggle in an empty forest, it might be Mew, saying hello.

Chikorita had a big green leaf on top of its head, and it loved to sunbathe. Every morning it found the warmest spot in the garden, closed its eyes and let the sun shine on its leaf.

The leaf smelled sweet, like fresh tea. When Chikorita waved it, the sweet smell drifted through the air, and everyone nearby felt calm and cheerful. When two Sentret got into a squabble over a berry, Chikorita trotted over and waved its leaf. Swish, swish. The Sentret sniffed, smiled and decided to share.

Bayleef had a ring of leaves around its neck, and tucked inside each leaf was a little bud. The buds gave off a spicy, tingly smell, like ginger and mint.

Whenever a friend felt tired, Bayleef came close and let them breathe in the smell. Sniff! Suddenly they felt full of energy, ready to run and jump and play. On the morning of the big meadow race, every single runner lined up next to Bayleef first. "Just one sniff, please!" they begged. Bayleef giggled and gave everyone a turn.

Meganium had a beautiful flower blooming around its neck. The flower smelled so lovely and gentle that anyone who smelled it forgot about being cross or sad.

And Meganium had another gift. When it breathed softly on a drooping plant, the plant perked right up again. One dry summer, the village flower garden wilted. The children were heartbroken. So Meganium walked slowly along every row, breathing on each flower. Hhhhh. By evening, the whole garden was blooming again, brighter than ever.

Cyndaquil was a small, shy Pokémon who liked to curl up in a ball. On its back were little holes where flames came out. Most of the time, the flames stayed tucked away.

But when Cyndaquil was surprised, or very excited, whoosh! The flames on its back burst out tall and bright. One night, the children at camp couldn't light their campfire. Cyndaquil was so excited to help that its flames went whoosh, and the campfire caught right away. Everyone cheered, and Cyndaquil curled up happily by the fire.

Quilava had a collar of flames around its neck and another at its tail. It was quick on its feet and could dodge and dart so fast that it left a little trail of warm air behind.

Quilava's favorite thing was playing tag. Nobody could catch it! Zip, zip, zip! But on cold days, Quilava slowed down on purpose, just enough to let its friends tag it. Then they all gathered around its warm flames, rubbing their paws together. Quilava knew that winning wasn't as fun as keeping everyone warm.

Typhlosion was big and strong, with a blazing collar of fire around its neck. When it got hot, the air around it shimmered and wobbled, like the air above a road on a summer day.

Typhlosion lived near a mountain village where winters were long and cold. Every evening, when the snow fell, it sat on top of the hill and let its flames burn high. The village children could see the glow from their windows. "Typhlosion is keeping watch," they told each other. And they snuggled into bed, warm and safe.

Totodile was a small blue Pokémon with a big mouth full of little teeth, and it was full of energy. It loved to snap its jaws at everything: leaves, bubbles, even its own reflection. Chomp, chomp, chomp!

Totodile didn't mean any harm. Chomping was just how it played. One day, it chomped a dandelion, and all the fluffy seeds blew up into the air. Totodile was so surprised that it did a happy dance. Then it went looking for another dandelion, and another, until the whole field was full of floating fluff.

Croconaw had a mouth full of sharp teeth. Sometimes one of its teeth fell out, but Croconaw never worried. A brand-new tooth always grew right back in its place.

The little Pokémon at the river collected Croconaw's lost teeth like treasures. They found them on the riverbank, shiny and white, and kept them in a box. "Did you lose another one, Croconaw?" they asked. Croconaw grinned its big toothy grin and showed them the new one growing in. Then it splashed back into the water for a swim.

Feraligatr was a big blue Pokémon with powerful jaws and a strong tail. In the water, it was fast and graceful. On land, it walked tall and proud.

Feraligatr looked very fierce, but it had a gentle side. Every spring, the little Totodile in the river were learning to swim. Feraligatr let them climb onto its back, and it swam slowly in circles while they practiced kicking their legs. Splash, splash, kick! When they got tired, they rode on its back all the way to shore.

Sentret had a long, striped tail, and it could stand up on it, tall and straight, to look around. It was always the lookout for its family. Up it went, peering over the tall grass.

If Sentret saw something coming, it squeaked loudly to warn the others. Squeak! Squeak! But one day, it saw something wonderful instead: a field full of ripe berries. "Squeak! Squeak!" it called, hopping up and down on its tail. Its whole family came running, and they had the biggest berry feast ever.

Furret was long and slim, with soft, stripy fur. It was so long that sometimes you couldn't tell which end was its head and which end was its tail.

Furret made its home in a narrow burrow, just its size. It curled around and around inside, like a cozy spiral. When its friends came to visit, Furret popped out of one hole, and then its tail popped out of another hole, far away. "Hello!" said the head. Wiggle, wiggle, said the tail. Everybody laughed every single time.

Hoothoot was a round, brown owl Pokémon that always stood on one foot. It had a perfect sense of time. Every evening, at exactly the same moment, it called out: "Hoo! Hoo!"

The other Pokémon used Hoothoot like a clock. When it hooted once, it was time to stop playing. When it hooted twice, it was time to wash up. And when it hooted three times, it was time for bed. Hoo, hoo, hoo. Listen carefully. Can you hear Hoothoot? It's saying it's time for bed.

Noctowl was a wise owl Pokémon with eyes that could see in the dark. It could turn its head almost all the way around, and it flew so softly that its wings didn't make a sound.

Noctowl watched over the forest every night. When a little Pokémon couldn't find its way home in the dark, Noctowl flew down silently and landed on a branch nearby. "This way," it hooted softly, and it lit the path with its glowing eyes. By morning, everyone was safe in bed, and Noctowl was dozing on its favorite branch.

Ledyba was a little red ladybug Pokémon with black spots. It was a bit shy, so it liked to stay in big groups with its friends, all bunched up together on a leaf.

When the weather was chilly, the Ledyba huddled even closer, sharing warmth. When the sun came out, they flew off together like a little red cloud, buzzing happily. And they talked to each other with tiny smells that only Ledyba could understand. Sniff: "Let's go!" Sniff: "This way!" Sniff: "Lunchtime!"

Ledian was a ladybug Pokémon that loved the night. The spots on its back glowed softly in the starlight, and the more stars there were in the sky, the brighter Ledian glowed.

On clear nights, Ledian flew over the fields, scattering a soft sparkle wherever it went. The children in the village watched from their windows and pointed. "Look, a flying star!" They made wishes on it, just in case. And Ledian twinkled back, as if to say that every one of those wishes was a good one.

Spinarak was a small green spider Pokémon, and it could spin silk thread from its mouth. It worked all night to weave a web between two branches, round and round, back and forth.

In the morning, the web was covered in tiny drops of dew, and it sparkled in the sunlight like a necklace of diamonds. The Pokémon of the forest stopped to admire it. "Did you make that, Spinarak?" they asked. Spinarak nodded shyly. It was very proud. It took a whole night of work to make something so pretty.

Ariados could spin silk thread from both ends of its body, and it never got its threads tangled. It was the best weaver in the whole forest.

Ariados had a clever idea. It tied one end of a silk thread to each of its little friends when they went out exploring. That way, if anyone got lost, they could follow the thread all the way back home. Tug, tug, follow, follow. Nobody in Ariados's forest ever got lost again, and Ariados always knew where everyone was.
