When Golbat became the very best of friends with someone, it changed into Crobat, a purple Pokémon with four wings instead of two. With four wings, it could fly faster than ever, and so quietly that you could barely hear a whoosh.

Crobat was fast and loyal. It zipped through the dark night sky on its four wings, delivering messages between friends. "Good night from the forest!" it whispered to the mountain. "Good night from the mountain!" it whispered back to the forest. By the time the moon was high, everyone had heard good night from everyone.

Chinchou lived in the deep, dark sea, where no sunlight could reach. On top of its head were two little antennae, and at the end of each one was a glowing light.

Chinchou used its lights to talk to its friends. Blink, blink meant "Hello!" Blink, blink, blink meant "Come here!" And one long glow meant "I'm happy." Down in the dark, the Chinchou blinked to each other all day long. If you could dive down deep enough, you would see the whole sea sparkling with their conversations.

Lanturn had a big glowing light at the end of its antenna, so bright that it could be seen from the very top of the sea. Sailors called it the star of the deep.

On dark nights, when fishing boats were far from home, the sailors looked over the side of their boats and saw a soft glow shining up from the deep water. "There's Lanturn," they said. "We're on the right path." Lanturn swam ahead of them, slow and steady, lighting the way home through the dark sea.

Pichu was a tiny Pokémon, the baby that grows up into Pikachu. It had round cheeks that could make electricity, but Pichu was still very little and couldn't control it yet.

When Pichu was surprised, or laughed too hard, or sneezed, zap! Its electricity went off by accident and made it jump. Bzzt! "Eek!" Its fur stood straight up, and it blinked in surprise. Then it giggled, because it looked so funny. Pichu was still learning. And one day, when it grew up, it would be the best little spark in the forest.

Cleffa was a tiny pink Pokémon shaped a bit like a star. People said that on nights with lots of shooting stars, you might see a Cleffa sitting in the grass, looking up at the sky.

One night, a little girl saw a shooting star and made a wish. The next morning, she found a tiny pink Cleffa sitting in her garden, smiling up at her. Nobody knew where it had come from. But every night after that, the two of them sat together and watched the stars, and Cleffa always pointed out the brightest one.

Igglybuff was the baby that grows up into Jigglypuff. It was a tiny, soft pink ball, and its body was so bouncy that it bounced everywhere it went. Boing, boing, boing!

Igglybuff loved to sing, just like Jigglypuff. But its voice was still very small, and its songs came out as little squeaks. "Igg-ly, igg-ly!" It didn't make anyone sleepy yet. It made them smile. And every night, Igglybuff practiced its lullaby, a little bit louder, a little bit sweeter, until one day it would sing the whole world to sleep.

Togepi was a tiny Pokémon that still wore half of its eggshell, like a little pair of pants. It had a round head with three little spikes and the happiest face you've ever seen.

People said that Togepi was filled with happiness. When it was around kind people, it soaked up their kindness and shared it back with everyone nearby. So wherever Togepi went, people felt lucky and cheerful. "Toge-toge-prriii!" it sang, waving its little arms. And everyone who heard it couldn't help smiling.

When Togepi felt very, very loved, it grew into Togetic, a little white Pokémon with tiny wings. Togetic flew around looking for kind people, and when it found them, it shared its happiness with them.

Togetic sprinkled a soft, glittering light over anyone who was being kind. When a boy helped his little sister tie her shoes, a sprinkle of sparkles floated down. When a girl shared her umbrella, another sprinkle. Nobody knew where the sparkles came from. But everyone knew that good things happened afterward.

Natu was a tiny green bird Pokémon with big round eyes. Its wings weren't big enough to fly yet, so it hopped everywhere instead. Hop, hop, hop!

Natu liked to stand very still and stare at things for a long time. It stared at clouds. It stared at flowers. It stared at its friends until they giggled. "What are you looking at, Natu?" they asked. Natu didn't answer. It just kept staring, very seriously. Then it hopped up onto a branch, hop, and stared at the sunset instead.

Xatu was a tall green bird Pokémon that liked to stand perfectly still and gaze at the sun. It stood there from sunrise to sunset, not moving a feather.

People said that Xatu could see things nobody else could, like what had happened long ago and what might happen tomorrow. When the villagers wanted to know if it would rain on the day of their festival, they asked Xatu. Xatu looked at the sun for a long time. Then it nodded. "Sunny," it seemed to say. And it was.

Mareep was a fluffy sheep Pokémon with soft, puffy wool. Its wool was special: when Mareep rubbed against things, the wool filled up with static electricity, and it puffed up bigger and bigger. Fluff, fluff, FLUFF!

On cold days, Mareep's friends liked to cuddle into its warm wool. But sometimes they got a tiny zap. Bzzt! "Ooh, ticklish!" Their fur stood straight up, and they all looked so silly that they laughed and laughed. Then Mareep shook itself, fluff, and they cuddled again.

When Mareep grew into Flaaffy, it lost some of its wool, and its pink skin showed through. But Flaaffy didn't mind, because now it had a long tail with a glowing ball on the end.

When Flaaffy had lots of electricity stored up, its tail ball glowed bright as a flashlight. Flaaffy loved to use it to light up dark places. It went into the barn at night to check on the other Mareep, swinging its glowing tail like a lantern. "Night, night, everyone," it whispered, and the sleepy Mareep fluffed up their wool and snored.

Ampharos had a long neck and a tail with a big red ball on the tip. The ball could shine so brightly that its light could be seen from far, far away across the sea.

Long ago, in a little seaside town, the lighthouse lamp broke. Ships couldn't find the harbor at night. So Ampharos climbed to the top of the lighthouse and made its tail glow brighter than ever. Every night, it shone out over the water, guiding the ships safely home. The town loved Ampharos, and they called it their lighthouse friend.

When Gloom touched a shiny Sun Stone, it became Bellossom, a small green Pokémon with a skirt of leaves and two bright red flowers on its head. And Bellossom loved to dance.

When the rain stopped and the sun came out, all the Bellossom gathered in the meadow to dance. They swished their leafy skirts and twirled, and their petals rubbed together with a soft, happy sound. Swish, swirl, shimmer. Everyone who saw them dancing felt like the sun had come out twice.

Marill was a round blue Pokémon with big ears and a tail that ended in a bouncy blue ball. The tail ball was full of air, so it floated in the water like a little balloon.

When Marill went swimming, its tail bobbed on top of the water, and Marill could never sink. Bob, bob, bob. Its friends always knew where Marill was, because they could see the blue ball floating. "There's Marill!" they called. And Marill splashed happily, wiggling its tail so the ball danced on the waves.

Azumarill had long rabbit ears and a round, cheerful body. It could hear even the tiniest sounds, like a fish swimming at the bottom of a fast river.

Azumarill loved making bubbles. It blew big, shiny bubbles that floated on the water and carried little Pokémon who couldn't swim yet. A Pichu climbed into one. A Togepi climbed into another. They floated along the river in their bubbles, giggling, while Azumarill swam beside them, listening to make sure everyone was safe.

Sudowoodo looked exactly like a little tree, with green bumps for leaves. It liked to stand very still by the side of the road, pretending to be a tree. Nobody ever guessed!

But Sudowoodo had a secret: it was really made of rock, and it didn't like water at all. One day, a gardener came by with a watering can. "Oh, this little tree looks thirsty," she said, and tipped the can. Sudowoodo jumped up, waved its arms and ran away as fast as it could. The gardener dropped her can and laughed for a week.

Politoed was a green frog Pokémon with a curly bit of hair on its head, like a little crown. It was the leader of the Poliwag in the pond, and when it sang, they all came hopping.

Every evening, Politoed climbed onto the biggest lily pad and puffed out its throat. "Ribbit, ribbit, RIBBIT!" Its croaky song echoed across the pond. One by one, the Poliwag swam over and gathered around. They sang together until the stars came out, a big croaky choir, and the whole pond rippled with their music.

Hoppip was so light that the wind could pick it up and carry it away. It was a pink Pokémon with leafy ears, and it was just about as heavy as a dandelion seed.

When the wind blew hard, Hoppip held onto the ground with its little feet so it wouldn't float off. Hold on, hold on! But on gentle days, it let go and drifted wherever the breeze took it. Up over the trees, over the river, over the hill. "Wheee!" Hoppip landed in a new place every day and made a new friend every time.

Skiploom had a flower on its head that opened and closed with the weather. When it was warm, the flower opened wide. When it was chilly, the flower closed up tight.

On sunny days, Skiploom floated high in the sky, its flower wide open, soaking up the sunshine. Its friends on the ground could tell what the weather was going to be just by looking up. "Skiploom's flower is open!" they cheered. "Picnic day!" And off they went, with Skiploom floating above them like a little pink parasol.

Jumpluff had three fluffy cotton puffs, and it floated on the wind wherever it wanted to go. It could drift all the way around the world, riding the breezes over oceans and mountains.

Wherever Jumpluff floated, it dropped tiny cotton seeds. Puff, puff, puff. They landed in fields and gardens and cracks in the sidewalk, and soon little plants sprouted up. Jumpluff never stayed in one place for long. But if you see a fluffy little plant growing somewhere unexpected, maybe a Jumpluff passed by.

Aipom was a purple monkey Pokémon with a long tail, and at the end of its tail was a hand. Aipom used its tail-hand so much that it was better at picking things up with its tail than with its real hands!

Aipom lived high in the trees and loved to play tricks. It used its tail to pick berries, swing from branches and tickle its friends from behind. Tickle, tickle! When the children came to the park, Aipom hung upside down and waved its tail-hand at them. "Hi, Aipom!" they waved back, and it gave them a high five with its tail.

Sunkern was a small, round seed Pokémon with two little leaves on top. It was not very strong, and it didn't move very much. But Sunkern had a big dream: it wanted to bloom.

Every morning, Sunkern drank the dew from the leaves and turned its face toward the sun. "Today, maybe today," it said. The other Pokémon smiled at its patience. And one bright morning, a Sun Stone glinted in the grass. Sunkern touched it, and, pop! It bloomed into a beautiful Sunflora. "I knew it," said Sunkern. "Today."

Sunflora was a sunflower Pokémon with bright yellow petals and a happy face. It loved the sun more than anything, and wherever the sun moved across the sky, Sunflora turned to face it.

In the morning, it faced east. At noon, it looked straight up. In the evening, it turned west to say goodbye. And when the sun went down, Sunflora closed its petals and went to sleep. The gardeners in the village always knew what time it was. They just looked at which way Sunflora was facing.

Yanma was a dragonfly Pokémon with big red eyes and four clear wings. Its eyes were so big that it could see all the way around itself without turning its head.

Yanma could also hover in one spot, perfectly still, flapping its wings very fast. Bzzzzz. One afternoon, the children were playing hide-and-seek, and nobody could find the last hider. Yanma hovered above the park, looked all around with its giant eyes and pointed: "There, behind the slide!" The children laughed. Nobody could hide from Yanma.

Wooper was a little blue Pokémon with a big happy smile. It lived in cool ponds and streams and covered its body in a slippery, slimy coat to keep from drying out.

When the evening got chilly, Wooper climbed out of the water to look for food. Pat, pat, pat, went its little feet. Its slippery skin made it hard to hold, so when the children tried to hug it, Wooper slipped right out of their arms. Bloop! It landed on the grass and smiled up at them. Hugs are hard when you're that slippery.

Quagsire was a big, easygoing Pokémon with a sleepy smile. It never hurried, and it never worried about anything. Life was good, as far as Quagsire was concerned.

Quagsire liked to swim along the bottom of the river with its mouth open, waiting for snacks to float in. Sometimes it swam right into a boat. Bonk! "Oh," said Quagsire. It didn't mind. It just smiled, turned around and swam the other way. The fishermen loved Quagsire. They said it was the calmest Pokémon in the world.

When Eevee became the very best of friends with someone during the daytime, it grew into Espeon, a sleek purple Pokémon with a red gem on its forehead and a tail that split in two at the end.

Espeon's fine fur could feel even the tiniest change in the air. It always knew when the weather was about to change, and it always knew what its friends were feeling. When a little boy was sad, Espeon felt it from across the house and came to sit with him. It didn't need to say anything. It just knew.

When Eevee became the very best of friends with someone at night, it grew into Umbreon, a black Pokémon with yellow rings on its body that glowed in the moonlight.

Umbreon loved the night. When the moon came out, its rings began to shine softly, like little lanterns. On dark walks home, Umbreon walked in front, glowing, so its friends could see the path. "Thank you, Umbreon," they said. Umbreon swished its tail. The night wasn't dark at all when Umbreon was around.

Murkrow was a black bird Pokémon with a big feathered hat on its head. It loved shiny things, just like a magpie. Shiny pebbles, shiny buttons, shiny bottle caps. It gathered them all and hid them in its nest.

Murkrow's nest was the sparkliest nest in the whole forest. When the sun hit it, it twinkled like a treasure chest. One day, a little girl lost her shiny hair clip. She looked up and saw it glinting in Murkrow's nest. Murkrow looked at her sad face. Then it flew down and gave it back. Well, mostly. It kept one shiny button.

Slowking used to be a Slowpoke. Then one day, a Shellder bit it on the head and stuck there like a crown. And suddenly, Slowpoke became very, very smart.

Slowking wore its Shellder crown proudly. It read books, solved puzzles and answered every question its friends asked. It was still a little bit slow, but it was the wisest Pokémon by the river. When the young Slowpoke came to visit, Slowking told them, "Being slow is fine. Just make sure you think while you're being slow."

Misdreavus was a little ghost Pokémon that loved to play tricks. It floated through the house at night and made funny noises, like a squeaky door or a whispery giggle. Hee-hee-hee!

The children in the house jumped the first time they heard it. But then they found Misdreavus floating in the corner, grinning. They weren't scared anymore. They laughed! After that, Misdreavus made silly noises every night, and the children made silly noises back, until their mother called up, "Bedtime!" Then everyone went quiet. Well, almost everyone.

Unown were tiny Pokémon shaped just like the letters of the alphabet. There was an A, a B, a C, and all the way to Z, plus one shaped like a question mark and one shaped like an exclamation mark.

The Unown lived in an old stone ruin, and they liked to line up on the walls to make words. One day, a little boy visited the ruins, and the Unown lined up just for him: H-E-L-L-O! The boy gasped. Then the Unown wiggled around and made a new word: F-R-I-E-N-D. The boy waved, and all the letters wiggled back.

Wobbuffet was a big blue Pokémon with a round, wobbly body and a black tail with two eyes on it. It always stood with one arm up, as if it were saluting. "Wob-buf-FET!"

Wobbuffet was very, very patient. It never started any trouble. It just stood there, smiling and wobbling. When the strong wind blew, it wobbled back. When a ball bounced off it, it wobbled back. Wobble, wobble, boing! Wobbuffet didn't mind anything. And no matter what happened, it always popped back up with its arm in the air. "Wob-buf-FET!"

Girafarig was a tall, spotty Pokémon with a long neck. And at the end of its tail was a second little head, with its own little brain!

The tail head never slept. So when Girafarig was tired, its front head closed its eyes and snoozed, while the tail head stayed awake, keeping watch. Snore, snore, said the front. Blink, blink, said the back. When morning came, the front head woke up and asked, "Anything happen?" And the tail head wagged as if to say, "Nothing at all. Good morning!"

Pineco looked just like a pinecone, and it liked to hang from tree branches, swaying in the breeze. Sway, sway.

Pineco made its shell thicker and cozier by adding layers of tree bark, one piece at a time. Every week, it was a tiny bit bigger. "Look at my new layer," Pineco said proudly to its friends. They knocked on its shell. Knock, knock. "Very sturdy," they agreed. Pineco smiled and swung happily on its branch.

Forretress had a hard steel shell, round as a ball. It stayed in one spot on a tree trunk all day and almost never moved. And nobody had ever seen what it looked like inside its shell.

The forest Pokémon were very curious. "What's inside?" they wondered. "A big jewel? A tiny Pokémon? A secret door?" They guessed and guessed. Forretress never told. It just opened its shell the tiniest crack, peeked out and then, clink, closed it again. Some secrets are more fun to keep.

Dunsparce was a funny-looking Pokémon with a stubby body, tiny wings and a drill-shaped tail. When it was in a hurry, it dug into the ground tail-first, whirrr, and disappeared.

Dunsparce built a maze of tunnels under the meadow, with twisty passages and secret rooms. It loved to invite friends down to play. "Follow me!" it called, and wriggled off. Its friends always got lost in the twisty tunnels. But Dunsparce always came back to find them, flapping its tiny wings and laughing.

Gligar was a purple Pokémon with big flappy wings like a kite. It liked to climb up high on cliffs and then jump off, gliding silently through the air. Whoosh!

The little Pokémon at the bottom of the cliff watched it glide. "Can we try?" they asked. So Gligar carried them up, one at a time, and held them gently as it glided down. Whoosh! Their ears flapped in the wind. It was the best ride in the whole valley, and Gligar never got tired of giving it.

Long ago, an Onix dug deeper and deeper underground. It dug so deep that the heavy earth pressed on its body, and its rocks turned to shiny steel. It had become Steelix!

Steelix's steel body was harder than diamonds. It lived very deep underground, where it was dark and quiet, and it dug long tunnels under the mountains. When miners got lost in the tunnels, they knocked on the walls. Knock, knock. And Steelix came rumbling through, shining in their lantern light, to guide them out.

Snubbull had a big underbite and a fierce-looking face, so everyone thought it was tough. But really, Snubbull was shy and sweet, and it loved to be cuddled.

When Snubbull went to the park, the other Pokémon backed away. "That one looks grumpy," they whispered. Snubbull felt sad. Then a little girl walked straight up and scratched it behind the ears. Snubbull's tail wagged so hard that its whole body wiggled. The other Pokémon blinked. "Oh," they said. "It's not grumpy at all!"

Granbull had a big jaw with two large teeth sticking up, and it looked very serious. But actually, Granbull was a bit of a scaredy-cat, and it got startled easily.

A leaf fell on its head. "Eek!" A Hoothoot hooted. "Eek!" Its own shadow followed it. "EEK!" Its friends thought this was very funny. So they made Granbull a soft blanket and showed it that leaves and hoots and shadows were all perfectly fine. Now Granbull carries its blanket everywhere and hardly ever says eek. Well, sometimes.

Qwilfish was a round fish Pokémon covered in little spikes. When it gulped in lots of water, it puffed up like a spiky balloon. Puff!

Qwilfish liked to puff up to show off. "Look how big I am!" it said, floating proudly. But being puffed up made it float to the top, and it bobbed there helplessly, spinning around. Bob, bob, spin. Its friends laughed so hard. Qwilfish let out its water, pfffft, and zoomed around in circles. Then it puffed up again, just to make them laugh some more.

When Scyther got a shiny Metal Coat, it changed into Scizor, a bright red Pokémon with a hard steel body. On its arms were two big pincers with patterns that looked just like eyes.

Scizor's pincers looked so much like eyes that other Pokémon thought it had three heads! Scizor thought that was hilarious. It liked to wave its pincers and make them talk to each other like puppets. "Hello, left claw." "Hello, right claw." The little Pokémon laughed and laughed. Scizor was the best puppet show in the forest.

Shuckle was a little Pokémon that lived inside a red shell with holes in it. It liked to collect berries and store them inside its shell. Then it waited.

Day by day, the berries inside Shuckle's shell turned into sweet, delicious berry juice. When it was ready, Shuckle shared it with all its friends. Slurp, slurp, yum! "How do you make it so tasty?" asked a Pichu. Shuckle smiled. "The secret ingredient," it said, "is waiting." It was the best juice in the whole land.

Heracross was a big blue beetle Pokémon with a strong horn on its head. It was so strong that it could lift things much, much heavier than itself!

Heracross loved sweet things, especially the sticky sap from trees. Slurp! One day, a big log rolled onto the path, and a whole family of Pokémon couldn't get home. Heracross slid its horn under the log and, heave-ho, flipped it right out of the way. As a thank you, the family gave Heracross a pot of honey. It was the happiest beetle in the world.

Sneasel was a quick, sneaky Pokémon with sharp claws and a feather on its head. It lived in the snowy mountains and loved to play tricks.

Its favorite trick was the snowball sneak. When the other Pokémon built a pile of snowballs, Sneasel tiptoed up behind them, very quietly, and took one. Then another. Then another. When the other Pokémon turned around, all their snowballs were gone! "Sneasel!" they shouted. And from behind a tree, a snowball came flying back. Poof! The snowball game was on.

Teddiursa was a little bear cub Pokémon with a crescent moon on its forehead. It loved honey more than anything in the whole world.

Teddiursa's paws were always sticky, because it dipped them in honey and licked them clean. Lick, lick, mmm! When it found a good honey tree, it hid some honey away for later. But it often forgot where it put it. So Teddiursa spent most of its days sniffing around the forest, looking for its own hidden honey. Every time it found some, it was like a surprise present.

Ursaring was a big, strong bear Pokémon with a ring shape on its chest. It had an amazing nose and could smell food from very, very far away.

Every autumn, Ursaring walked through the forest, sniffing out the best berries and honey before winter. Sniff, sniff. It followed its nose to all the secret spots. The little Teddiursa followed behind it in a line, copying every sniff. Sniff, sniff, sniff, sniff. By the end of autumn, everyone had full tummies, ready for a long winter's nap.

Slugma was a little slug Pokémon made of warm, glowing magma. It had to keep moving, because if it stopped for too long, its body started to cool down and get stiff.

So Slugma was always on the go. Slither, slither, slither. It crawled through the rocky hills, leaving a warm, glowing trail behind it. On cold nights, the little Pokémon on the mountain followed Slugma's warm trail like a path of tiny campfires. And Slugma, slithering ahead, was happy to have company.

Magcargo was a hot, glowing Pokémon with a shell made of cooled lava rock. Its body was so hot that it bubbled and steamed, and snowflakes melted before they even touched it.

On the coldest winter days, the children in the mountain village set their mittens on a rock near Magcargo to warm them up. Toasty! Then they made snow angels and ran back to grab their warm mittens. Magcargo didn't mind being the village's mitten warmer. It liked hearing the children laugh.

Swinub was a little brown Pokémon with a fuzzy coat and a big pink nose. It used its nose to dig through the snow, looking for tasty mushrooms hidden underneath. Snuffle, snuffle!

One snowy morning, Swinub smelled something wonderful. It dug and dug, nose down, until it found the biggest mushroom it had ever seen. Swinub was so excited that it snuffled over to every friend in the forest to share it. Everyone got a nibble, and they all agreed: Swinub had the best nose in the whole wide snow.

Piloswine had long, shaggy fur that covered its eyes, so it couldn't see very well. But that was all right, because Piloswine had an amazing nose.

Piloswine walked through the snowy mountains, sniffing its way. It never got lost, and it always knew where the warm springs and the tasty roots were. When a family of Pokémon got lost in a blizzard, they couldn't see anything either. So they held onto Piloswine's long fur, and it sniffed its way, step by step, all the way to a cozy cave.

Corsola was a pink Pokémon made of coral, with little branches growing on its head. It lived in warm, clear seas, where the water was bright and blue.

If one of Corsola's branches broke off, Corsola didn't worry. A new one always grew back. The fish Pokémon liked to swim between its branches and play hide-and-seek. And sometimes, when the sea was very calm, the children on the beach could see Corsola's pink branches shining in the water, like a tiny underwater garden.

Remoraid was a little fish Pokémon that could shoot water out of its mouth, like a water gun. Pew! And it almost never missed.

Remoraid liked to practice its aim. It knocked down leaves floating over the river. It popped bubbles in the air. Pew, pew, pop! One day, a kite got stuck in a tall tree by the water. The children were sad. Remoraid swam over, took aim and, pew! The water knocked the kite loose, and it floated down into the children's hands. "Remoraid, you're the best!"

Octillery was an orange octopus Pokémon with lots of suction-cup arms. When it was surprised, it squirted out a cloud of ink and zoomed away.

Octillery made its home in a hole between rocks at the bottom of the sea. It decorated its home with shells and sparkly pebbles, and it was very proud of it. When its friends came to visit, Octillery used its suction-cup arms to hug all of them at once. Squish, squish, squish! Its arms were sticky, but its hugs were the best.

Delibird was a little red and white bird Pokémon that carried a sack made from its own tail. It loved to give presents.

Delibird flew around all winter, delivering little gifts to anyone who needed them. A warm berry to a cold Pidgey. A shiny pebble to a sad Pichu. A crunchy snack to a hungry Swinub. "For you!" it chirped, and flew off before anyone could say thank you. Nobody knew how Delibird always had just the right present. It was a wonderful mystery.

Mantine was a big, flat Pokémon with wide fins, and it glided through the sea like a kite in the sky. Swoosh! Sometimes it swam so fast that it leaped out of the water and soared through the air.

Little Remoraid liked to hold onto Mantine's fins and go along for the ride. Mantine swam over the waves, leaping and gliding, while the Remoraid held on tight and cheered. "Higher, Mantine! Higher!" And Mantine leaped so high that they could see all the way to the shore.

Skarmory was a bird Pokémon with shiny steel feathers that glinted in the sun. It built its nest in prickly bushes, where nobody could bother it.

Even though its feathers were hard metal, Skarmory could fly fast and light, swooping through the sky like a silver arrow. When the sun shone on it, it flashed so brightly that people below thought it was a shooting star. "Make a wish!" the children shouted every time they saw it. Skarmory always did a little loop, just for them.

Houndour was a small black Pokémon with orange markings and little ridges on its back. It lived in a pack with lots of other Houndour, and they talked to each other with howls.

One long howl meant "Over here!" Two short howls meant "Let's go!" And a soft, low howl meant "Good night, everyone." Every evening, as the sun went down, the Houndour pack sat on a hill and howled together. Ow-ooo! It echoed across the valley, and the little Pokémon in their beds knew it was time to sleep.

Houndoom was the leader of the Houndour pack, with curved horns on its head and a long, swishing tail. When it howled, its voice echoed far across the mountains.

Houndoom looked serious, but it took good care of its pack. When the young Houndour ran too far ahead, it called them back. When they were cold, it curled around them and warmed them with its fiery breath. And when the moon rose high, it sat at the top of the hill and kept watch, so everyone else could sleep.

Kingdra was a blue sea dragon that lived at the very bottom of the sea, where it was dark and quiet. It slept there most of the time, deep, deep down.

When Kingdra woke up, it yawned a great big yawn. Yaaawn! The yawn was so big that it made the water swirl round and round into a spinning whirlpool. The fish Pokémon loved it. They rode the whirlpool like a merry-go-round, wheee, round and round, until Kingdra closed its mouth and went back to sleep.

Phanpy was a little blue elephant Pokémon with big ears and a long trunk. It loved water, and it loved to share it.

On hot days, Phanpy filled its trunk at the river and sprayed water at its friends. Fwoosh! They squealed and laughed and ran around in the sparkly spray. Then Phanpy filled its trunk again and watered the thirsty flowers. Fwoosh! Phanpy's favorite thing was making sure that nobody, and no flower, was too hot.

Donphan was a big, strong elephant Pokémon with tough gray skin and two long tusks. When it wanted to move fast, it curled up into a ball and rolled. Rumble, rumble, ROLL!

Donphan could roll so fast that it looked like a little rolling hill. It rolled down the dusty paths, smoothing them out flat so the little Pokémon could walk along them easily. Every evening, it rolled all the way around the village, and every morning, the paths were smooth and neat. The villagers called Donphan the road roller.

Porygon2 was Porygon, made even better with a special upgrade. It was round and smooth and shiny, and it could learn new things all by itself.

Porygon2 was always curious. It learned how to dance by watching the Bellossom. It learned how to sing by listening to Jigglypuff. Some people said it was made to explore outer space someday. "What's up there?" it wondered, looking at the stars. Every night, Porygon2 learned the name of one more star. It already knew a hundred.

Stantler was a deer Pokémon with big curly antlers. Its antlers were so special that the air around them seemed to shimmer and wiggle, like a dream.

When people looked at Stantler's antlers for too long, they started seeing funny things. Flowers that weren't there. Rainbows in the sky. Butterflies made of light. Stantler didn't do it to trick anyone. It just liked making people smile. When a sad little girl looked at its antlers, she saw a field of dancing flowers, and she laughed for the first time all day.

Smeargle was an artist Pokémon. At the end of its long tail was a fluffy brush, and the brush was always dripping with paint.

Smeargle painted everything. It painted swirls on rocks. It painted smiley faces on tree trunks. It painted a rainbow on the side of an old gray barn. Every Smeargle has its own favorite color, and this one loved green. When the children saw its paintings, they wanted to paint too. So Smeargle let them borrow its tail, and they painted the town together.

Tyrogue was a little Pokémon who wanted to be strong. It practiced every single day, punching the air and kicking at leaves. Hi-yah! Hi-yah!

Tyrogue got frustrated sometimes. It practiced and practiced, but it was still small. "I'll never be strong," it sighed. Then an old Hitmonchan sat down beside it. "When I was little like you," said Hitmonchan, "I felt the same way. Keep practicing." So Tyrogue did. Every morning. And one day, it found out exactly what kind of strong it was going to be.

Hitmontop could spin on its head like a spinning top. Whirrr! Round and round and round it went, so fast that it looked like a blur.

Hitmontop's favorite thing was dancing. It spun on its head at every party and festival, and the crowd cheered and clapped along. Spin, spin, spin! One day, it spun so fast that it drilled a little hole in the ground. "Oops," it said, dizzy. The children used the hole to plant a tree, and every year, Hitmontop danced under it.

Smoochum was a little pink Pokémon who loved to look at herself. Whenever she saw a puddle, a window or a shiny spoon, she stopped to check her reflection. "Looking good!" she said with a smile.

Smoochum used her lips to find out what things were like. She smooched flowers to see if they were soft. She smooched leaves to see if they were smooth. She even smooched a rock and decided it was too hard. When she smooched her best friend Pichu on the cheek, she decided that was the very best thing of all.

Elekid was a little yellow Pokémon with plugs on its head, and it was full of electricity. It spun its arms round and round to make even more. Whirr, whirr, zap!

Elekid loved thunderstorms. When the sky got dark and the thunder rumbled, it ran outside and danced in the rain, waving its arms at the lightning. "More! More!" Its friends watched from the window, cozy and dry. When the storm was over, Elekid came back inside, buzzing with energy, and told them all about it.

Magby was a little red Pokémon with a fiery body. When it breathed out, little flames puffed from its mouth. Puff, puff!

When Magby was healthy and happy, its breath was a bright yellow flame. Its friends could tell how it was feeling just by looking. Yellow meant "I'm great!" One winter day, Magby caught a cold, and its breath was a little gray. So its friends tucked it into bed and brought it soup. By morning, Magby sneezed, achoo, and a big yellow flame puffed out. Hooray!

Miltank was a pink Pokémon with a gentle face and a big heart. It gave sweet, warm milk that was full of goodness.

People said Miltank's milk could help anyone feel better. When the little Pokémon on the farm had colds, the farmer warmed up a cup of Miltank's milk for them. Sip, sip. They felt better right away. Miltank liked to watch the babies drink their milk, and it mooed softly to them until they fell asleep.

Blissey was a big, round, fluffy pink Pokémon with the softest fur and the kindest heart. It could feel sadness from far away, and whenever it felt someone was sad, it came hurrying over.

Blissey carried a special egg that made whoever tasted it feel happy. Even the grumpiest Pokémon smiled after a nibble. When a little boy was crying because he missed his mom, Blissey sat beside him, fluffed up its fur and gave him a gentle hug. It stayed with him until his mom came home, and by then he was smiling.

Raikou was a legendary Pokémon of thunder. People said it came down from the sky with a bolt of lightning, and it roared so loudly that the air shook.

Raikou ran across the land, faster than the wind, and wherever it went, thunder rumbled. But Raikou wasn't trying to scare anyone. It loved the storm. On rainy nights, if you listen very closely to the thunder, you might hear Raikou running across the sky, roaring with joy.

Entei was a legendary Pokémon of fire. People said it was born when a volcano erupted, and it carried the warmth of that volcano deep inside its body.

Entei roamed across the land, never staying in one place for long. Wherever it went, the air grew warm and flowers bloomed early. Farmers liked it when Entei passed through, because their crops grew big and strong. "Entei came by," they said, pointing at the sunflowers that had grown taller than their houses.

Suicune was a legendary Pokémon of water, with a flowing purple mane that rippled like the north wind. It could run across the top of the water without making a single splash.

Wherever Suicune went, the water became clean and sparkling. When a pond in the village got cloudy and muddy, the fish Pokémon couldn't see anything. Then one morning, Suicune ran across it, light as a breeze. Swish! The water turned crystal clear, and the fish could see the sky again. Suicune was already gone, off to clean another pond.

Larvitar was born deep underground, and the first thing it did was eat. It ate dirt. Lots of dirt. Chomp, chomp, chomp. It ate so much dirt that it ate its way all the way up to the surface!

When Larvitar popped out of the ground, it blinked in the sunlight. "Oh," it said. "It's bright up here." It made friends with a Sunkern and a Wooper, and they showed it around. Then Larvitar felt sleepy from all that eating. It curled up in the warm sun and took a very, very long nap, because that's how Larvitar grow.

Pupitar was a hard gray shell with eyes, and it couldn't walk at all. But Pupitar had a trick: it could push out a burst of air from inside its shell and shoot through the sky like a rocket. WHOOSH!

Pupitar didn't always aim very well. WHOOSH! It zoomed into a tree. WHOOSH! It zoomed into a pond. Splash! Its friends giggled. But Pupitar kept practicing, and soon it could zoom right where it wanted to go. Its friends started calling it the rocket. And Pupitar liked that very much.

Tyranitar was a huge, strong Pokémon with armor like solid rock. It was so big that the hills seemed small next to it. When it walked, the ground went BOOM, BOOM.

But Tyranitar liked peace and quiet. It lived alone on top of a mountain, watching the clouds go by. One day, a little Larvitar climbed all the way up to visit it. "Will I be big like you someday?" it asked. Tyranitar smiled, which made the ground rumble a little. "Yes," it said. "But first, you'll need lots of naps."

Lugia was a legendary Pokémon who lived deep beneath the sea. It had silver-white wings, and it was so powerful that just one flap of its wings could stir up a storm.

So Lugia was very careful. It stayed quietly in its underwater home, keeping the seas calm. People called it the guardian of the sea. Sailors told stories of seeing it once, rising from the waves on a moonlit night, its wings glowing silver. It looked at them gently. Then it slipped back into the water, and the sea was calm all the way home.

Ho-Oh was a legendary bird with shining wings of red, gold and green. When it flew through the sky, its feathers glowed in the sunlight, and a rainbow appeared behind it.

People said that anyone who saw Ho-Oh would be happy forever. So when a rainbow appeared after the rain, the children always ran outside and looked up, hoping to spot it. Maybe it was just a rainbow. Or maybe, just maybe, Ho-Oh had flown by. Either way, they always felt a little happier.

Celebi was a tiny green Pokémon with wings like a fairy and big blue eyes. It lived in the oldest, greenest forests, and it could travel through time.

When Celebi was near, the trees grew taller and the flowers bloomed brighter. People said that if a forest was healthy and happy, it meant Celebi was there, watching over it. Celebi flew from yesterday to today to tomorrow, making sure the forest was always green. And if you take good care of the trees, it might visit your forest too.

Treecko was a little green Pokémon who lived in a big old tree in the jungle. The bottoms of its feet had tiny hooks, so it could walk straight up the tree trunk, and even across the ceiling of its cozy hollow.

Treecko was very calm. When the other Pokémon got scared of a thunderstorm, Treecko stayed cool as a cucumber. "It's just noise," it said, and climbed a little higher to watch the lightning. The others climbed up next to it, holding on tight, and by the end of the storm, they thought it was rather pretty too.

Grovyle had long leaves growing from its arms and head, and it was the fastest climber in the whole jungle. It leaped from branch to branch, never missing a step. Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh!

The jungle trees were so tall that the little Pokémon at the bottom had never seen the treetops. So one day, Grovyle carried them up, one at a time. Leap, leap, leap. At the very top, they gasped. They could see the whole jungle, green and endless, and a river shining like a silver ribbon. "Wow," they whispered. Grovyle smiled. It saw this every day.

Sceptile was a tall, green jungle Pokémon with long, leafy arms and a tail full of leaves. On its back grew yellow seeds that were full of goodness for growing things.

When a tree in the jungle was sick and droopy, Sceptile visited it. It took one of its seeds and planted it gently at the tree's roots. A few days later, the tree was green again, standing tall and strong. Sceptile visited every tree in the jungle, one by one, and that's why the jungle where Sceptile lives is the greenest jungle of all.

Torchic was a little orange chick Pokémon, and inside its tummy was a tiny fire. When you hugged Torchic, it felt warm, like a fluffy hot water bottle.

Torchic liked to follow its friends wherever they went, cheep, cheep, cheep, hopping on its little legs. On chilly mornings, the children at the farm picked it up and held it in their laps while they ate breakfast. Torchic snuggled down and warmed their hands. "Cheep," it said happily, and the children shared their toast crumbs.

Combusken had strong legs and loved to practice its kicks. Hup! Hup! It kicked high, and it kicked fast, and its loud crow woke up the whole farm every morning. "Cock-a-doodle-COMBUSKEN!"

The farmer used to grumble about the noise. But one morning, he overslept on market day. Then Combusken crowed, louder than ever, right at his window. The farmer jumped out of bed, grabbed his basket of vegetables and made it to the market just in time. After that, he never grumbled about Combusken's crowing again.

Blaziken was a tall, fiery Pokémon with powerful legs. It could jump so high that it leaped right over tall buildings in a single bound. BOING!

Blaziken was the town's helper. When a kite got stuck on the roof of the tallest tower, Blaziken jumped up and got it. When a Skitty was stuck on a high ledge, Blaziken jumped up and brought it down. "Is there anything you can't reach?" asked a little girl. Blaziken thought about it. "The moon," it said. "But I'm practicing."

Mudkip was a little blue Pokémon with a fin on top of its head. The fin could feel tiny movements in the water and the air, so Mudkip always knew what was going on around it.

Mudkip looked small, but it was very strong. Once, a big boulder rolled into the stream and blocked the water. The fish Pokémon couldn't swim past. So Mudkip put its head down and pushed. Heave, heave! The boulder rolled away, and the water rushed through again. The fish cheered. Mudkip shook its fin proudly. "Mud-KIP!"

Marshtomp loved mud. Squishy, squelchy, splashy mud. It walked through the muddy marsh on its strong back legs, stomp, squelch, stomp, squelch, getting muddier with every step.

Being covered in mud kept Marshtomp's skin nice and damp. But it also made Marshtomp the best mud-pie maker in the world. It made mud pies, mud castles and mud sculptures of all its friends. Squish, pat, pat. When the rain came, the sculptures melted away, and Marshtomp just made new ones.

Swampert was a big, strong water Pokémon that could swim faster than a speedboat. It was so strong that it could pull a whole boat through the water.

Swampert also had a special talent. The fins on its head could feel when a storm was coming, long before anyone else knew. So when the clouds looked calm but Swampert started piling up rocks around its nest, the fishermen paid attention. "Storm's coming," they said, and tied up their boats. And sure enough, a storm always came, and everyone was ready.

Poochyena was a little gray puppy Pokémon with a bushy tail and a very good nose. It liked to chase things. Leaves, butterflies, its own tail. Woof, woof!

Poochyena never gave up when it was chasing something. Once, it chased a ball all the way across the meadow, through the stream and up a hill. When it finally caught it, it was so tired that it lay down in the grass with the ball between its paws. A little boy came over, panting, and laughed. "That was my ball!" Poochyena wagged its tail and gave it back.

Mightyena was a big gray Pokémon with a black, fluffy mane. It lived in a pack, and every member of the pack followed the leader very loyally.

Mightyena was the leader of its pack, and it took the job seriously. It led the way through the forest, found the best places to rest and made sure nobody got left behind. When a young Poochyena got tired, Mightyena slowed down and walked beside it, step by step, until they got home together.

Zigzagoon never walked in a straight line. It walked zig, then zag, then zig, then zag, all over the place. That's how it got its name!

Zigzagoon was very curious, and it was always finding things. A shiny button here. A lost marble there. A tasty berry under a leaf. Zigzagoon picked them all up and brought them home. One day, a little girl lost her favorite hair ribbon. Zigzagoon zigged and zagged across the whole park, and guess what it found? The ribbon, of course!

Linoone was a long, stripy Pokémon that could run very, very fast. But it could only run in straight lines. Zoom! When it came to a corner, it had to stop, turn and start again.

Linoone loved racing. On a long, straight road, nobody could beat it. Zoom, zoom, ZOOM! But on a twisty path, it kept zooming past the turns. "Oops! Wait for me!" Its friends always waited at the corners, laughing, and Linoone always caught up on the next straight bit.

Wurmple was a little red caterpillar Pokémon with spikes on its back. It loved to munch on leaves, and it was always hungry. Munch, munch, munch.

Wurmple had a big question. When it grew up, would it become a shiny white cocoon or a purple one? Nobody knew, not even Wurmple. "It's a surprise," said its friend. So Wurmple stopped worrying and kept munching. After all, the leaves were delicious, and surprises are fun.

Silcoon wrapped itself up in a cozy white cocoon made of silk. It tied itself to a tree branch with a few threads, and there it stayed, all wrapped up and warm.

Silcoon didn't move, and it didn't eat. It just rested, while its body changed on the inside. The morning dew collected on its silk like tiny pearls. Sometimes, if you looked closely, you could see Silcoon peeking out through a little gap in the silk. It was waiting to find out what it would become.

Beautifly had the most beautiful wings in the forest, with bright patterns of yellow, red and blue. It fluttered from flower to flower, sipping the sweet nectar.

When Beautifly flew over the garden, the children stopped playing to watch. "It's like a flying painting," said one. Beautifly heard them and did a little twirl in the air, showing off its wings. Then it landed on a little girl's nose for just one second, tickle, and fluttered off again. She giggled for the rest of the day.

Cascoon wrapped itself up in a purple silk cocoon and hung from a branch, very still. It had two little eyes that peeked out through the silk.

Cascoon was patient. It watched the world go by from inside its cocoon. It saw the rain fall and the flowers bloom and the other Pokémon play. Sometimes it wished it could join them. "Soon," it told itself. "Soon I'll have wings." And every night, it dreamed of flying under the moon.

Dustox was a moth Pokémon that came out at night. It had big green wings with purple patterns, and when it flew, a soft dust drifted from its wings.

Dustox loved the bright lights of the city. Every night, it flew to the tall streetlights and danced around them, fluttering its wings. The people walking home looked up and smiled. "There's the night dancer," they said. And Dustox danced until the sun came up. Then it flew back to the forest to rest.

Lotad had a big lily pad growing on top of its head. It liked to float on ponds, lazy and happy, looking just like a leaf on the water.

The lily pad was the perfect size for a little passenger. So whenever a small Pokémon needed to cross the pond, Lotad gave it a ride. A Pichu climbed on. Then a Togepi. Then a Wurmple. Lotad paddled slowly across the pond with its little feet, and everyone waved at the fish below. Paddle, paddle, splash!

Lombre was a mischievous Pokémon who lived in the river and loved to play tricks. It liked to swim up under fishing boats and tug on the fishing lines. Tug, tug!

The fishermen would shout, "I've got a big one!" and pull and pull. But when the line came up, there was nothing on the hook, just a little ripple and a giggle from under the water. Lombre swam away, laughing. The fishermen grumbled. But secretly, they thought it was pretty funny too.

Ludicolo was a happy Pokémon with a big lily pad hat and a sunny smile. And when Ludicolo heard music, it simply had to dance.

Cha-cha-cha! As soon as the band started playing, Ludicolo jumped up and danced. It wiggled its hips, it swung its arms, it kicked its feet. Everyone laughed and joined in. Soon the whole town was dancing in the square, all following Ludicolo. When the music stopped, Ludicolo took a big bow. Then it asked the band to play one more song.

Seedot looked exactly like an acorn. It liked to hang from tree branches by the little cap on its head, swinging in the breeze.

Pidgey sometimes flew by and thought Seedot was a real acorn. They tried to peck it. Peck, peck! Then Seedot opened its eyes and said, "Hey!" The Pidgey jumped so high that their feathers flew everywhere. Seedot laughed and laughed. It was the best joke in the forest, and Seedot never got tired of it.

Nuzleaf had a leaf on its head that it used to make music. When it put the leaf to its lips and blew, it made a sweet, whistling sound. Wheee-ooo!

Nuzleaf played its leaf flute every evening as the sun went down. The sound drifted through the forest, and the other Pokémon stopped to listen. Some of them felt a bit sleepy. Some felt a bit sad. Some felt very happy. Nuzleaf played until the stars came out, and then it played one last quiet tune for good night.

Shiftry lived in the oldest trees in the forest. It had big leafy fans on its arms, and when it waved them, it made gusts of wind. Whoosh!

The people in the village told stories about Shiftry, the guardian of the forest. When autumn came, Shiftry waved its fans, and all the leaves came swirling down, red and gold and orange. The children ran outside and jumped into the leaf piles. "Thank you, Shiftry!" they shouted to the wind. And a gentle breeze always answered back.

Taillow was a small bird Pokémon who was very, very brave. Even though it was little, it wasn't scared of anything. It flew right up to big Pokémon and said hello.

When winter came, Taillow got a little homesick for the warm south. So it gathered all the little birds in the town and led them on a trip to the sunny lands. Flap, flap, flap. It was a long way, but Taillow was brave, and it never let anyone fall behind. When spring came, they all flew home together.

Swellow was a beautiful bird Pokémon with shiny blue feathers and a long, forked tail. It loved to fly high and fast, swooping through the sky.

Swellow took great care of its feathers. Every morning, it cleaned and smoothed each one, until it shone like a mirror. When it flew past the lake, its reflection flashed in the water. Whoosh! The fish Pokémon looked up. "There goes Swellow," they said, "the shiniest bird in the sky." And Swellow did an extra loop, just to show off.

Wingull was a white seabird Pokémon with long, thin wings. It loved to ride on the sea breezes, gliding up and down without flapping at all. Glide, glide, glide.

Wingull liked to carry little treasures in its beak and hide them in its nest on the cliff. Shells, pebbles, bits of colorful glass from the sea. When the children came to the beach, Wingull flew down and dropped a shell at their feet. "For me?" they asked. Wingull flew away, and when they looked up, it was gliding on the wind again.

Pelipper had a huge yellow beak that could hold lots of things. It flew over the sea, carrying things from one place to another, like a flying mailbox.

Pelipper delivered letters to the little islands where there were no post offices. It carried them in its beak, flew across the water and dropped them at each house. Plop! The islanders waved. "Thank you, Pelipper!" One day it brought a letter to a little boy from his grandmother far away. He read it three times, smiling, while Pelipper rested on his roof.

Ralts was a little Pokémon with green hair that covered its eyes and two little red horns. With those horns, Ralts could feel what people around it were feeling.

When people were angry, Ralts felt it, and it hid. When people were sad, Ralts felt that too, and it came closer to comfort them. But when people were happy, Ralts felt warm and cheerful all over. That's why Ralts liked to be around kind, happy people. So if you smile at Ralts, it will smile right back.

Kirlia was a graceful Pokémon who loved to dance. It had a skirt like a ballerina, and when it spun, it spun so lightly that it almost floated.

Kirlia danced whenever its friends were happy. If its friend laughed, Kirlia twirled. If its friend sang, Kirlia leaped. And if its friend had the best day ever, Kirlia danced so beautifully that the air around it seemed to sparkle. Pirouette, leap, spin! Happy feelings were Kirlia's favorite music.

Gardevoir was a tall, elegant Pokémon with a long, flowing gown. It cared deeply about its friends, and it would do anything to keep them safe.

One night, a little girl got lost in the forest. It was dark, and she was scared. Then a soft light appeared between the trees. It was Gardevoir, glowing gently. It took her hand and walked with her through the dark, all the way home. When the girl got to her door, she turned around to say thank you. But Gardevoir had already vanished, leaving only a faint glow and a warm feeling.

Surskit was a little blue bug Pokémon that could skate across the top of the water, like an ice skater on a frozen pond. Skate, skate, skate!

It had a special trick: it made a sweet syrup on top of its head. The syrup smelled like honey and flowers. When the little Pokémon came to the pond, Surskit skated over to them and shared a taste. Mmm! Then it skated off again, twirling in circles on the water while everyone cheered.

Masquerain had big antennae with patterns that looked like angry eyes. But behind those fake eyes was a gentle Pokémon who just liked to fly around and enjoy the breeze.

When Masquerain flew through the forest, other Pokémon sometimes got startled. "Those eyes!" they said. "It looks so cross!" But then Masquerain turned around and smiled with its real face, and they laughed. "Oh, it's just pretending." Masquerain flapped its four wings and floated off, looking very pleased with its disguise.

Shroomish was a little round mushroom Pokémon that lived on the damp forest floor. It liked dark, wet places under fallen leaves.

When something startled Shroomish, it shook its head, and a little puff of spores came out. Poof! The spores floated in the air and made everybody nearby sneeze. Achoo! Achoo! Shroomish didn't mean to cause so much sneezing. It just got shy. So now its friends always say hello very softly, and Shroomish only goes poof when it's really, really surprised.

Breloom had a mushroom cap on its head and a long, stretchy arm that could reach really far. Boing! Its arms stretched out and snapped back like springs.

Breloom used its stretchy arms to help in the forest. It reached up and picked fruit from the very top of the trees. It reached across the stream and helped little Pokémon cross. And once, it reached down into a deep hole and pulled out a little Zigzagoon who had fallen in. "Thanks, Breloom!" said Zigzagoon, shaking off the dirt. Boing! went Breloom's arm, back to normal.

Slakoth was the laziest Pokémon in the whole jungle. It spent twenty hours a day lying down, and it only moved when it absolutely had to. Yawn.

Slakoth ate the leaves that were close enough to reach without getting up. When those leaves were gone, it rolled over to a new spot. Slowly. Very slowly. Its friends came to visit and asked, "Don't you want to play?" Slakoth thought about it for a long time. "Maybe tomorrow," it said, and went back to sleep. Zzz.

Vigoroth was the opposite of lazy. It couldn't sit still for even one second! It jumped, it ran, it climbed, it spun. Zoom, zoom, zoom!

At bedtime, Vigoroth tried to lie down. But its feet kept wiggling, and its arms kept waving, and its tail kept swishing. "I can't sleep!" it said. So its friends gave it a job: run ten laps around the tree. Zoom, zoom, zoom... By the tenth lap, Vigoroth was so tired that it flopped onto the grass and fell fast asleep.

Slaking was big and strong, but it was also very, very lazy. It lay on its tummy all day long and ate the grass right next to it. Munch, munch, munch.

When all the grass around Slaking was gone, it would grumble and roll over to a new spot. Then it would eat that grass. Munch, munch. The gardeners in the village were very happy about this. "Slaking is the best lawnmower we've ever had," they said, "and it never needs any gas." Slaking just yawned and kept munching.

Nincada lived underground for a long, long time. It was almost blind from living in the dark, so it used its feelers to find its way around. Feel, feel, feel.

Nincada spent its days sipping water from tree roots and sleeping in the cool earth. It was very patient. It knew that someday, it would climb out of the ground and see the sunshine. Until then, it was happy in its quiet, dark home, listening to the sounds of the world above.

Ninjask was so fast that it was almost invisible. Zip! It was here. Zip! It was there. All you could hear was the buzz of its wings. Bzzzz.

Ninjask's friends loved to play catch with it. They threw a ball, and Ninjask caught it before it even touched the ground. Zip! They threw it higher. Zip! Ninjask caught it again. "How do you do that?" they asked. But Ninjask was already gone, buzzing around the meadow, looking for the next ball.

Shedinja was a very strange and mysterious Pokémon. It was a hollow, golden shell that floated quietly in the air. It didn't eat, it didn't breathe and it never made a sound.

Shedinja appeared one day when a Nincada grew up and left its old shell behind. Instead of staying on the ground, the shell floated up and became a Pokémon all on its own. Shedinja liked to drift along beside the Ninjask, quietly keeping them company. It never said anything. But it was always there, and its friends were glad of that.

Whismur was a small pink Pokémon with big round ears. Usually it was very, very quiet, whispering so softly you could barely hear it.

But when Whismur got scared, it covered its ears and cried out so loudly that the windows rattled. WAAAAH! Everyone jumped. So its friends learned to be extra careful and not startle it. They tiptoed. They whispered. And when Whismur wasn't scared, it whispered back the sweetest little secrets you have ever heard.

Loudred was a Pokémon with big ears like speakers, and it was very, very LOUD. When it shouted, its whole body shook, and its voice boomed across the valley. "HELLO!"

The other Pokémon covered their ears. "Not so loud, Loudred!" But one day, a little Pichu got lost on the other side of the mountain. Nobody could find it. Then Loudred took a deep breath and shouted, "PICHU! THIS WAY!" Its voice boomed over the mountain, and the little Pichu followed it all the way home. After that, nobody minded the noise.

Exploud was covered in tubes and pipes, and it could make all kinds of sounds through them, like a big, walking band. Toot! Honk! Whistle!

Exploud talked to its friends by playing different sounds. A whistle meant "Hello!" A honk meant "Let's play!" And a soft hum meant "Good night." At the village festival, Exploud played all its sounds at once, and it was the best music anyone had ever heard. The children danced until their feet were tired.

Makuhita was a sturdy little Pokémon who loved to practice its pushing. It pushed against trees, and it pushed against rocks, and it pushed against the wind. Hup! Hup! Hup!

Makuhita never gave up. If it fell down, it got right back up and pushed again. It ate a big bowl of rice every evening, so it would be strong for tomorrow's practice. "Someday," Makuhita said, "I'll push a whole mountain." Its friends laughed. But they also helped it carry its rice.

Hariyama was a big, strong Pokémon who practiced pushing and stomping every day. It was so strong that it could push a truck. Stomp! Stomp!

But Hariyama was gentle with little ones. When the children came to watch it practice, Hariyama let them sit on its shoulders and gave them rides around the field. Stomp, stomp, giggle. At the end of the day, it ate a huge bowl of noodles and fell asleep with a big smile. Being strong was fun, but giving rides was even more fun.

Azurill was a tiny blue Pokémon with a big, round, bouncy tail. The tail was even bigger than Azurill itself!

Azurill loved to bounce on its tail. Boing, boing, boing! It bounced across the grass, over puddles and around trees. Sometimes it swung its tail around and around and then let go, flinging itself through the air. Wheee! It landed with a soft bounce on the grass and giggled. Then it did it all over again.

Nosepass was a Pokémon made of stone with a big red nose. And its nose was a magnet that always, always pointed north, like a compass.

Nosepass never moved much. It just stood still, its nose pointing north. But hikers loved it. When they got lost in the mountains, they looked for Nosepass. "Which way is north?" they asked. Nosepass's nose pointed the way. And the hikers found their path home, thanking the little stone Pokémon with the magnet nose.

Skitty was a pink kitten Pokémon with a long tail and a playful heart. It loved anything that moved, and most of all, it loved chasing its own tail.

Round and round Skitty went, chasing, chasing, chasing. Zoom, zoom, zoom! It never caught its tail, but that didn't matter. It got so dizzy that it flopped onto the floor, giggling. The little girl who lived with Skitty watched and laughed. "Silly Skitty," she said, and rubbed its tummy until it purred.

When Skitty touched a sparkly Moon Stone, it became Delcatty, an elegant cat Pokémon with soft purple fur. Delcatty liked to do things its own way.

Delcatty didn't have a favorite bed. It napped wherever it liked: on the sunny windowsill, on top of the bookshelf, in a basket of warm laundry. Its family never knew where they would find it next. "Where's Delcatty?" they would ask. And somewhere, a soft purr would answer.

Sableye lived in dark caves deep in the mountains. Its eyes were two sparkling gems, and it loved anything that sparkled.

Sableye spent its days digging for shiny crystals in the cave walls. Scratch, scratch, sparkle! It munched on some of them, crunch, and kept the prettiest ones in a pile. When a lost boy wandered into the cave with a flashlight, Sableye's gem eyes glittered in the light. The boy jumped. But then Sableye held out a shiny crystal as a gift, and the boy smiled.

Mawile was a small, cute Pokémon with big eyes and a sweet smile. But on the back of its head was a big, strong pair of jaws, like a giant ponytail.

The jaws were very useful. Mawile carried things in them, like a backpack! It carried apples, toys and even its little friends. "All aboard!" said Mawile, and three Pichu climbed into its back jaws. They rode around the park, giggling, while Mawile skipped along with a big smile.

Aron was a small Pokémon covered in hard steel armor. It loved to eat iron. Crunch, crunch, crunch! It found little bits of iron in the mountain rocks and munched them like crackers.

Every time Aron ate iron, its armor got a little stronger and a little shinier. When it bumped into something, clang! It didn't even notice. Aron's friends liked to knock on its armor. Knock, knock. "Is anybody home?" And Aron would peek out and say, "Me! Always me!"

Lairon was a strong steel Pokémon who loved its mountain home. It drank fresh water from the mountain springs and munched on iron rocks, and its armor shone in the sun.

Lairon's armor was so hard that it could walk right through bushes and over sharp rocks without getting a scratch. It liked to explore the mountain, clang, clang, clang, looking for new springs. When it found a really good one, it brought all its friends to share the fresh, cold water. "Ahh," they all said together.

Aggron was a huge steel Pokémon who loved its mountain. It thought of the whole mountain as its home, and it took very good care of it.

One summer, a big rockslide knocked down lots of trees on Aggron's mountain. The slopes were bare and sad. So Aggron got to work. It carried soil up the mountain, load after load. It planted new trees, one by one. It took a very long time. But Aggron never gave up, and years later, the mountain was green and full of trees again.

Meditite was a small Pokémon who loved to meditate. Every morning, it sat very still with its eyes closed, breathing slowly. In... and out... In... and out...

Meditite ate only one berry a day, and it practiced its balance by standing on one foot for hours. Its friends tried to copy it, but they always wobbled and fell over. Wobble, wobble, plop! Meditite smiled. "Just breathe," it said. "In... and out..." Try it now. Breathe in... and out... Doesn't that feel nice?

Medicham was a graceful Pokémon who moved like a dancer. It had practiced and meditated for so long that it could sense what others were feeling.

Medicham liked to teach the young Pokémon how to stretch and how to breathe. "Reach up high," it said. "Now touch your toes." They all stretched together in the morning sunshine. Then Medicham showed them a slow, beautiful dance, and they copied it, step by step. It was the most peaceful way to start a day.

Electrike was a little green puppy Pokémon with a yellow mane. When it ran, the wind rubbed against its fur and made static electricity. Bzzt, bzzt!

The faster Electrike ran, the more electricity it collected. Its fur crackled and sparkled. Electrike loved running on breezy days. Zoom! It came back sparkling and buzzing with energy. "Don't pet it yet!" said the children, laughing, because they knew they would get a little zap.

Manectric was a strong electric Pokémon with a spiky blue and yellow mane. Its mane crackled with electricity, and it could make sparks fly whenever it wanted.

Manectric loved thunderstorms, and people said it made its nest wherever lightning struck. During a storm, it stood on the hilltop with its mane glowing, watching the lightning dance across the sky. When the storm was over, it trotted home through the puddles, its mane still sparkling like a string of lights.

Plusle was a little cheerleader Pokémon with red cheeks and plus signs on its cheeks and tail. It loved to cheer for its friends, and it cheered with sparks! Fizz, fizz, pop!

Whenever its friends tried something hard, Plusle was there, waving its arms and making little pom-poms of sparkly light. "You can do it! Go, go, go!" When a little Wurmple tried to climb a tall tree, Plusle cheered the whole way up. And when Wurmple reached the top, Plusle cheered so hard that it made fireworks.

Minun was a little blue Pokémon with minus signs on its cheeks and tail, and it was Plusle's best friend. Like Plusle, Minun loved to cheer, and it made sparkly pom-poms too.

Minun cared about its friends so much. If a friend was falling behind in a race, Minun cheered even louder, until its pom-poms sparkled bright blue. "Don't give up!" Together, Plusle and Minun made the best cheering team in the world. Red sparks and blue sparks, plus and minus, side by side.

Volbeat was a firefly Pokémon whose tail glowed with a bright light. At night, it flew through the sky, and its tail left a trail of light behind it.

When lots of Volbeat flew together, they drew shapes in the night sky with their lights. Stars, circles, hearts and squiggles! The children in the village came out on summer nights to watch the light show. "Draw a moon!" they called. And the Volbeat drew a big round moon, glowing right next to the real one.

Illumise was a firefly Pokémon with a sweet perfume. At night, it sent out its sweet smell, and all the Volbeat followed it through the sky.

Illumise was the leader of the light show. It flew this way and that, and the Volbeat followed, drawing pictures in the sky with their glowing tails. Swirl, loop, zigzag! Illumise planned a new picture every night. The children never knew what it would be. A flower? A fish? A smiling face? They waited every night to find out.

Roselia had a red rose on one hand and a blue rose on the other. Its roses gave off a lovely smell, and the cleaner the water it drank, the more beautiful its roses grew.

Roselia loved its garden by the clear mountain stream. It drank the fresh, clean water every morning, and its roses bloomed bright and sweet. When people walked past, they stopped to smell the air. "Mmm, roses!" Roselia waved its flowers, happy to share. It always reminded its friends: keep the stream clean, and the roses will bloom.

Gulpin was a little green Pokémon that was almost all tummy. It had a tiny heart and a tiny brain, but its tummy was enormous, and it could swallow almost anything in one big gulp!

Gulpin would eat anything. Berries? Gulp. Leaves? Gulp. A whole sandwich? GULP! One day, it gulped down a whole picnic's worth of sandwiches before anyone could stop it. The children stared. Gulpin looked at them, burped a tiny burp and smiled. "Sorry," it said. "They looked delicious." Everyone laughed and made more sandwiches.

Swalot was a big purple Pokémon with a wide mouth and no teeth at all. It could open its mouth so wide that it could swallow a whole watermelon in one gulp!

Swalot didn't chew. It just swallowed. Gulp! The children loved watching it eat. They lined up watermelons on the table, and Swalot swallowed them, one by one. Gulp, gulp, gulp! Then it patted its round tummy and let out a big, happy sigh. "Ahhh. Delicious."

Carvanha was a small fish Pokémon with a big mouth full of sharp teeth. It lived in rivers deep in the jungle, swimming in big, fast groups. Zip, zip, zip!

When the Carvanha swam together, the river looked like it was sparkling. They moved as one, turning left, turning right, all at the same time. Zip! Swish! The other fish watched them in wonder. And the Carvanha never left anyone behind. If one got tired, the whole group slowed down to wait.

Sharpedo was a shark Pokémon that could swim incredibly fast. It shot water out behind it, like a jet, and zoomed across the ocean. ZOOM!

Sharpedo was the fastest swimmer in the sea, and it loved racing. When ships sailed across the ocean, Sharpedo raced alongside them, jumping out of the water. Splash! Splash! The sailors cheered. "Look at it go!" Sharpedo always won, of course. Then it did a big splashy flip to say goodbye.

Wailmer was a round, bouncy whale Pokémon. It liked to gulp in seawater until it was as round as a beach ball, and then bounce along the beach. Boing! Boing!

When Wailmer was full of water, it sprayed it out of the hole on top of its head. Whoosh! A tall fountain of water shot up into the sky. The children on the beach ran through the spray, squealing with delight. "Again, Wailmer! Again!" And Wailmer gulped and sprayed again, as many times as they wanted.

Wailord was one of the biggest Pokémon of all. It was as long as a whole street, and when it swam, it looked like an island moving through the sea.

Wailord swam slowly through the ocean, singing a deep, rumbly song. Hmmmmmmmm. The song traveled through the water for miles and miles. Other Wailord far away heard it and sang back. When sailors heard the singing, they stopped and listened. "Wailord is talking to its friends," they whispered. And they kept very quiet so they could hear.

Numel was a little Pokémon with a hump on its back, and inside the hump was hot, bubbling magma. It was very slow, and it didn't seem to notice much of anything.

Numel didn't mind the heat, and it didn't mind the cold. Hot sun? Fine. Snowstorm? Fine. When its friends were cold in winter, they snuggled up against Numel's warm hump. "Ahh, so cozy," they said. Numel blinked slowly. It hadn't noticed it was being a heater. But it was happy to have friends nearby.

Camerupt was a big Pokémon with two volcanoes on its back. The volcanoes rumbled and steamed, and sometimes they puffed out little clouds of warm smoke.

When winter came, Camerupt went to the village hot spring and sat down right next to it. Its volcanoes warmed up the water, and soon the hot spring was steaming and cozy. All the Pokémon came to soak in it. "Ahhh," they sighed, relaxing in the warm water. Camerupt smiled and puffed out a happy little cloud.

Torkoal was a tortoise Pokémon with a shell full of fire. It puffed out black smoke from the holes in its shell, puff, puff, puff, like a little steam engine.

Torkoal lived in the mountains, where it dug up coal to burn inside its shell. When it was happy, it puffed out more smoke. The villagers could see the smoke from far away, and they knew Torkoal was in a good mood. One cold morning, Torkoal puffed so happily that it made smoke rings. The children counted them: one, two, three... twenty!

Spoink was a little gray Pokémon that bounced on its springy tail. Boing! Boing! Boing! It never stopped bouncing, not even for a second.

On top of Spoink's head was a shiny pink pearl, and Spoink was very proud of it. It bounced through the meadow, showing its pearl to everyone. "Look at my pearl!" Boing! "Isn't it shiny?" Boing! Its friends tried to bounce like Spoink, but they always fell down. Spoink giggled and bounced circles around them.

Grumpig was a Pokémon with two black pearls on its head. It used the pearls to help it concentrate, and when it danced, the pearls glowed.

Grumpig liked to dance a strange, wiggly dance. Wiggle to the left, wiggle to the right, hop, hop, spin! When it danced, its pearls glowed purple, and everyone watching felt a little bit dizzy and a little bit happy. "What kind of dance is that?" asked a friend. "The Grumpig dance," said Grumpig. "Want to learn?"

Spinda was a wobbly little Pokémon who could never walk in a straight line. It tottered and tumbled and spun, as if it were dizzy all the time. Wobble, wobble, spin!

And here's the amazing thing: every Spinda in the whole world has a different pattern of spots. No two are the same! So when the Spinda got together, they played a game called find your twin. They wobbled around, looking at each other's spots. But nobody ever found a twin. And every time, they all fell down laughing.

Trapinch lived in the desert, in a cozy pit at the bottom of the sand. It had a big head with big jaws, and it waited at the bottom of its pit very, very patiently.

Trapinch could wait for a whole week without getting bored. It watched the sand slide down. It watched the clouds float by. It counted the stars at night. "One, two, three..." When its friends came to visit, they slid down the sandy sides of the pit like a slide. Wheee! It was Trapinch's favorite part of the week.

Vibrava had long, thin wings, but they weren't big enough to fly far yet. So Vibrava flapped them very, very fast. Bzzzzzz! The fast flapping made a humming sound.

Vibrava practiced its flying every day in the desert. Flap, flap, buzz! It went a little bit farther each time. When it hummed its wings just right, the sound was almost like music. The desert Pokémon came to listen to Vibrava's humming, and they all agreed it was the best song in the sand.

Flygon was a beautiful green dragon Pokémon with red covers over its eyes to keep out the sand. When it flapped its wings, it made a soft singing sound, and the sand below swirled up around it.

People called Flygon the spirit of the desert. Travelers who got lost in a sandstorm sometimes heard a gentle singing in the wind. If they followed the song, they found their way out of the storm and into a green oasis with cool water and shady palm trees. And above them, a green shape flew away into the sky.

Cacnea was a little cactus Pokémon with prickly arms and a round green body. It lived in the hot, dry desert, where it hardly ever rained.

Once a year, something wonderful happened. A beautiful yellow flower bloomed on top of Cacnea's head, and it smelled sweet and lovely. All the desert Pokémon came to see it. "Your flower is so pretty, Cacnea!" Cacnea blushed. It waited all year for that one flower, and it was always worth the wait.

Cacturne was a tall cactus Pokémon who stood very still in the desert during the hot day. But when the cool night came, it woke up and walked through the sand, step, step, step.

Cacturne knew the desert well. It knew where every rock and every dune was, even in the dark. When travelers crossed the desert at night, they sometimes saw a tall shape walking ahead of them. Cacturne led them to the cool caves where they could rest. By morning, it was standing still again, pretending to be just a cactus.

Swablu was a little blue bird Pokémon with fluffy white wings that looked like cotton clouds. It loved everything to be neat and clean.

If Swablu saw something dirty, it cleaned it with its fluffy wings. Swish, swish! It wiped dusty windows and polished shiny apples. And it loved to land on people's heads and sit there like a soft, fluffy hat. "I'm wearing a Swablu!" the children giggled. Swablu just fluffed up its wings and made itself comfortable.

Altaria was a blue dragon Pokémon with big, fluffy wings like clouds. It loved to fly through the sky and sing.

Altaria's song was the most beautiful sound in the world. It sang high and clear, like a silver bell. When it flew among the white clouds, it was hard to tell which were clouds and which were Altaria's wings. The children lay on the grass and looked up. "Which one is Altaria?" they asked. Then they heard the singing, and they knew.

Zangoose was a white Pokémon with red markings and sharp claws. It liked to stand up tall on its back legs and keep its fur nice and clean. Lick, lick, lick.

Zangoose was always very curious about the world. It peeked under rocks, sniffed every flower and asked everyone questions. "What's that? Where are you going? Can I come too?"
