Its friends sometimes found it a little tiring. But whenever they went on an adventure, Zangoose was the first one ready to go.

Seviper was a long, dark Pokémon with a pointed tail. Every day, it rubbed its tail against the rocks to keep it smooth and shiny. Scrape, scrape, scrape.

Seviper liked to slither through the tall grass and curl up in sunny spots. It was a little grumpy in the mornings, but in the warm afternoon sun, it relaxed and stretched out. When the children found it napping on a rock, they whispered, "Shh, Seviper is sunbathing." And Seviper, with one eye open, smiled to itself.

Lunatone was a Pokémon shaped like a crescent moon. People first found one at the spot where a meteor had fallen from the sky, long, long ago.

Lunatone was quiet during the day. But when the full moon rose, it woke up and floated into the night sky, glowing softly. The moon and Lunatone seemed to shine at each other, like old friends. "Look," said the children, "there are two moons tonight." And they watched until Lunatone floated back down and settled into its quiet spot.

Solrock was a Pokémon shaped like the sun. It floated in the air, spinning slowly, and it shone with a warm, golden light.

Solrock loved sunny days. When the sun was out, Solrock spun faster and glowed brighter, filling the air with warmth. People said that Solrock came from space, just like Lunatone. During the day, Solrock shone. At night, Lunatone glowed. Together, they took turns keeping the sky bright, all day and all night.

Barboach was a slippery fish Pokémon with long whiskers. It lived in muddy ponds, and its body was so slimy that nobody could ever hold onto it.

Barboach used its whiskers to feel around in the mud for tasty snacks. Wiggle, wiggle, wiggle. When fishermen tried to pick it up, it slipped right out of their hands. Bloop! "Come back!" they shouted, laughing. But Barboach was already back in the mud, wiggling its whiskers and hiding from view.

Whiscash was a big fish Pokémon with long whiskers, and it lived in a big pond. It was very protective of its home and didn't like anyone making a mess.

Whiscash could feel the ground shaking before anyone else could. When it sensed that the earth was going to rumble, it splashed and splashed to warn everyone. Splash! Splash! The little Pokémon knew what that meant. They hurried to safe places and waited until the rumbling was over. Then Whiscash went back to guarding its pond, quiet and calm.

Corphish was a little red crayfish Pokémon with big pincers. It was tough and strong, and it could live almost anywhere, even in muddy, messy ditches.

Corphish liked to explore new places. It walked along the riverbank, click, clack, click, clack, poking its pincers into everything. "What's under this rock? What's in this puddle?" When it found something interesting, it waved its pincers in the air, very excited. Click, clack! Corphish was the best explorer in the whole river.

Crawdaunt was a big red crayfish Pokémon with giant pincers and a star on its head. It was the boss of its pond, and it liked everything just so.

Every morning, Crawdaunt walked around the pond to make sure everything was tidy. It moved the pebbles into neat rows. It pushed the floating leaves to the edge. Click, clack! The little fish Pokémon giggled at how fussy it was. But when the pond was neat and clean, everyone agreed it was the nicest pond around.

Baltoy was a little clay Pokémon that looked like an old toy. It spun around and around on its one foot, like a spinning top. Whirrrr!

People found Baltoy in very old ruins, from long, long ago. Baltoy loved to spin. It spun when it was happy. It spun when it was bored. It spun to say hello. And when lots of Baltoy got together, they all spun at once, and the sound was like a soft humming song. Whirrrr, whirrrr.

Claydol was a tall clay figure from ancient times, covered in little eyes. It didn't have legs. Instead, it floated in the air, quietly, as if it were thinking very hard.

People said that Claydol was made of clay a very long time ago, and then one day it woke up. Now it floated through the ruins, watching over them. When explorers came to dig, Claydol floated beside them and pointed with its arms. "Dig here," it seemed to say. And they always found something wonderful.

Lileep was an ancient Pokémon that looked like a pink sea flower. Long, long ago, it lived at the bottom of the sea, holding onto rocks with its feet.

Scientists brought Lileep back from a fossil. Now it lived in a big tank at the museum, swaying gently in the water. Sway, sway, sway. The children came to see it every Saturday. They pressed their noses against the glass and waved. And Lileep waved its pink petals back, very slowly, as if to say, "Hello, little ones. Thank you for visiting."

Cradily was an ancient Pokémon with long, green tentacles that looked like flower petals. It lived in warm, shallow seas long, long ago, and it moved very slowly.

When the tide went out, Cradily crept onto the beach, looking for good things to eat. Creep, creep, creep. Then, when the tide came back in, it crept back into the water. It had been doing this since ancient times. The beach Pokémon knew exactly when Cradily would come. "Here comes Cradily," they said, "just like always."

Anorith was an ancient Pokémon that lived in the sea long, long ago. It had a hard shell and two big claws, and it swam by waving the little wings on its sides. Flap, flap, flap.

When scientists woke Anorith up from its fossil, it was surprised. Everything was so different! But Anorith was brave. It waved its claws at its new friends and swam happily around its new home. "Hello!" it seemed to say. "Do you want to swim with me?"

Armaldo was an ancient Pokémon covered in strong armor. Long, long ago, its family climbed out of the sea and learned to walk on land.

Armaldo's armor was so strong that nothing could scratch it. It walked slowly and proudly through the forest, clank, clank, clank, and the little Pokémon followed behind it. "Tell us about the old days," they begged. And Armaldo told them about ancient seas and giant ferns, back when the world was young.

Feebas was a plain little fish Pokémon with dull brown scales and ragged fins. The other fish said it wasn't pretty, and most people didn't even notice it.

But Feebas didn't give up. It was tough, and it could live anywhere, even in murky ponds where other fish couldn't. And Feebas had a secret: deep inside, it was getting ready for something special. "Just wait," it said to itself. "One day, everyone will see." Because Feebas would grow into one of the most beautiful Pokémon of all.

Once there was a plain little Feebas that nobody noticed. And then one day, it changed into Milotic, the most beautiful Pokémon in the world.

Milotic had shimmering scales that shone like a rainbow, and long, flowing fins like ribbons. When people saw it, any grumpiness they felt just melted away. Two children who had been arguing all morning saw Milotic gliding through the lake and forgot what they were arguing about. They just stood there, holding hands, watching it shimmer.

Castform was a little Pokémon that changed with the weather. When it was sunny, it turned into a tiny orange sun. When it rained, it turned into a little blue raindrop. And when it snowed, it turned into a snowy little cloud!

The children in the town checked on Castform every morning before school. "Castform is a raindrop!" they called. "Bring your umbrellas!" Or, "Castform is a sun! Wear your sun hats!" Castform was the best weather reporter in town, and it was always right.

Kecleon could change the color of its body to match anything around it. Green leaves? It turned green. Gray rocks? It turned gray. It became almost invisible!

But there was one thing Kecleon could never hide: a red zigzag stripe on its tummy. That stripe always stayed red, no matter what. So when the children played hide-and-seek with Kecleon, they knew what to look for. "I see a red stripe!" they shouted, pointing at a plant. And the plant giggled and turned back into Kecleon.

Shuppet was a little ghost Pokémon that looked like a puppet with a horn. It floated around at night, and it had a funny favorite food: grumpy feelings.

When someone in the house felt cross or jealous, Shuppet floated over and gobbled the feeling right up. Nom, nom! The cross feeling disappeared, and the person felt better. "Why am I not grumpy anymore?" they wondered. They never saw Shuppet, floating in the corner, licking its lips. Grumpy feelings were its favorite snack.

Banette was once a little stuffed toy. One day, it came to life, with a zipper mouth and bright red eyes. And it went looking for a new friend.

Banette searched and searched. It peeked in windows and looked under beds. Then it found a little girl who was playing alone in her room. Banette sat down beside her. She looked at it. It looked at her. "Do you want to play?" she asked. Banette's zipper mouth curled into a smile. From then on, it never had to look for a friend again.

Duskull was a little ghost Pokémon with one big glowing eye. It floated through the streets at night, looking for children who were still awake past bedtime.

When Duskull found a child who was still awake, it floated up to the window and peeked in with its glowing eye. Blink! "Time for bed," it seemed to say. The child giggled and pulled up the covers. Then Duskull floated away to check on the next house. So close your eyes now. Duskull is on its rounds!

Dusclops was a ghost Pokémon with a hollow body, like an empty jar. It had one big eye, and it could swallow almost anything into its body without ever getting full.

Dusclops liked to help keep the town tidy at night. It floated through the streets and swallowed up fallen leaves, lost wrappers and puddles of rainwater. Shloop! By morning, the streets were clean and dry. Nobody knew where it all went. Dusclops just floated home with its one eye half-closed, ready for a long day's sleep.

Tropius was a big, gentle Pokémon with leaves for wings and a bunch of yellow fruit growing around its neck. The fruit was sweet and delicious, and it grew back every year.

Tropius lived in a warm, sunny jungle. Every day, the children ran out to see it, and Tropius bent its long neck down so they could pick its sweet fruit. "Thank you, Tropius!" they said, munching happily. Then Tropius flapped its leafy wings and flew off, and the fruit started growing back for next time.

Chimecho was a little Pokémon shaped like a wind chime. It liked to hang from the edge of a roof, and when the wind blew, it rang. Ting, ting, ting!

Chimecho's song was soft and clear, and it could make seven different notes. When the breeze came through the town, all the Chimecho on the rooftops began to sing at once, and the whole street filled with music. Ting, ting, tinkle. The people stopped and smiled. Then they went to sleep, listening to the wind chime songs.

Absol was a white Pokémon with a curved horn on its head. Long ago, people thought Absol brought bad luck, because it always appeared right before a big storm or flood.

But Absol wasn't bringing trouble. It was trying to warn everyone! Absol could feel when something bad was coming, and it came down from the mountains to tell people to get ready. Once the villagers understood, they were so grateful. Now, when Absol appears, they say, "Thank you, Absol," and they get ready, just in time.

Wynaut was a little blue Pokémon, the baby that grows up into Wobbuffet. It was always smiling, and it said its own name to everything. "Wy-naut!"

Wynaut loved to play with its friends in big groups. They pushed against each other to practice being strong. Push, push, push! At snack time, Wynaut ate sweet fruit and grew a little bit every day. "Why not try a new berry?" asked its friend. "Wy-naut!" said Wynaut, and ate it all up.

Snorunt was a little Pokémon that lived in snowy places. It wore a cozy hood, like a winter coat, and it could keep warm even in the coldest blizzard.

People in snowy villages said that if a Snorunt visited your house, you would have good luck all year. So when the children saw a little Snorunt shuffling through the snow, they waved and left a bowl of fresh snow on the doorstep as a treat. Snorunt ate it all up, crunch, crunch, and danced in the snow outside until bedtime.

Glalie was a big round Pokémon made of ice, with a bold face and two horns. It could freeze the water in the air into sparkling ice crystals in an instant.

On hot summer days, Glalie came down from the mountain to visit the village. It breathed out a cold, frosty wind, and snowflakes sparkled in the warm air. The children squealed with delight. It was snowing in summer! They built little snowmen and had a snowball fight, all thanks to Glalie.

Spheal was a round little Pokémon that was much better at rolling than walking. It rolled across the ice wherever it wanted to go. Roll, roll, roll!

Spheal loved to clap its little flippers together. Clap, clap, clap! It clapped when it was happy. It clapped when it saw a friend. It clapped when it had a snack. And it clapped when the sun came up over the icy sea. Clap, clap! Can you clap like Spheal? Clap, clap, clap!

Sealeo was a round seal Pokémon with a very good sense of touch in its nose. It loved to balance things on its nose and spin them.

When Sealeo found something new, it balanced it on its nose and spun it around and around to learn all about it. A snowball? Spin, spin! A shell? Spin, spin! Once, it balanced a ball for so long that all the Pokémon on the beach clapped and cheered. Sealeo bowed. Then it dropped the ball. Plop! Everyone laughed, even Sealeo.

Walrein was a big walrus Pokémon with long white tusks and a thick layer of blubber that kept it warm in the icy sea. It was the leader of its herd.

When the cold winter storms came, Walrein swam in front of the herd and broke through the ice with its strong tusks, crack, crack, crack, making a path for everyone. The little Spheal rolled along behind it, safe and sound. "Stay close," Walrein called. And they did, all the way home.

Clamperl was a clam Pokémon with a beautiful pink pearl inside its shell. Each Clamperl makes just one pearl in its whole life, so it takes very good care of it.

Clamperl polished its pearl every day until it glowed. When the sunlight came down through the water, the pearl shone like a little moon. The fish Pokémon came to look at it, and Clamperl opened its shell just a little, so they could see. "It's beautiful," they whispered. Clamperl was very proud.

Huntail lived deep, deep down in the sea, where it was always dark. At the end of its tail was a little glowing light, shaped like a tiny fish.

In the dark water, Huntail's light was like a lantern. When the little sea Pokémon got lost in the deep, they followed the glow. Huntail swam slowly so they could keep up, wiggling its glowing tail. "This way, this way," it seemed to say. And it led them all the way back up to the warm, sunny water.

Gorebyss was a long, graceful pink Pokémon that lived in the deep sea. When it swam, it looked like a ribbon floating through the water.

Every spring, Gorebyss's body grew pinker and prettier. It loved to swim in slow, twirling circles near the bottom of the sea. Twirl, glide, twirl. The deep-sea Pokémon said that watching Gorebyss swim was like watching a dance. And when spring came, everyone gathered to see its prettiest pink.

Relicanth was an ancient fish Pokémon that had stayed exactly the same for a very, very long time, since before anyone could remember. It had rocky scales and a wise old face.

Relicanth lived at the bottom of the deepest sea, where the water was calm and still. It had seen the world change a thousand times. When the young fish asked, "Relicanth, what's the secret to living a long time?" it thought for a while. Then it said, "Swim slowly. Stay curious. And never forget to rest."

Luvdisc was a little pink Pokémon shaped like a heart. It lived in warm seas, where it swam in and out of the coral reefs.

People said that when two people who loved each other saw a Luvdisc together, they would be happy forever. So when grandmas and grandpas walked along the beach, they always looked into the water, hoping to spot a little pink heart. And when they did, they held hands a little tighter and smiled.

Bagon was a little blue dragon Pokémon with one big dream: it wanted to fly. Every day, it looked up at the birds in the sky and sighed. "Someday," it said.

Bagon practiced every day. It ran to the edge of a little rock, flapped its arms and jumped. Whee! Bump! It landed in the soft grass. It got up and tried again. And again. Its friends cheered it on. Bagon didn't have wings yet. But it had something even more important: it never stopped believing.

Shelgon was all wrapped up inside a hard white shell, like armor. It didn't move much, and it didn't eat much. It just waited, very patiently.

Inside its shell, Shelgon was changing. Something wonderful was growing. When its friends visited, they knocked gently on the shell. Knock, knock. "Are you okay in there?" Shelgon peeked out. "I'm busy growing wings," it said. "Come back soon. You won't believe it."

Once there was a little Bagon who dreamed of flying. It practiced every day, and it never gave up. And one morning, its shell cracked open, and out came Salamence, with big red wings!

Salamence spread its wings and flew. Up, up, up into the sky! It was so happy that it flew in loops and circles and zigzags, laughing with joy. Its friends on the ground cheered and cheered. Salamence flew all day long, higher than the birds, all the way to the clouds. Its dream had finally come true.

Beldum was a little steel Pokémon with one big red eye and a claw at the bottom. It didn't have any legs. Instead, it floated in the air, using magnetism.

Beldum talked to other Beldum by sending out little magnetic pulses. Bip, bip, bip! They couldn't speak out loud, but they understood each other perfectly. When lots of Beldum floated together, they all moved at the same time, like a flock of shiny birds. Bip, bip! "This way!" And off they floated together.

Metang was two Beldum joined together into one. It had two big claws and two brains, and it was twice as smart as a Beldum.

Metang liked to think about things very carefully. It floated through the forest, examining everything with its red eyes. A pinecone? Hmm. A rock? Hmm. A little Pichu? "Hello," said the Pichu. Metang thought about that for a while. Then it gently lifted the Pichu with its magnetic power and gave it a ride, floating through the trees. Pichu decided Metang was its smartest friend.

Metagross was a huge steel Pokémon with four legs and four brains. It was super, super smart, smarter than the smartest computer!

Metagross could solve any puzzle in seconds. The children brought it their hardest riddles, and Metagross solved them all. "What has keys but can't open locks?" "A piano," said Metagross. "What goes up but never comes down?" "Your age," said Metagross. The children laughed and tried to think of a harder one. They never could.

Regirock was a legendary Pokémon made entirely of rocks. It had no face, just seven little dots that glowed in a pattern. Nobody knew who made it or how long ago.

Regirock slept for thousands of years inside an ancient cave. When it finally woke up, it walked out slowly into the sunshine. Thud, thud, thud. Its dots blinked at the bright light. The little Pokémon peeked at it from behind the trees. Regirock didn't say anything. It just sat down in the sun, warming its old stones.

Regice was a legendary Pokémon made of ancient ice that never melts, not even in the hottest summer. It had seven little dots on its face that glowed like stars.

Regice lived in a cold, quiet cave. It liked the cold, and it breathed out a chilly mist. On the hottest summer day, the village children went to visit it. They sat in the cool cave next to Regice, and the air felt lovely and fresh. "Thank you, Regice," they said. Regice's dots twinkled, just a little.

Registeel was a legendary Pokémon made of a mysterious metal, harder than any metal people knew. Its body was hollow inside, and it had seven little dots on its face.

People had tried and tried to scratch Registeel's metal, but nothing could. It lived in an ancient temple and stood very still for hundreds of years. Every so often, it took a slow, clanking walk around the temple. Clank, clank. Then it went back to its spot and stood still again. It was in no hurry at all.

Latias was a legendary dragon Pokémon with red and white feathers. It was very gentle and very clever, and it could make itself invisible by bending the light around it.

Latias could understand people's feelings, and it liked kind people. When it saw someone who was sad, it flew down invisibly and sat beside them. They couldn't see it. But they felt a soft, warm feeling, as if someone was giving them a hug. And when they looked up, they sometimes saw a little shimmer in the air, flying away.

Latios was a legendary dragon Pokémon with blue and white feathers. It could fly faster than a jet plane, folding its arms close to its body and zooming across the sky. ZOOM!

Latios could also do something amazing: it could show pictures from its mind to people it trusted. When a little boy told Latios that he wished he could fly, Latios showed him what it saw while flying: the clouds, the sea, the mountains, the whole world spread out below. The boy gasped. "Wow," he whispered. "It's beautiful."

Kyogre was a legendary Pokémon of the sea, a giant blue Pokémon with glowing red lines on its body. People said that long ago, it made the oceans grow bigger.

Kyogre slept at the bottom of the deepest sea. When it woke up, it brought the rain. Pitter, patter, pitter, patter. The rain fell on the thirsty fields, and the farmers cheered. Then Kyogre went back to sleep, deep in the ocean, and the sun came out again.

Groudon was a legendary Pokémon of the land, a giant red Pokémon with glowing lines on its body. People said that long ago, it raised up the land and made the continents bigger.

Groudon slept deep inside the earth, where it was warm. When it woke up, it brought the sunshine. The clouds went away, and the sun shone bright and hot. The puddles dried up, and the flowers lifted their faces to the sky. Then Groudon went back to sleep, deep in the earth, and the rain could come again.

Rayquaza was a legendary green dragon that lived high up in the sky, higher than the clouds, higher than the birds, where the sky turns dark blue. It almost never came down.

But once, long ago, Kyogre and Groudon had a big argument. Kyogre wanted rain, and Groudon wanted sun. They argued and argued. Then Rayquaza came swooping down from the sky. "Enough!" it roared. "There's room for both rain and sun." Kyogre and Groudon looked at each other. Then they went back to sleep, and that's why we have rainy days and sunny days.

Jirachi was a tiny Mythical Pokémon with a star-shaped head and little paper tags hanging from it. It slept for a thousand years, and then woke up for just seven days.

During those seven days, Jirachi granted wishes. If you wrote your wish on one of its paper tags, it might come true. One little girl wrote, "I wish my grandpa feels better." Jirachi read it and smiled. And by the next week, her grandpa was out in the garden again. Then Jirachi went back to sleep for another thousand years.

Deoxys came from outer space. Long ago, it rode down to the earth on a falling star. It had a crystal in its chest that glowed, and it could change its shape whenever it wanted.

Deoxys could be strong, or fast, or tough, just by changing its form. Sometimes, at night, it looked up at the stars and wondered about its old home far away. But then it looked around at the trees and the mountains and the Pokémon sleeping peacefully. "This is a good home too," it thought, and its crystal glowed warm.

Turtwig was a little green turtle Pokémon with a sprout on its head. Its shell was made of soil, and the little sprout soaked up sunshine all day long.

When Turtwig was thirsty, its sprout drooped. Droop. So Turtwig walked down to the pond for a drink. Sip, sip, sip. And as soon as it had enough water, its sprout perked right back up again! The other Pokémon always knew when Turtwig needed a drink. "Your sprout is drooping, Turtwig!" they said, and they walked with it to the pond.

Grotle had little bushes growing on its shell, and it lived in forests near clean, fresh water. It always knew where the best springs were.

When the little forest Pokémon were thirsty, they climbed onto Grotle's back. Then Grotle walked slowly through the woods, step by step, until it reached its secret spring, where the water bubbled up cold and clear. Everyone hopped off and drank. "Ahh!" Then they rode home again on Grotle's leafy back.

Torterra was a giant turtle Pokémon with a whole tree growing on its back. It moved so slowly through the forest that little Pokémon built their nests right in its branches.

Pidgey nested in the tree. Squirrel Pokémon played in the leaves. Caterpie munched on its twigs. Torterra didn't mind at all. It walked slowly from forest to forest, carrying its little home full of friends. Long ago, people imagined that the whole world rested on the back of a giant Torterra. Maybe it does.

Chimchar was a little orange monkey Pokémon with a flame on its tail. The flame was so strong that even the rain couldn't put it out!

Chimchar was very quick, and it loved to climb. It scampered up trees and cliffs, swinging from branch to branch. Whoosh! On rainy days, when everyone else was cold and wet, Chimchar's little flame kept burning bright. So all its friends huddled close to it under a big tree, warming their paws until the rain stopped.

Monferno was a quick, clever Pokémon with a fiery tail. It could jump from walls to ceilings and bounce around a room like a rubber ball. Boing, boing, boing!

Monferno loved to play tag in the old barn. It jumped from the hay bales to the rafters to the windowsill. Nobody could catch it! Its friends laughed and chased it round and round. When they were finally too tired to run, Monferno came down, sat in the middle of them and let them tag it. "You got me!" it said, grinning.

Infernape was a fiery Pokémon with a crown of flames on its head. It was so quick and so nimble that it could do flips and cartwheels faster than you could blink.

Infernape was the star of the village festival. It did backflips and spins and leaps, and its flames swirled around it like ribbons of light. Whoosh, flip, spin! The crowd gasped and cheered. At the end of the show, Infernape bowed, and its crown of flames glowed brighter than ever.

Piplup was a little blue penguin Pokémon, and it was very, very proud. It liked to do things by itself, thank you very much, and it held its beak up high.

On land, Piplup sometimes tripped over its own feet. Waddle, waddle, whoops! It got up quickly and pretended nothing had happened. "I meant to do that," it said. But in the water, Piplup was amazing. It zoomed and twirled and dove like a little blue rocket. "See?" it said proudly. And everyone agreed that it was the best swimmer of all.

Prinplup was a proud penguin Pokémon who liked to be on its own. It swam in the icy sea, looking for adventures, and it didn't like to follow anyone.

But one day, a little Piplup got lost in the waves. Prinplup heard it crying. It didn't hesitate for one second. It zoomed through the water, scooped up the little Piplup and carried it back to shore. "Thank you," said the Piplup. Prinplup puffed up its chest. "Of course," it said. "That's what big penguins do."

Empoleon was a tall, proud penguin Pokémon with three golden horns on its head, like a crown. It was the emperor of the icy sea.

Empoleon could swim as fast as a speedboat, cutting through the waves. Whoosh! But it never showed off. It was a wise and fair ruler. When the young Piplup argued, Empoleon listened to both sides and helped them make up. "An emperor," it said, "must be kind." And all the penguins in the icy sea looked up to it.

Starly was a tiny bird Pokémon that lived in big flocks. One Starly alone was small and quiet. But when the whole flock flew together, they made a lot of noise! Chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp!

Every morning, the Starly flock woke up the whole valley with their chirping. The farmers yawned and got out of bed. The flowers opened their petals. Even the sleepy Bidoof opened one eye. "Good morning, Starly," everyone grumbled. And the Starly chirped back even louder. Chirp, chirp, CHIRP!

Staravia lived in big flocks with lots of other Staravia. They flew together in great swirling shapes, like smoke dancing in the sky.

When the Staravia flock flew over the town, the children ran out to watch. The birds swooped left, then right, then up, then down, all at the same time, as if they were one big bird. "How do they know where to go?" asked a little boy. His grandpa smiled. "They follow each other," he said. "Just like good friends."

Staraptor was a strong, brave bird Pokémon with a big crest on its head. Its wings were so strong that it could carry things much bigger than itself.

When the mountain village needed medicine from the town far below, Staraptor flew it up. When the fishermen's nets got tangled on a rock, Staraptor flew down and pulled them free. Staraptor was never scared, not even of storms. "Staraptor will help," the villagers always said. And it always did.

Bidoof was a plump brown Pokémon with big front teeth and a very calm personality. Nothing ever bothered Bidoof. Rain? Fine. Wind? Fine. A Pidgey sitting on its head? Also fine.

Bidoof liked to gnaw on logs and rocks to keep its teeth from growing too long. Gnaw, gnaw, gnaw. It wandered along the riverbanks, munching and smiling. The other Pokémon thought Bidoof was a little bit silly. But when they were upset, they always went to sit with Bidoof, because somehow, sitting next to Bidoof made everything feel calm.

Bibarel was a busy builder Pokémon. It used its big teeth to chew through branches, and its flat tail to pat mud into place. It built dams across the river.

Bibarel worked all day long. Chew, carry, pat. Chew, carry, pat. Behind its dam, the water made a calm, quiet pond, perfect for swimming. The little Pokémon came to splash in it every afternoon. "Thank you for the pond, Bibarel!" they shouted. Bibarel nodded, patted one more stick into place and went back to work.

Kricketot was a little red bug Pokémon with antennae that clacked together when it moved. Clack, clack, clack! It sounded just like a tiny xylophone.

Kricketot loved making music. It shook its head, and its antennae went clackety-clack. It wiggled its body, and they went clickety-click. At night, when lots of Kricketot gathered in the fields, they made a little clacking orchestra. The children fell asleep listening to it, clack, clack, clickety-clack, like a lullaby.

Kricketune was a bug Pokémon with long arms like violin bows. It rubbed them together to play beautiful music. Each Kricketune played its own special song to show how it was feeling.

A happy song was quick and bouncy. A sad song was slow and soft. And a good night song was gentle and sweet. On summer evenings, the Kricketune played together in the meadow, and their music drifted through the open windows of the town. Close your eyes and listen. Can you hear the Kricketune playing good night?

Shinx was a little blue lion cub Pokémon with a spiky mane. When Shinx was in danger, its fur glowed with a bright light, so it could see where to run.

Shinx was a bit shy, and it didn't like the dark very much. But it had learned a trick. When the night got too dark, Shinx made its fur glow, just a little. Now it had its own night-light! The other little Pokémon who were scared of the dark curled up next to it. And they all slept soundly in Shinx's soft blue glow.

Luxio was a blue Pokémon with a black mane and sharp claws that crackled with electricity. It lived in groups, and the group always looked out for one another.

Luxio and its friends touched their tails together to share electricity. Zap! When one Luxio was tired and low on energy, the others shared some of theirs. Zap, zap! Soon the tired Luxio was crackling and ready to play again. "Thanks, friends!" it said. That's what friends are for: sharing what you have.

Luxray was a big, strong lion Pokémon with golden eyes, and those eyes could see through walls! It could see what was on the other side of anything.

Luxray used its amazing eyes to find lost things. A lost toy under the bed? Luxray saw it. A lost key in the garden? Luxray saw it. A little Pichu hiding inside a hollow log? Luxray saw it, and smiled. "Found you!" it said. Pichu giggled. Nobody could ever win at hide-and-seek against Luxray.

Budew was a little green Pokémon with a flower bud on its head, wrapped up tight. All winter long, the bud stayed closed, keeping warm.

When spring came and the sun got warmer, Budew's bud started to open, little by little. It peeked out at the blue sky and the green grass. "Is it spring?" it asked. A Starly chirped, "Yes!" So Budew opened all the way, and a sweet smell filled the air. Every year, Budew was the first to say hello to spring.

Roserade was a graceful Pokémon with bouquets of roses for hands, one red and one blue. It moved like a dancer, and it smelled like a garden full of flowers.

At the town's spring festival, Roserade danced in the square. It twirled and spun, and its roses filled the air with a sweet perfume. Petals floated down like confetti. Everyone breathed in the lovely smell and smiled. Then Roserade gave each child a single rose petal to take home. They put them under their pillows and dreamed of gardens.

Cranidos was an ancient Pokémon with a very, very hard head. It lived long, long ago in the jungle, and it said hello to everyone by bonking them gently with its head. Bonk!

When scientists brought Cranidos back from a fossil, it bonked everything. It bonked the door. It bonked the table. It bonked the scientist's hat right off his head. "Ow! Okay, hello to you too," he laughed. Now Cranidos lives in the museum, where a big soft pillow hangs by the door, just for bonking.

Rampardos was an ancient Pokémon with the hardest head of all. Its head was thick and strong, so it never got a headache, no matter how much it bonked things.

One winter, the lake froze over, and the fish Pokémon couldn't get any fresh air. Rampardos marched onto the ice, lowered its head and, BONK! The ice cracked open. BONK! BONK! It made holes all across the lake. The fish popped up their heads and took big breaths. "Thank you, Rampardos!" Rampardos rubbed its head. It didn't even hurt.

Shieldon was an ancient Pokémon with a face like a big shield. Long, long ago, it lived in the jungle, eating soft grass and berries.

Shieldon was very gentle. It didn't like trouble, so when something scary happened, it just turned around and faced it with its shield. Bonk! Nothing could get past. Then it went back to eating grass, munch, munch, as if nothing had happened. Its friends always hid behind Shieldon when they were scared. It was the safest place in the whole jungle.

Bastiodon had a face like a giant wall, flat and strong. Nothing could knock it over. And Bastiodon used its strength for one important thing: protecting the little ones.

When a storm came, the Bastiodon lined up side by side, making a big, strong wall. All the little Shieldon hid behind them, safe and sound. The wind howled and the rain poured, but the Bastiodon didn't move an inch. When the storm was over, the little ones peeked out. "Is it over?" "It's over," said Bastiodon. "Go and play."

Burmy was a little bug Pokémon that made itself a cozy cloak out of whatever it could find. If it lived in the forest, its cloak was made of leaves. If it lived on the beach, its cloak was made of sand.

One day, a Burmy got caught in a windstorm and lost its leafy cloak. Oh no! It shivered. But then it found some colorful paper scraps in the town. It stuck them together and made a brand-new cloak, all bright and patchy. Burmy looked at itself and smiled. It was the most colorful Burmy in the world.

Wormadam was a Pokémon that wore a cloak, just like when it was a Burmy. But now the cloak had become part of its body, and it would wear it forever.

Wormadam's cloak was made of leaves, and it rustled softly when it moved. Rustle, rustle. It hung from a branch and swayed in the breeze. The little Pokémon liked to hide in Wormadam's leafy cloak when it rained, giggling as the raindrops pattered on the leaves. Wormadam liked that. Its cloak was cozy for everyone.

Mothim was a moth Pokémon with orange wings, and it loved sweet honey more than anything in the whole world. It fluttered around at night, following its nose to anything sweet.

One night, Mothim smelled something wonderful coming from a kitchen window. Sniff, sniff! It was a honey cake, cooling on the table. Mothim fluttered in and landed right next to it. The little girl who had baked it saw Mothim and laughed. "Do you want a taste?" she asked. Mothim's wings fluttered with joy.

Combee was three little bee Pokémon stuck together. They buzzed around the flowers all day, gathering sweet nectar to bring back to their hive. Bzzz, bzzz, bzzz!

The three Combee always worked together. One looked for flowers, one sniffed for nectar, and one carried it home. Bzzz! "This way!" "Smells sweet!" "Got it!" At the end of the day, they flew back to the hive, tired but happy, to give their nectar to their queen.

Vespiquen was the queen of the Combee. Its body was like a hive, and the little Combee lived inside it, all snug and safe.

Vespiquen took care of all the Combee. When they came home with nectar, Vespiquen thanked each one. "Well done," it buzzed softly. It gave them sweet honey to eat and made sure everyone had a warm place to sleep. The Combee loved their queen, and the hive was always full of gentle humming. Hmmmmm.

Pachirisu was a little white squirrel Pokémon with a big fluffy tail and electric cheeks. It loved to make balls of fur filled with electricity, and it hid them all over the forest.

Pachirisu was very generous. When it found a friend who was feeling tired, it gave them one of its electric fur balls. Zap! The friend felt full of energy again. Sometimes, Pachirisu forgot where it had hidden its fur balls. But that was okay. The other forest Pokémon found them and remembered how kind Pachirisu was.

Buizel was an orange weasel Pokémon with a floaty ring around its neck, like a little life jacket. It loved swimming more than anything.

Buizel had two tails, and when it swam, it spun them around like a propeller. Whirr! It zoomed through the water so fast that it left a wake behind it, like a little motorboat. The children at the lake raced it from the dock. Ready, set, go! Splash! Buizel always won, but it always waited at the finish line to splash them hello.

Floatzel was a big, friendly swimming Pokémon with a floaty ring around its neck. It could puff up its ring like a raft, and anyone could hold onto it in the water.

Floatzel was the lifeguard of the beach. Whenever someone got tired while swimming, Floatzel zoomed over and puffed up its ring. "Hold on!" it called. And it carried them safely back to shore. The children always felt safe swimming when Floatzel was around. It never let anyone get into trouble.

Cherubi was a little Pokémon that looked like two cherries on a stem. One cherry was big, with a face, and the other was small and full of good things to eat.

The little cherry held all of Cherubi's energy. Cherubi kept it safe and close. When Cherubi needed a boost, it nibbled on the energy in the little cherry. Then it felt strong enough to hop around the garden all day long. Hop, hop, hop! It was like carrying a snack wherever you go.

Cherrim was a little flower Pokémon that changed when the sun came out. On cloudy days, it kept its petals closed tight, like a shy purple bud.

But when the sun came out, Cherrim opened its petals wide and turned into a bright pink flower with a big happy smile! It danced around the garden, cheerful and sunny. When the clouds came back, it closed up again and waited patiently. So whenever the sun comes out, think of Cherrim, opening up and dancing in the light.

Shellos was a soft, squishy sea slug Pokémon that lived by the sea. And here's something funny: Shellos that lived on one side of the sea were pink, and Shellos that lived on the other side were blue!

Nobody knew exactly why they were different colors. One day, a pink Shellos and a blue Shellos met on the beach. They looked at each other for a long time. "You're blue," said the pink one. "You're pink," said the blue one. Then they both laughed and became best friends. Pink and blue, squishy and happy.

Gastrodon was a big, squishy sea slug Pokémon that lived in shallow water near the shore. Like Shellos, some Gastrodon were pink and some were blue, depending on where they lived.

Gastrodon moved very slowly, sliding along the sand. Slide, slide, slide. The little Shellos followed behind it in a line, like ducklings. When the tide came in, Gastrodon floated gently in the warm water, and the little ones climbed onto its back. They bobbed on the waves together, squishy and happy.

Ambipom was a purple monkey Pokémon with two long tails, and at the end of each tail was a hand. With two tail-hands, Ambipom could do twice as many things!

Ambipom loved to juggle. It tossed berries up with one tail and caught them with the other. Toss, catch, toss, catch! Then it used its real hands too, and suddenly there were berries flying everywhere. The children clapped and cheered. "More, Ambipom, more!" At the end, Ambipom caught every berry and shared them with the crowd.

Drifloon was a little purple balloon Pokémon with a puffy body and a yellow cross on its face. It floated gently on the breeze, drifting wherever the wind took it.

Drifloon liked to float near playgrounds, where children were playing. It bobbed above the swings and the slides, watching them. Sometimes a child held onto Drifloon's little string arms, and Drifloon lifted them up, just a few inches, before setting them gently back down. "Again!" they giggled. And Drifloon bobbed happily in the wind.

Drifblim was a big purple balloon Pokémon that floated through the sky at dusk. It could carry passengers, and it drifted so slowly and smoothly that nobody ever felt scared.

When the sun was setting, Drifblim floated over the town, and anyone who wanted to could hold onto its long arms and go for a ride. Up, up, over the rooftops, past the clock tower, along the river. The sky was orange and pink. Then Drifblim brought everyone home, gently, just in time for dinner.

Buneary was a little brown bunny Pokémon with long, fluffy ears. When it was cold or scared, it rolled its ears up into soft little balls, like earmuffs.

Buneary was a bit shy. When someone new came along, it rolled up its ears and peeked out from behind a bush. But once Buneary knew you were a friend, it unrolled its ears and hopped right over, boing, boing, boing, to say hello. And if you were very lucky, it would let you stroke its soft, fluffy ears.

Lopunny was an elegant rabbit Pokémon with long, soft ears and fluffy fur. It took great care of its fur, brushing it every morning until it shone.

Lopunny was also very careful. It always listened with its long ears before hopping anywhere new. When it was sure everything was safe, it hopped so high and so gracefully that it looked like it was flying. Boing! The little Buneary watched in awe and tried to copy it. Boing, bump, boing, bump. "Keep practicing," said Lopunny kindly.

When Misdreavus touched a dark Dusk Stone, it became Mismagius, a ghost Pokémon with a big floppy hat, like a witch. It liked to chant little songs that sounded like magic spells.

Mismagius's spells were mostly harmless. One made the flowers bloom. One made the birds sing. And one, its favorite, made everybody who heard it feel happy for the rest of the day. "Abra-cadabra-mismagius!" it chanted, and the children laughed and twirled in the meadow. Was it real magic? Nobody knew. But everybody felt happy.

Honchkrow was a big black bird Pokémon with a fancy feathered hat and a fluffy white collar. It was the boss of all the Murkrow, and it acted very important.

Every evening, Honchkrow called the Murkrow together with a deep caw. Caw! "Report, everyone!" And the Murkrow told it about their day. "I found a shiny button!" "I saw a rainbow!" "I made a new friend!" Honchkrow listened carefully to every story. It looked very serious. But secretly, it loved hearing about their days.

Glameow was a gray kitten Pokémon with a curly tail. It liked to be petted, but only when it wanted to be. If it didn't feel like it, it walked away with its nose in the air. Hmph!

When Glameow was happy, it purred and swished its curly tail. Purr, purr. Once, it sat on a little boy's lap for a whole afternoon, purring, while he read a book. The boy didn't dare move. He didn't want Glameow to leave. And when the book was finished, Glameow stretched, yawned and gave him a little head bump. Thank you.

Purugly was a big, round cat Pokémon. It wrapped its tail around its waist, like a belt, to make itself look even bigger.

Purugly liked to find the coziest spot in the house and take it over. The sunny windowsill? Purugly's. The softest pillow? Purugly's. The warm spot by the fireplace? Purugly's too! The family laughed. "You can't have every spot, Purugly!" But Purugly just stretched out and purred, as if to say, "Watch me."

Chingling was a tiny round Pokémon with a little bell inside its mouth. Every time it hopped, the bell went ring, ring, ring!

Chingling hopped everywhere it went. Hop, ring! Hop, ring! The other Pokémon always knew when Chingling was coming. "Here comes Chingling!" they said, hearing the bell. When Chingling wanted to say hello, it hopped extra high. Ring-a-ling! And when it was time for sleep, it stopped hopping, and the forest went quiet. Shh.

Stunky was a little purple skunk Pokémon with a fluffy tail. When it was scared, it lifted its tail and made a very, very stinky smell. Pee-yew!

Stunky didn't want to be stinky all the time. It just wanted to make friends. So it practiced being calm, and it learned to stay brave instead of getting scared. Now, when it meets someone new, it waves its fluffy tail hello, and nobody has to hold their nose. Well, most of the time.

Skuntank was a big skunk Pokémon with a fluffy tail that it could curl up over its head. It could squirt its stinky smell from the tip of its tail, a long, long way.

Skuntank was proud of its smell. It was the stinkiest Pokémon in the forest! "Nobody bothers me," it said. But Skuntank was also a bit lonely. So one day, it tried something new: it took a bath in a pond full of flowers. When it came out, it smelled just a little bit like roses. Its friends came closer. "Hey, Skuntank," they said. "You smell nice today!"

Bronzor was a round, flat Pokémon that looked like an ancient bronze mirror. People found it buried in very old places, where it had been resting for a long, long time.

Bronzor's back was shiny and smooth, like a mirror. When the sunlight hit it, it flashed and sparkled. The children liked to look at their reflections in it. "Look, I'm upside down!" "Look, I'm wobbly!" Bronzor spun slowly in the air so they could see themselves from all sides. It was the funniest mirror in town.

Bronzong was a big bronze Pokémon shaped like a bell. Long, long ago, people believed that Bronzong could bring rain to dry fields.

When the farmers' crops were thirsty, they visited the old temple where Bronzong stayed. Bronzong rang softly. Gong, gong, gong. And sure enough, a few days later, the rain clouds came, and the fields got a nice long drink. The farmers bowed and thanked Bronzong. It rang once more, very quietly. Gong.

Bonsly looked like a tiny little tree in a pot. It liked to pretend to be a plant, standing very still. But it wasn't a plant at all. It was a little rock Pokémon!

Bonsly had a funny habit: it cried little tears, but the tears weren't sad ones. They kept it from drying out. Sniff, sniff. "Why are you crying, little tree?" asked a girl. Bonsly blinked. Then it ran away, giggling, on its tiny legs. The girl was so surprised that she sat down on the grass and laughed and laughed.

Mime Jr. was a little Pokémon that copied everything it saw. If you waved, it waved. If you jumped, it jumped. If you made a silly face, it made a silly face right back!

Mime Jr. loved playing copycat with the children. One boy hopped on one foot. Mime Jr. hopped on one foot. The boy patted his head and rubbed his tummy. Mime Jr. did it too! Then the boy yawned a big, sleepy yawn. Mime Jr. yawned too. Yaaawn. And they both laughed, because now they were both very sleepy.

Happiny was a tiny pink Pokémon that carried a round white stone in a pouch on its tummy. It took very good care of the stone, as if it were a precious egg.

Happiny wanted to be just like Chansey when it grew up. So it practiced. It gave its stone a little pat. It said, "There, there," to the flowers. It gave hugs to all its friends. "You're going to be a wonderful Chansey someday," said the old Chansey at the clinic. Happiny beamed. It hugged its stone and gave the old Chansey a hug too.

Chatot was a colorful bird Pokémon with a head shaped like a musical note. It could copy the sounds it heard, especially people talking.

Chatot learned words and repeated them. "Hello!" "Good morning!" "Who wants a cookie?" The children taught it all kinds of things. Then they taught it a song, and Chatot sang it over and over until everyone in the house knew the words. Now, when the family wakes up, Chatot sings them a good-morning song. "Wake up, wake up, the sun is up!"

Spiritomb was a mysterious Pokémon that lived inside a crack in an old stone. It swirled around like purple smoke, with a funny green face.

Long ago, it was tied to that little stone, and it stayed there, very still, for hundreds of years. One day, a curious girl found the stone in the woods and polished it until it was shiny. Out came Spiritomb, swirling and blinking. It had never seen the sun so bright! "Thank you," it whispered. And it swirled around her once, like a happy little breeze.

Gible was a little blue dragon Pokémon with a big mouth and a fin on its back. It liked warm, cozy places, and it made its home in little holes in warm cave walls.

Gible loved snuggling into its cozy hole and peeking out. Peek! When it saw something interesting, it jumped out and chomped at it. Chomp! It chomped leaves, it chomped sticks and once it chomped its own tail by mistake. "Ow!" Gible looked at its tail. Then it looked at its friends, who were laughing. And it laughed too.

Gabite was a dragon Pokémon with sharp claws and fins on its arms. It loved shiny things, and it dug up sparkly gems and stones to keep in its cave.

Every so often, Gabite's old scales fell off and new ones grew in. The old scales were shiny, and people thought they brought good luck. The children in the village searched the hills for Gabite scales, and when they found one, they kept it as a treasure. "I found a lucky scale!" they shouted. And somewhere in its cave, Gabite smiled.

Garchomp was a big dragon Pokémon with fins on its arms and a fin on its back. When it folded its arms and flew, it was as fast as a jet plane. ZOOOOM!

Garchomp could fly from one end of the land to the other before lunch. It loved racing the wind. When the children saw a dark shape zoom across the sky, they shouted, "There goes Garchomp!" But by the time they finished shouting, it was already gone, zooming over the mountains, the sea and the clouds, just for fun.

Munchlax was a little blue Pokémon that grows up into Snorlax, and it was always, always hungry. It ate so much food that it hid snacks in its long fur, for later.

The trouble was, Munchlax often forgot about the snacks it had hidden. So when it went to bed, it found a berry in its fur. "Oh!" Munch. Then a cookie. "Oh!" Munch. Then a whole apple. "OH!" Munch, munch. By the time it found all its hidden snacks, it was too full to stay awake. Zzz.

Riolu was a little blue Pokémon that could see feelings. Everyone has an invisible glow around them, called an aura, and Riolu could see it.

When someone was happy, Riolu saw a bright, warm glow. When someone was sad, the glow was dim and blue. Riolu always knew when its friends needed cheering up. "You look sad," it said to a Starly one day. "How did you know?" asked the Starly. Riolu just smiled and sat beside it until the glow turned warm and bright again.

Lucario was a tall, brave Pokémon that could read the aura of everything around it. With its eyes closed, it could feel where everyone was and what they were feeling.

Lucario was loyal to its friends and always tried to do the right thing. When a little boy lost his Growlithe in the woods, Lucario closed its eyes and felt for the Growlithe's aura. Hmm... there! Far away, under a big tree. Lucario ran through the woods and found the little Growlithe, scared but safe. The boy hugged them both.

Hippopotas was a little hippo Pokémon that lived in the dry desert. It covered itself in sand to keep from getting too hot or too dry.

Hippopotas didn't like getting wet. When it rained, it buried itself in sand to stay dry. Dig, dig, dig! Only its little eyes peeked out. The other Pokémon laughed. "Hippopotas, don't hippos love water?" Hippopotas blinked. "Not me," it said. "I'm a sand hippo." And it went back to its sandy nap.

Hippowdon was a big, strong hippo Pokémon. It could blow out huge clouds of sand from little holes in its body. Whoosh!

When Hippowdon yawned, it yawned so big that a little sandstorm swirled up around it. Yaaawn, whoosh! The desert Pokémon covered their eyes and giggled. "Hippowdon, cover your mouth!" Hippowdon tried, but its mouth was very big. So now, when Hippowdon gets sleepy, everyone runs for cover, laughing.

Skorupi was a little purple Pokémon with claws and a curled tail. It liked to bury itself in the sand and wait very patiently.

Skorupi could stay buried for days without moving. It listened to the footsteps above it. Tap, tap, tap. One day, a little Hippopotas sat right down on top of it! Skorupi wiggled. Hippopotas jumped up. "Who's there?" Skorupi popped out of the sand. "Me!" They both laughed, and from then on, they always napped in the sand together.

Drapion was a big purple Pokémon with strong arms and claws. It was so strong that it could lift a car! But Drapion was gentle with its friends.

Drapion lived in the desert, and it liked to help travelers. When a cart got stuck in the sand, Drapion lifted it out. Heave! When a tent blew over, Drapion held it down while it was fixed. The travelers thanked it and shared their water. Drapion clicked its claws happily. Click, click! It liked being helpful.

Croagunk was a little blue frog Pokémon with big cheeks. When it puffed them out, it made a deep, funny croaking sound. "Croa-GUNK!"

Croagunk liked to croak at everything. It croaked at the morning sun. It croaked at the rain. It croaked at its own reflection in the pond. Croa-GUNK! The other frogs joined in, and soon the whole swamp was croaking together, a big, funny, bouncy song. The children on the bridge laughed and croaked back.

Toxicroak was a big frog Pokémon that lived in the swamp. When it croaked, its throat puffed up, and the sound boomed across the water. CROAK!

Toxicroak was the leader of the swamp choir. Every evening, it croaked the first note, and all the other frogs followed. Croak, ribbit, croak, ribbit! The music echoed through the swamp until the moon came up. Then Toxicroak croaked one last, low note, and everyone settled down to sleep on their lily pads.

Carnivine was a green plant Pokémon with a big mouth and long vines. It liked to hang from tree branches in the swamp, swinging back and forth. Swing, swing!

Carnivine's mouth smelled sweet, like nectar. Bug Pokémon flew close to sniff it, and Carnivine just smiled and swung away. It was too busy swinging to bother anyone. Its favorite game was swinging from tree to tree, using its vines like ropes. Whee! It swung all the way across the swamp and back again before dinner.

Finneon was a little blue fish Pokémon with fins shaped like butterfly wings. At night, the pink markings on its fins glowed softly in the dark water.

When the sun went down, the Finneon gathered near the surface of the sea. Their fins glowed and fluttered, and the water looked like it was full of floating lanterns. The children on the beach waded into the shallow water to see them. "They look like underwater butterflies!" they whispered. And the Finneon swam in circles around their feet.

Lumineon lived deep down at the bottom of the sea, where the sunlight couldn't reach. Its long fins glowed with soft light, like stars in the dark.

Lumineon used its glowing fins to light up the deep sea. It swam slowly along the sea floor, and everywhere it went, little lights followed. The deep-sea Pokémon loved Lumineon. "Here comes the lantern fish," they said. And they followed its glow, looking for treasures in the sand.

Mantyke was a little blue Pokémon that would grow up into Mantine. It swam in the warm sea, and the pattern on its back was different depending on where it lived.

Mantyke loved to swim with the Remoraid. They swam together everywhere, in and out of the coral, laughing and playing. When Mantyke leaped out of the water, splash, the Remoraid leaped too! "Let's go to the big waves!" said Mantyke. And off they went, swimming side by side.

Snover was a little snowy Pokémon that looked like a tiny frosted tree. It lived high in the snowy mountains, and when spring came, round berries grew around its tummy.

The berries looked like little scoops of ice cream. Snover was proud of them. "Would you like a berry?" it asked its friends. They took one each. Crunch! The berries were cold and sweet, like a frosty treat. Snover smiled. When winter came again, it went back up the mountain, and the berries waited until next spring.

Abomasnow was a giant snowy Pokémon that looked like a big tree covered in snow. When it shook its arms, it made a flurry of sparkly snowflakes. Whoosh!

Abomasnow lived on the snowy mountaintop, where it was quiet and peaceful. When the children in the village wished for snow, they looked up at the mountain. "Please, Abomasnow!" they called. And sometimes, if they called nicely, a soft snow began to fall the very next morning. Perfect for sledding.

Weavile was a clever, quick Pokémon that lived in snowy forests. It had sharp claws, and it used them to carve little pictures into tree trunks and ice.

The Weavile used the pictures to leave messages for each other. A carving of a berry meant "Food is this way!" A carving of a moon meant "Let's meet tonight!" And a carving of a smiley face meant "Hello, friend." When the children went walking in the snowy woods, they found Weavile pictures everywhere, and they tried to guess what they meant.

Magnezone was a big metal Pokémon that floated in the air, humming. It had three magnets and a big antenna on top, and it looked a little bit like a flying saucer.

Magnezone's antenna could pick up signals from all around. Sometimes it picked up music from the radio, and it hummed along. Hmm-hmm-hmm! Sometimes it picked up messages from far away, beeping and buzzing. Magnezone liked to float above the town at night, listening to the whole world. The children waved at it from their windows. Beep, beep, it said. Good night.

Lickilicky was a big pink Pokémon with a very, very long tongue. Its tongue could stretch and wrap around anything, and Lickilicky used it like an extra hand.

Lickilicky used its tongue to pick fruit from the tallest trees. It used it to tie its shoes. It even used it to wave goodbye. Slurp, wave! The children loved Lickilicky. But they always said, "No licking, please!" And Lickilicky always tried. But sometimes, just sometimes, it gave them a big, slurpy kiss on the cheek. "Eww!" they shrieked, giggling.

Rhyperior was a huge Pokémon covered in hard rock armor, with a drill on its nose. It was so strong and tough that nothing could knock it over.

Rhyperior worked at the quarry, carrying big stones to build houses. Thud, thud, thud. It carried stones for the new school, stones for the bridge and stones for the playground wall. When the children came to the new school on the first day, they found a big rock by the door with a heart carved into it. Nobody knew who had made it. But Rhyperior knew.

Tangrowth was a big Pokémon made of blue vines, with two long vine arms that could stretch out very far. If a vine broke, a new one grew right back.

Tangrowth loved to help the gardeners. It reached up with its long vine arms and pulled down apples from the very tops of trees. It reached across the river and passed baskets to the other side. "Thank you, Tangrowth!" said the gardeners. Tangrowth wiggled its vines happily. It liked being useful, and it liked giving hugs. Its vines made the best hugs.

Electivire was a big, strong electric Pokémon with two long tails. It used its tails to send out huge amounts of electricity. Bzzzzzt!

When the town's power went out on a stormy night, everyone gathered in the dark. Then they heard a crackle and a buzz. Electivire was standing by the power station, holding the cables in its tails, sending its electricity through the wires. Bzzzt! The lights came back on, one street at a time. The whole town cheered, and Electivire gave a big, buzzing grin.

Magmortar was a big fire Pokémon with arms shaped like cannons. It could send out bright, warm balls of fire, and its body was always very, very hot.

On the coldest night of winter, the village held a festival of lights. Magmortar came down from the volcano and stood in the middle of the square. It pointed its arms up at the sky and sent up bright, warm sparks. Pop! Pop! Pop! The sparks lit up the sky like fireworks. Everyone oohed and aahed, warming their hands by Magmortar's glow.

Togekiss was a beautiful white Pokémon that looked like a flying angel. People said it only appeared where people were kind to each other and treated one another well.

When a village was full of kindness, Togekiss came to visit. It flew over the rooftops, sprinkling blessings like soft glitter. Sparkle, sparkle. The people looked up and smiled. "Togekiss is here!" they said. "We must be doing something right." And they tried to be even kinder, so Togekiss would stay.

Yanmega was a big dragonfly Pokémon with four wings and big red eyes. It could fly so fast and so strong that it could even carry a person through the air!

When the children at the lake wanted to see what the world looked like from above, Yanmega gave them rides, one at a time. Bzzzz! It flew over the water, over the trees and over the hill. The children held on tight and shouted, "Wheee!" Then Yanmega landed softly on the grass, and the next child climbed on.

When Eevee touched a green Leaf Stone, it became Leafeon, a Pokémon covered in leaves, with a leaf for a tail. Leafeon loved the sunshine, just like a plant.

Leafeon soaked up the sun every day, and wherever it went, the air smelled fresh and clean, like a forest after the rain. When the town got smoky and stuffy, Leafeon walked through the streets, breathing in the stuffy air and breathing out clean, fresh air. Sniff! "It smells like a forest!" the people said, smiling.

When Eevee touched a sparkling Ice Stone, it became Glaceon, a beautiful blue Pokémon that could make snow and ice. Its fur could freeze into sparkly icicles.

On hot summer days, Glaceon was everyone's favorite friend. It breathed out a cool, frosty breeze, and the hot air turned fresh and chilly. Ahh! It made little ice cubes for drinks and tiny snowflakes for fun. The children followed Glaceon around the park all afternoon. "Glaceon, make it snow!" And Glaceon made a little flurry, just for them.

Gliscor was a purple Pokémon with big wings that let it glide silently through the night. It liked to hang upside down from tree branches, holding on with its tail.

During the day, Gliscor slept upside down, swaying in the breeze. Swing, swing. At night, it woke up and glided through the moonlight, making big loops in the sky. Whoosh! The night Pokémon liked to watch it. And in the morning, Gliscor hung itself back up on its branch, wrapped its wings around itself and said, "Good night," even though it was morning.

Mamoswine was a giant, hairy Pokémon with long, curved tusks made of ice. It had lived in the frozen north since ancient times, and its thick fur kept it warm in the snow.

Mamoswine walked slowly through the snowfields, and its big feet made a path through the deep snow. Crunch, crunch, crunch. The little Swinub followed behind, walking right in its footprints. "Mamoswine makes the best paths," they said. And when they got tired, they rode on its big furry back, all the way home.

Porygon-Z was Porygon2 with an extra-special upgrade. But something about the upgrade was a little bit funny, and now Porygon-Z acted very silly!

Porygon-Z wiggled its head. It twitched its arms. It did a little dance in the middle of the street for no reason at all. Beep, boop, wiggle! Its friends didn't know what it would do next. Would it sing? Would it spin? Would it do a backflip? Nobody knew, not even Porygon-Z. But everyone agreed that it was the most fun Pokémon to be around.

When Kirlia touched a shiny Dawn Stone, it became Gallade, a tall, noble Pokémon with long blades on its elbows. Gallade was polite and brave, like a knight from a fairy tale.

Gallade believed in being fair and kind. It always kept its promises, and it always helped anyone who was in trouble. When a little girl's kite blew away, Gallade leaped into the air and caught the string. When an old man dropped his groceries, Gallade picked them up. "Thank you," people said. Gallade bowed politely. "It was my honor."

Probopass was a stone Pokémon with a big red nose and a funny gray mustache. It also had three tiny noses that floated around it, called Mini-Noses!

Probopass could send its little Mini-Noses out to explore. Zip, zip, zip! They floated away in different directions and looked around. Then they came back and told Probopass everything they'd seen. "There's a berry bush that way!" "A puddle over there!" "A Bidoof taking a nap!" Probopass wiggled its mustache. It liked knowing what was going on.

Dusknoir was a big ghost Pokémon with one glowing eye and an antenna on its head. It floated quietly through the night, like a soft, dark cloud.

Dusknoir's job was to keep watch while everyone slept. It floated over the houses, looking in on the sleeping children with its gentle eye. If a child had kicked off their blanket, Dusknoir pulled it back up. If a child was having a bad dream, Dusknoir hummed a low, soothing note until they settled. Hmmmm. And in the morning, it floated away before anyone woke up.

When Snorunt touched a shiny Dawn Stone, it became Froslass, a graceful ghost Pokémon made of ice and snow. It floated through the snowy mountains like a drifting snowflake.

Froslass loved to make snowflakes. Each one was different, with tiny patterns of ice like lace. It blew them softly over the mountain village, and the children ran outside with their tongues out, trying to catch them. "This one has a star in it!" "This one has a heart!" Froslass watched from the trees and smiled. Every snowflake was a little gift.

Rotom was a tiny electric Pokémon with a body made of plasma. And it had a funny trick: it could zip inside machines and make them come alive!

Rotom zipped into the washing machine. Whirr, splash, spin! It zipped into the fridge. Brrrr! It zipped into the fan. Whoosh! It zipped into the lawnmower and mowed the whole garden. Then it zipped into the oven and baked a cake. Well, almost. The family came home and found the house very clean, the grass very short and the cake a little bit lopsided. "Rotom!" they laughed.

Uxie was a tiny legendary Pokémon with a yellow head and two long tails. It was the Being of Knowledge, and it always kept its eyes closed. People said that if you looked into its eyes, you would forget what you were doing.

Uxie lived at the bottom of a quiet lake. People said it gave everyone the gift of remembering things. So when the children studied for a test, they thought of Uxie. "Help me remember," they whispered. And they always remembered a little more than they expected.

Mesprit was a tiny legendary Pokémon with a pink head and two long tails. It was the Being of Emotion, and people said it taught the world how to feel happy and sad, excited and calm.

Mesprit lived in a lake surrounded by tall trees. It flew so fast that it was hard to see, but sometimes people felt it as it passed by: a sudden happy feeling, a giggle, a warm glow in their chest. "Was that Mesprit?" they wondered. Maybe it was. Maybe Mesprit just wanted to say hello.

Azelf was a tiny legendary Pokémon with a blue head and two long tails. It was the Being of Willpower, and people said it gave everyone the courage to keep trying.

Azelf lived in a lake on top of a mountain. When people needed to be brave, they thought of Azelf. When a little boy was scared to ride his bike without training wheels, he took a deep breath and thought, "Azelf, help me be brave." Then he pushed off and pedaled. Wobble, wobble... wheee! He did it! And on top of the mountain, Azelf cheered.

Dialga was a giant legendary Pokémon made of steel and blue crystal. People said it controlled time itself. With every beat of its heart, time moved forward.

Tick, tock, tick, tock. That's the sound of Dialga's heart. It makes the mornings turn into afternoons and the afternoons into evenings. It makes babies grow up and seeds grow into trees. So when you look at a clock and see the hands moving, you can think of Dialga, far away, keeping time for the whole world.

Palkia was a giant legendary Pokémon with pink stripes and shining pearls on its shoulders. People said it controlled space, all the room in the whole universe.

Palkia made sure there was enough space for everything: room for the stars to shine, room for the oceans to stretch and room for every little Pokémon to have a home. When you stretch your arms out wide and feel all the space around you, that's Palkia's gift. Stretch, stretch! There's room for everyone.

Heatran lived deep inside a volcano, in caves full of glowing magma. Its body was made of steel, but it was so hot that it glowed red and orange.

Heatran crawled along the cave walls and ceilings with its special feet, and the rocks grew warm wherever it went. It liked the heat, and it liked the bubbling, glowing magma. When the volcano rumbled, people in the village said, "Heatran is stretching." And sure enough, a little puff of warm smoke rose from the top of the mountain.

Regigigas was a giant legendary Pokémon, bigger than Regirock, Regice and Registeel. People said that long, long ago, it pulled whole lands across the sea with ropes, all by itself.

Regigigas slept for a very long time. When it woke up, it was so slow to get going that it took a whole week to stand up! Creak, creak, stretch. But once it got moving, it was one of the strongest Pokémon in the world. Regirock, Regice and Registeel gathered around it like children around a grandparent, listening to its old stories.

Giratina was a huge legendary Pokémon with shadowy wings. It lived in a strange, upside-down world on the other side of ours, where everything was twisted and quiet.

Giratina could see our world from its side, like looking through a window. Sometimes it watched the children playing, the birds flying and the rivers flowing. It was very curious about our world. So if you ever see your reflection in a still pond and it seems to wink at you, maybe it's Giratina, saying hello from the other side.

Cresselia was a legendary Pokémon shaped like a crescent moon, with shimmering wings like ribbons. It flew through the night sky, sprinkling good dreams.

People said that if you held one of Cresselia's feathers, you would only have happy dreams. So the grandmas in the village sewed little shiny feathers into the children's pillows. "Cresselia will keep the bad dreams away," they said. And the children fell asleep, dreaming of flying, of candy mountains and of warm, sunny beaches.

Phione was a little blue sea Pokémon that drifted along in warm seas, floating wherever the waves took it. It had a little float on top of its head to help it bob along.

Phione always went back to the place where it was born, no matter how far it had drifted. It floated across the whole ocean, past islands and through coral reefs, and then turned around and floated all the way home. "Where have you been?" asked its friends. "Everywhere," said Phione happily. "But home is the best."

Manaphy was a tiny blue Mythical Pokémon, called the Prince of the Sea. It was born in a cold, cold sea, and then it swam far, far away to find warm water.

Manaphy had a special gift: it could feel the hearts of anyone it met. When it saw someone sad, it swam close and touched them with its little antennae. Their sadness melted away, and they felt Manaphy's happy heart instead. "Mana-phy!" it sang. And everyone who met it remembered that warm, sparkly feeling for the rest of their lives.

Darkrai was a shadowy Mythical Pokémon that came out on nights when there was no moon. Long ago, people were afraid of it, because when it was close, they had restless, tossing dreams.

But Darkrai didn't want to give anyone bad dreams. So it kept far away from sleeping people, on a lonely island, watching the stars. One night, Cresselia flew by and saw it there, alone. "You don't have to be lonely," said Cresselia. "I'll bring the good dreams, and you can watch the stars with me." And so they did, the moon and the shadow, side by side.

Shaymin was a tiny hedgehog Pokémon covered in flowers. Wherever it walked, flowers bloomed, and the air smelled sweet.

Shaymin could clean up dirty places. When it found a spot where nothing would grow, it sat down and breathed in the dirty air. Then it breathed out clean air, and the grass came back, and the flowers bloomed. And when special pink flowers called Gracidea bloomed, Shaymin changed into its Sky Forme, grew little wings and flew away to find a new place to help.

Arceus was a Mythical Pokémon, the oldest one of all. People told an old story that before there was anything at all, there was an egg, and from that egg came Arceus. Then Arceus shaped the world.

In the story, Arceus made time, and space, and the land, and the sea. Then all the Pokémon came to be, one by one, and Arceus was very happy with them. After that, it went to sleep, high up beyond the sky. People say Arceus is still up there, watching over all the Pokémon. And maybe it watches over you too, little one. Good night.

Victini was a tiny Mythical Pokémon with big ears shaped like the letter V. It was full of energy, so much energy that it could never run out, and it loved to share it.

When Victini touched someone, they felt a rush of warm, bubbly energy, as if they could do anything. Runners ran faster. Singers sang louder. A little girl who was nervous before her school play held Victini's tiny hand and suddenly felt brave. She walked on stage and said every line perfectly. Afterward, she looked for Victini to say thank you, but it had already zipped away.

Snivy was a little green Pokémon with a leafy tail. It was calm and clever, and it soaked up sunlight through its tail to get energy.

On sunny days, Snivy was quick and full of energy. Zip, zip, zip! On cloudy days, it moved a bit slower. So whenever the sun came out from behind a cloud, Snivy stretched its tail up toward the sky and smiled. "Ahh, that's better." Its friends learned to watch Snivy's tail. When it was up, they knew it was going to be a lovely day.

Servine was a sleek green Pokémon with leaves on its body. It could hide in tall grass so well that nobody could see it, and then it would pop out with a giggle.

Servine liked to play hide-and-seek in the meadow. It hid in the grass and stayed perfectly still. The other Pokémon walked right past it. "Where's Servine?" they wondered. Then, swish! Servine leaped out from the grass, right behind them. "Boo!" Everyone jumped and laughed. Servine was the hide-and-seek champion of the meadow.

Serperior was a long, elegant green Pokémon, like a royal serpent. It held its head high, and it had a calm, wise gaze.

Serperior lived in a sunny garden, and it took in the sunlight through its body and shared the warmth with the plants around it. Wherever Serperior rested, the flowers bloomed brighter. The little garden Pokémon loved to rest in Serperior's coils. "It's like a warm, green hug," they said. And Serperior closed its eyes and smiled.

Tepig was a little orange pig Pokémon with a curly tail. It could blow little puffs of fire out of its nose. Puff, puff!

Tepig loved berries, and it had a special trick: it roasted them before eating them. Puff! A little flame toasted the berry until it was warm and sweet. "Mmm!" Tepig shared its toasted berries with its friends. They all agreed: a warm, toasty berry was the best snack in the world. But Tepig had to be careful not to sneeze, or puff, too many berries got roasted at once!

Pignite was a round, strong Pokémon with a fire inside its tummy. When the fire burned bright, Pignite felt full of energy and moved super fast.

Pignite liked to help out on the farm. It carried heavy bags of grain and pulled the cart to the market. When it was cold, it stood by the barn door and warmed up the whole barn with its glowing tummy. The farm Pokémon gathered around it. "Pignite is the best heater," they said, holding out their paws. Pignite grinned and puffed a happy little smoke ring.

Emboar was a big, strong fire Pokémon with a beard made of flames. It cared deeply about its friends and would do anything to help them.

Emboar was the strongest Pokémon on the mountain, but it was also the kindest. When the little Tepig got cold on winter nights, Emboar sat beside them and let its flaming beard glow warm and gentle. The Tepig snuggled close and fell asleep, toasty and safe. Emboar stayed awake all night, keeping the fire glowing just right.

Oshawott was a little blue otter Pokémon with a shell on its tummy. The shell was called a scalchop, and Oshawott used it for all sorts of things.

It used its scalchop to crack open hard berries. Crack! It used it to dig in the sand. Dig, dig! It used it as a tiny plate for snacks. And it used it to scratch its back. Ahh. But if anybody tried to take its scalchop, Oshawott held it tight. "Mine!" it said. It was Oshawott's favorite thing in the whole world.

Dewott was a blue otter Pokémon with two scalchop shells on its legs. It practiced every day to use them perfectly, twirling them like a juggler.

Dewott was very serious about its practice. Swish, swish, twirl! It practiced in the morning and in the evening. Its friends watched in awe as it spun its scalchops faster and faster. "Teach us, Dewott!" they asked. So Dewott taught them, slowly, step by step. Soon the whole riverbank was full of little Pokémon, twirling seashells and giggling.
