Samurott was a big, noble blue Pokémon with a shell helmet and a long shell sword tucked into its armor. It looked like a knight from long ago.

Samurott was wise and calm. When the young Pokémon of the river argued, Samurott listened to everyone and helped them find a fair answer. "A true warrior," it said, "knows when to be gentle." The little Oshawott looked up to Samurott more than anyone. Someday, they hoped, they would be just as wise.

Patrat was a little brown Pokémon that was always on the lookout. It stood up on its tail, tall and watchful, keeping an eye out for anything new.

Patrat also stored food in its cheeks, just in case. Its cheeks puffed out like balloons, full of seeds and berries. When its friends got hungry, Patrat opened its mouth and, pop, pop, pop, shared its snacks. "How do you fit so much in there?" they asked. Patrat just smiled with its puffy cheeks.

Watchog was a lookout Pokémon with stripes on its body and eyes that could see in the dark. It stood up tall on its tail and watched over its home all night long.

When Watchog saw something interesting, the stripes on its body glowed. Glow, glow! That was its signal. The other Patrat knew what it meant: "Something's happening! Come look!" One night, the stripes glowed bright, and everyone came running. It was a shooting star, falling across the sky. Watchog had wanted everyone to see.

Lillipup was a little brown puppy Pokémon with a fluffy face. The long fur around its face could feel things around it, like whiskers.

Lillipup was brave for its size and very loyal. It followed its family everywhere, wagging its tail. When the little boy went to the park, Lillipup went too. When he went to bed, Lillipup curled up at his feet. And when he had a bad dream, Lillipup licked his cheek until he giggled and fell back asleep. Lillipup was the best puppy in the world.

Herdier was a loyal dog Pokémon with a coat of black fur like a cape. It loved to help on the farm, especially herding the other Pokémon.

When it was time to go home, Herdier ran around the field, gently guiding the Mareep back to the barn. Woof! Woof! "This way, everyone!" The Mareep trotted along in a fluffy line. Herdier never lost a single one. At the end of the day, it lay down by the barn door, tired and happy, and the farmer gave it a big pat on the head.

Stoutland was a big dog Pokémon with long, shaggy fur like a beard. Its fur was so thick and warm that it kept Stoutland cozy even in the snowiest mountains.

Stoutland was a hero of the mountains. When hikers got lost in the snow, Stoutland sniffed them out and found them. Then it lay down beside them and kept them warm with its fluffy fur until help arrived. Many people in the mountains owed their safe trip home to Stoutland, and they always gave it the biggest bone at dinner.

Purrloin was a little purple cat Pokémon with big eyes and a very cute face. It was also a little bit sneaky. When it wanted something, it looked up with its big eyes, and nobody could say no!

Purrloin especially liked fish. When it sat by the kitchen and looked up with its big, sweet eyes, the cook couldn't help but give it a little snack. Then Purrloin sat by the window and looked up at the neighbor. Snack! Then the baker. Snack! By the end of the day, Purrloin had a very full tummy, and everyone in town had been charmed.

Liepard was a sleek purple cat Pokémon with beautiful spots. It moved so quietly and gracefully that you could never hear it coming.

Liepard liked to sit on high walls and watch the town at night. It was very independent. It came and went as it pleased, and it slept wherever it liked. But it had one special friend: a little girl who left a bowl of milk on her windowsill every night. And every night, when she was asleep, Liepard came and drank it, and purred her a quiet song.

Pansage was a green monkey Pokémon with a tuft of leaves on its head. When it met a Pokémon who was tired, it shared one of its leaves.

Pansage's leaves were special. When you nibbled one, all your tiredness went away, and you felt fresh and relaxed. Pansage gave leaves to anyone who needed them: a tired Pidove, a sleepy Patrat, a worn-out farmer. "Here," it said, holding out a leaf. "This will help." Its leaves always grew back, so Pansage never ran out of kindness.

When Pansage touched a Leaf Stone, it became Simisage, with a big leafy tuft on its head and a thorny tail. Simisage had a bit of a temper, but it had a big heart too.

When Simisage got cross, it swished its thorny tail around. Swish! But its friends knew the trick: give Simisage a big leafy salad, and it calmed right down. Munch, munch. "Okay," it said, smiling. "I'm not cross anymore." Then it shared its salad with everyone.

Pansear was a red monkey Pokémon with a tuft of fire on its head. It lived in warm caves near volcanoes, and the tuft on its head was very, very hot.

Pansear used its hot tuft to toast berries. It held a berry near its head, and in just a few seconds, the berry was warm and toasty. Sizzle! Pansear loved to make toasted berries for its friends. They lined up with their berries, and Pansear toasted them one by one. "Who's next?" it asked, and its tuft glowed bright.

When Pansear touched a Fire Stone, it became Simisear, a fiery Pokémon with flames on its head and tail. When it was excited, the flames grew bigger. Whoosh!

Simisear had a sweet tooth. It loved anything sweet: honey, berries, cakes. When it smelled something sweet, its flames flickered with excitement. One day, a baker left a tray of cookies to cool by the window. Simisear's flames went whoosh! But instead of taking them, it knocked on the door. The baker laughed and gave it the warmest cookie of all.

Panpour was a blue monkey Pokémon with a tuft on its head that stored water. The water inside was full of goodness, and it made plants grow big and strong.

When Panpour found a thirsty plant, it leaned over and sprayed water from its tuft. Spritz, spritz! The plant perked right up. Panpour went all around the garden, watering every flower and every vegetable. The gardener smiled. "Thank you, Panpour," she said. "You're the best sprinkler in the world." Panpour bowed, and a few drops of water dripped down its nose.

When Panpour touched a Water Stone, it became Simipour, with a big splashy tuft on its head. It could spray water from its tail, high into the air.

On hot summer days, Simipour stood in the middle of the playground and sprayed water from its tail. Whoosh! The water fell down like a fountain, and the children ran through it, laughing and splashing. "More, Simipour!" And Simipour sprayed higher and higher, until a rainbow appeared in the spray.

Munna was a pink Pokémon with flower patterns on its body. It floated in the air at night, and it ate dreams. But only happy ones!

Munna floated from house to house, sniffing the dreams of sleeping children. When it found a happy dream, it nibbled a tiny bit, and a pink mist floated out of its forehead. The mist smelled sweet, like flowers. Whoever breathed it in had even happier dreams. So if you dream something lovely tonight, maybe Munna floated by your window.

Musharna was a pink, dreamy Pokémon that floated in the air, half asleep. A soft pink mist always drifted from its forehead, full of happy dreams.

When people breathed in Musharna's dream mist, they saw beautiful pictures in their minds: fields of flowers, flying through clouds, swimming with friendly fish. Musharna liked to float in the children's room at bedtime, filling the air with gentle pink mist. And one by one, the children closed their eyes and floated off into the happiest dreams.

Pidove was a little gray bird Pokémon that lived in towns and parks. It liked to hang around people, especially people with crumbs.

When someone sat on a park bench with a sandwich, Pidove hopped right up. Hop, hop, hop. Then another Pidove came. And another. And another! Soon, there were twenty Pidove gathered around, cooing politely. Coo, coo, coo. The person laughed and shared the crumbs. Pidove always said thank you with a little bob of its head.

Tranquill was a bird Pokémon with a special talent: it always knew the way home. No matter how far it flew, it could always find its way back.

People in the old days used Tranquill to carry letters. A little boy tied a note to Tranquill's leg. "Please take this to Grandma," he said. Tranquill flew over hills and rivers and forests, all the way to Grandma's house. Then it flew back, carrying Grandma's reply. "I love you too," it said. The boy read it a hundred times.

Unfezant was a beautiful bird Pokémon. The boys had colorful, fancy feathers on their heads, and the girls had soft, gray feathers and were the best fliers.

Unfezant always stayed with its family. When they flew together, they flew wing to wing, never far apart. When one landed, they all landed. When one took off, they all took off. The children on the hill watched them fly by. "They're always together," they said. "Just like a family should be."

Blitzle was a little zebra Pokémon with a spiky mane that glowed when it was full of electricity. Flash!

The Blitzle herd talked to each other by flashing their manes. Flash, flash meant "Let's run!" Flash, flash, flash meant "Over here!" And a slow, soft glow meant "Good night." At night, you could see the whole herd on the plains, their manes twinkling like little lightning bugs. The children counted the flashes until they fell asleep.

Zebstrika was a fast, powerful zebra Pokémon with a bright, crackling mane. When it ran, it was as fast as lightning, and its hooves made the sound of thunder.

Zebstrika loved to race across the plains during thunderstorms. Clip, clop, CRACK! Its mane flashed with every bolt of lightning. The other Pokémon watched from their shelters. "There goes Zebstrika!" they said. And when the storm was over, Zebstrika trotted home, its mane still glowing, happy and tired from its stormy run.

Roggenrola was a little rock Pokémon with a hexagon-shaped ear on its side. It could hear tiny sounds through the ground, like the footsteps of a faraway friend.

Roggenrola liked to sit very still and listen. It heard the Diglett digging underground. It heard the rain falling on the hills. It heard the river flowing far away. "What do you hear, Roggenrola?" asked a friend. Roggenrola thought for a moment. "I hear you," it said. "Walking right this way." And they both laughed.

Boldore was a rock Pokémon with shining orange crystals growing out of its body. When it was full of energy, the crystals glowed bright, like little lanterns.

Boldore lived in caves, and it used its glowing crystals to light up the dark. When the explorers came into the cave with their flashlights, Boldore glowed even brighter to help them see. "Thank you, Boldore!" they said. They found sparkly crystals in the walls, and underground pools, and tiny cave flowers, all lit up by Boldore's gentle glow.

Gigalith was a big rock Pokémon covered in bright orange crystals. The crystals soaked up sunlight during the day, and at night they glowed warm and bright.

Gigalith liked to stand on the hilltop in the sunshine, soaking up the light. Then, when the night came, it walked down into the village and stood in the square. Its crystals glowed like a big bonfire, lighting up the whole square. The villagers gathered around to tell stories and sing songs in Gigalith's warm glow.

Woobat was a little blue bat Pokémon with a nose shaped like a heart. And when Woobat stuck its nose to something, it left a little heart-shaped mark!

Woobat liked to fly around the cave and stick its nose on the walls. Boop! A heart. Boop! Another heart. Boop! Another! Soon, the whole cave was covered in little hearts. When the explorers came in with their flashlights, they gasped. "Who made all these hearts?" From the ceiling, Woobat giggled. Boop!

Swoobat was a fluffy blue bat Pokémon with a heart-shaped nose and a long, wiggly tail. It could make special sounds that made everyone who heard them feel happy.

When Swoobat was happy, it sang its special song. It was so high that people couldn't quite hear it, but they could feel it, a warm, fluttery feeling in their chests. When Swoobat flew over the town, people started smiling and humming for no reason at all. "What a lovely day," they said. And Swoobat swooped happily overhead.

Drilbur was a little brown mole Pokémon with sharp claws. When it put its claws together and spun around, it turned into a drill. Whirrr! And it zoomed right through the dirt!

Drilbur could dig tunnels faster than anyone. It dug a tunnel under the river, so the Pokémon could cross without getting wet. It dug a tunnel under the hill, so they didn't have to climb. And it dug a secret tunnel to the berry patch, just for its best friends. Whirrr! "Follow me!" it called.

Excadrill was a big, strong mole Pokémon with a drill on its head and steel claws. When it spun, it could drill through solid rock. Whirrrrrrr!

Excadrill helped the people build tunnels for the trains. It dug through the mountains, whirr, whirr, whirr, making long, straight tunnels. When the first train went through the tunnel, choo-choo, all the people cheered. Excadrill stood at the entrance and waved its claws. The train driver honked the horn, just for Excadrill. Toot, toot!

Audino was a soft, pink Pokémon with big, curly ears. Its ears were so good at listening that they could hear a heartbeat, and they could tell if someone wasn't feeling well.

Audino worked at the Pokémon Center, helping the nurse. When a Pokémon came in feeling sick, Audino put its ears close and listened. Thump, thump, thump. "I know what's wrong," it said. Then it helped the nurse make the Pokémon feel better, with soft hugs and gentle care. Everyone felt better after a visit with Audino.

Timburr was a little gray Pokémon that always carried a wooden log. It was a hard worker, and it loved helping people build things.

Timburr helped the builders fix houses and build fences. It carried planks and logs, one at a time, hup, hup, hup. When the work was done, Timburr sat down with the builders and shared their lunch. "You're a great helper, Timburr," they said. Timburr hugged its log proudly. Tomorrow, there would be more to build.

Gurdurr was a strong Pokémon that carried a big steel beam everywhere it went. It was so strong that the builders couldn't believe it.

Gurdurr helped build the tallest building in town. It carried steel beams up, up, up, all the way to the top. Hup, hup, hup! When the building was finished, the builders gave Gurdurr a special gift: a shiny steel beam with its name painted on it. Gurdurr carried it everywhere after that, showing it off to everyone.

Conkeldurr was a big, strong Pokémon that carried two stone pillars like walking sticks. People said that long ago, Conkeldurr taught people how to make concrete.

Conkeldurr was very old and very wise. It had helped build bridges, walls and houses for hundreds of years. The young builders came to learn from it. "Mix the stone just so," it said. "Pour it carefully. Let it set." And the young builders listened. Thanks to Conkeldurr, the town's buildings were the strongest in the land.

Tympole was a little blue tadpole Pokémon that sang high-pitched songs. The songs made little ripples in the water, and the other Tympole could feel them.

The Tympole talked to each other with their songs. One high note meant "Hello!" Two notes meant "Let's swim!" Three notes meant "Danger!" And a long, wobbly note meant "I'm happy." On quiet evenings, the whole pond rippled with their little songs, like a big, watery choir.

Palpitoad was a blue frog Pokémon with bumps on its head. When it sang, the bumps wobbled and made the water vibrate. Wobble, wobble, splash!

Palpitoad liked to sing in the rain. Pitter, patter, wobble, wobble! The rain made the pond ripple, and Palpitoad's songs made it ripple even more. The other Pokémon came to listen. "It sounds like the pond is singing," they said. Palpitoad puffed up proudly and sang another song.

Seismitoad was a big blue frog Pokémon covered in bumps. When it vibrated the bumps, they shook very fast, like a little earthquake. Brrrrrr!

People found out that Seismitoad's bumps were perfect for something wonderful: massages! When the farmers had sore backs after a long day, Seismitoad let them lean against its bumpy side. Brrrrrr! The vibration made their sore muscles feel so much better. "Ahh," they sighed. "Seismitoad, you're the best."

Throh was a strong red Pokémon that wore a belt made of vines. It practiced its throws every day, and whenever it got a little bit stronger, it tied its belt a little bit tighter.

Throh lived in a group with other Throh, and they practiced together in the mountains. Hup! Hup! When the young Throh fell down, the older ones helped them up. "Try again," they said. "Practice makes perfect." And every evening, they sat together under the stars, tightening their belts and telling stories.

Sawk was a strong blue Pokémon that loved practicing karate. It practiced its chops and kicks every day, deep in the mountains, where nobody would disturb it.

When Sawk tied its belt tighter, it felt stronger. When it practiced, it focused so hard that it didn't notice anything else. Hi-yah! Once, it practiced so hard that it didn't notice a Pidove landing on its head. The Pidove sat there for an hour. When Sawk finally noticed, it laughed so hard that it fell over. Hi-yah... ha-ha!

Sewaddle was a little yellow bug Pokémon that made its own clothes! It chewed up leaves and used sticky thread from its mouth to sew them together.

Sewaddle made itself a cozy leaf hood that covered its head. It looked so cute that people who made clothes chose Sewaddle as their mascot. "Look at Sewaddle's lovely hood!" they said. Sewaddle was very proud. It made a new hood every season: green in spring, yellow in autumn and a cozy brown one for winter.

Swadloon wrapped itself in a cozy blanket of leaves, like a burrito. It sat in the forest, all snug and warm, and it took care of the trees around it.

Swadloon had a special job. It turned fallen leaves into good soil that helped the forest grow. Wherever Swadloon lived, the trees grew tall and the flowers bloomed brightly. "The forest is so healthy here," said a visitor. "That's because of Swadloon," said the Pidove. Swadloon just snuggled deeper into its leafy blanket.

Leavanny was a tall, kind bug Pokémon that loved to sew. It made beautiful clothes out of leaves, using the sharp edges of its arms to cut them and its silky thread to sew them.

When Leavanny found a little Pokémon in the forest, it made it a leafy coat. A tiny leaf jacket for a little Sewaddle. A soft leaf scarf for a little Pidove. A leaf hat for a little Patrat. "Now you're all dressed up," Leavanny said kindly. And the little Pokémon twirled around in their new clothes, feeling like the best-dressed Pokémon in the forest.

Venipede was a little centipede Pokémon with lots and lots of legs. It could run very fast, scurrying through the grass. Skitter, skitter, skitter!

Venipede liked to count its legs. "One, two, three... oh no, I lost count!" It always lost count. So its friends helped. "One, two, three, four..." But they always lost count too! Finally, they gave up and went for a run instead. Skitter, skitter, skitter! Venipede was the fastest runner of all. All those legs had to be good for something!

Whirlipede was a round, purple Pokémon wrapped in a hard shell. It didn't move much. But when it wanted to, it curled into a ball and rolled. Whirrrr!

Whirlipede spun so fast that it whistled as it rolled downhill. Wheeee! Its friends lined up at the bottom of the hill to watch it zoom past. Then they all ran up the hill to do it again. Whirlipede thought rolling was the most fun thing in the world. And at the end of the day, it was so dizzy that it fell asleep right where it stopped.

Scolipede was a big, purple centipede Pokémon with long horns. It was very fast, and it could curl its long body around to make itself into a wheel.

Scolipede loved to race along the forest paths, rolling like a giant hoop. Whoosh! The leaves flew up behind it. The children in the forest heard it coming and jumped aside, cheering. "Go, Scolipede, go!" And Scolipede rolled all the way to the end of the path, uncurled and took a bow.

Cottonee was a little puff of cotton with a tiny face. It was so light that it floated on the breeze, drifting wherever the wind went. Floaty, floaty.

When lots of Cottonee got together, they stuck to each other and made one big cotton ball. Then they floated across the sky like a fluffy cloud. The children on the hill looked up and pointed. "Is that a cloud?" "No, it's Cottonee!" When the wind dropped, the Cottonee floated down and landed softly on the children's heads, like fluffy hats.

Whimsicott was a fluffy Pokémon covered in cotton. It was full of mischief, and it could slip through the tiniest cracks, like a puff of wind.

Whimsicott loved to sneak into houses and leave little surprises. It left cotton fluff on pillows. It left a cotton bunny on the kitchen table. It left a cotton trail across the living room floor. "Whimsicott was here!" laughed the family, finding fluff everywhere. They never saw Whimsicott. But the house always felt a little softer after it came.

Petilil was a little green Pokémon with leaves on top of its head. The leaves were very bitter, but if you made them into tea, they could help a tired person feel better.

When the old farmer felt tired after a long day of work, Petilil came to visit. It gave him one of its leaves, and he made a cup of leaf tea. Sip. "Blech, bitter!" he said, making a face. But then he smiled. "But I feel much better!" Petilil wiggled its leaves happily. Its leaves always grew back, so it could visit again tomorrow.

Lilligant was a graceful Pokémon with a beautiful red flower on its head. Even gardeners who were very good at growing flowers found it hard to make Lilligant's flower bloom.

But when Lilligant's flower did bloom, it was the most beautiful flower in the garden. It smelled so sweet and calm that anyone who smelled it felt relaxed. The busy grown-ups in town came to visit Lilligant after work. Sniff. "Ahh," they said, their shoulders relaxing. And Lilligant danced a slow, pretty dance for them before they went home.

Basculin was a fish Pokémon that came in two colors: some had red stripes, and some had blue stripes. The red-striped ones and the blue-striped ones didn't always get along.

One day, a red-striped Basculin and a blue-striped Basculin got stuck in the same little pond after a big rain. At first, they swam on opposite sides. But it was a very small pond. Slowly, they swam closer. "Your stripes are nice," said the red one. "So are yours," said the blue one. By the time the river flowed again, they were best friends.

Sandile was a little crocodile Pokémon that lived in the desert. It buried itself in the warm sand, leaving only its eyes and nose peeking out.

Sandile had a dark film over its eyes that kept out the sand and the bright sun. It was like wearing sunglasses! When its friends came to visit, Sandile popped out of the sand, shook itself off and grinned. "Want to go for a sand swim?" And they dove into the sand together, wiggling through it like water.

Krokorok was a crocodile Pokémon with a dark band across its eyes, like a mask. The band let it see in the dark, so it could travel through the desert at night.

Krokorok lived in a group with other Krokorok. When the sun went down and the desert cooled, they went out together, walking in a line across the sand. Step, step, step. Under the stars, the desert was quiet and beautiful. Krokorok led the way, its eyes shining in the darkness, until they reached a cool oasis to rest.

Krookodile was a big, strong crocodile Pokémon with sharp eyes that could see very far across the desert. It could spot a tiny friend from miles away.

Krookodile liked to stand on the tallest sand dune and look around. Nothing in the desert escaped its sharp eyes. When a little Sandile wandered too far from home, Krookodile spotted it right away. It walked across the dunes, scooped up the little Sandile and carried it home. "You have to stay close," it said gently. The Sandile nodded and snuggled in.

Darumaka was a little red Pokémon with a warm, fiery body. When it slept, it pulled in its arms and legs and looked just like a round ball.

Darumaka's body was always warm inside, and it loved to play. It bounced around all day, full of energy. Bounce, bounce, bounce! But when bedtime came, it curled up into a round, warm ball and fell fast asleep. The children in the house liked to have Darumaka at the foot of their bed on cold nights. It was better than a hot water bottle.

Darmanitan was a big, fiery Pokémon with strong arms. It was full of energy, but when it got very tired, it did something surprising: it sat down, still as a statue, and began to meditate.

In its calm form, Darmanitan sat very still and quiet, letting its energy come back. The children in town liked to sit beside it and copy it. They crossed their legs, closed their eyes and breathed slowly. In... and out... In... and out... Soon they felt calm too. Then Darmanitan opened its eyes and jumped up, full of energy again!

Maractus was a cactus Pokémon that loved to dance. When it moved, it made a rattling sound, just like maracas. Shake, shake, shake!

Maractus danced in the desert to a rhythm only it could hear. Shake, shake, cha-cha-cha! The desert Pokémon couldn't help but dance along. Sandile wiggled. Krokorok tapped their feet. Even the cactus flowers seemed to sway. When the sun went down, Maractus did one last spin and bowed. Shake, shake! Good night, desert!

Dwebble was a little hermit crab Pokémon that carried a rock on its back for a home. When it found a good rock, it made a hole in it and moved right in.

Dwebble's rock was its house, and it carried it everywhere. When it was tired, it tucked itself inside and took a nap. When it was scared, it hid inside. One day, Dwebble's rock cracked. Oh no! It walked all around the beach, looking for a new one. Not too big. Not too small. Then it found the perfect rock, and it moved in with a happy sigh.

Crustle was a big hermit crab Pokémon that carried a huge, heavy rock on its back. Its legs were very strong, and it could carry its rock all day without getting tired.

Crustle's rock was so big that the little Pokémon liked to climb on top of it. A Sandile sunbathed on it. A Pidove built a nest on it. A little Dwebble used it as a lookout. Crustle didn't mind. It walked slowly along the beach, carrying its rock and all its little friends, like a moving island.

Scraggy was a little yellow Pokémon with loose, droopy skin. Its skin hung down around its legs like baggy pants, and Scraggy was always pulling them up!

Scraggy tried to look tough. It puffed out its chest and said, "I'm the toughest Pokémon around!" But then its baggy skin slipped down, and it had to pull it up again. Tug, tug! Its friends giggled. Scraggy's cheeks turned pink. Then it giggled too. Being tough was hard work when your pants kept falling down.

Scrafty was a Pokémon with a red crest on its head and loose skin like baggy pants. It looked very tough, but it was very loyal to its friends.

Scrafty was the leader of a group of young Pokémon, and it took good care of them. When one of them was being teased, Scrafty stood beside them and said, "Leave my friend alone." When one of them was sad, Scrafty sat with them. And when one of them had a birthday, Scrafty baked a cake. A tough-looking Pokémon with the softest heart.

Sigilyph was a strange, colorful bird Pokémon that looked like a painting from long ago. It flew the same path every day, around and around an old ruined city.

Sigilyph never changed its path. Around the old towers, over the broken walls, past the old fountain and back again. People said it was the guardian of the ancient city, watching over it as it had for thousands of years. When explorers came to visit, Sigilyph flew beside them, showing them the way, like a tour guide from long ago.

Yamask was a little ghost Pokémon that carried a golden mask. It held the mask close and looked at it often, as if it were trying to remember something from long ago.

Yamask liked to float through old museums at night, looking at the paintings and statues. It was curious about the past. "What was it like back then?" it wondered. The night guard at the museum got used to Yamask. He made it a little cup of tea every night, and they sat together looking at the old treasures, wondering about the old days.

Cofagrigus was a ghost Pokémon that looked like a shiny golden treasure box. It had four shadowy arms, and it liked to sit very still in old pyramids.

People sometimes thought Cofagrigus was a treasure chest! They walked up to it, excited. "Treasure!" Then Cofagrigus opened its eyes and waved its shadowy arms. "Boo!" The explorers jumped back and then laughed. "You got us!" Cofagrigus liked that game. It never hurt anyone. It just liked a good joke.

Tirtouga was an ancient turtle Pokémon that lived in the sea long, long ago. Scientists brought it back from a fossil, and now it swims in the museum's big pool.

Tirtouga could dive very deep, and it could also walk on land. It liked to swim to the bottom of the pool and then climb out onto the rocks to dry off in the sun. The children at the museum waved at it. "Hi, Tirtouga!" It waved its flippers back. It had been asleep for a very long time, but it was happy to have so many new friends.

Carracosta was a big ancient turtle Pokémon with strong flippers and a hard shell. Long ago, it could swim fast and walk on land, and it was very strong.

Carracosta was the oldest Pokémon in the aquarium, and the young Pokémon loved to hear its stories. "When I was young," it said, "the seas were full of ancient Pokémon. Omanyte, Kabuto, Tirtouga..." The young ones listened with wide eyes. Carracosta told stories until feeding time, and then it shared its lunch with everyone.

Archen was an ancient Pokémon that looked like a little bird with colorful feathers. People thought it might be the ancestor of all bird Pokémon. But Archen couldn't fly yet!

Archen hopped from branch to branch, flapping its little wings. Flap, flap, hop! It tried and tried to fly. Sometimes it glided a little way, then landed with a bump. "Almost!" said its friends. Archen didn't give up. It hopped higher and flapped harder, every day. And one day, it glided all the way across the clearing!

Archeops was an ancient bird Pokémon with bright feathers. It could run very fast on its legs, but it wasn't very good at flying. It needed a running start!

Archeops ran across the field as fast as it could. Run, run, run, flap! It took off into the air, flew a little way and landed. Then it ran again. Run, run, run, flap! The children cheered it on. "Go, Archeops!" It might not fly like a Pidgeot, but it was the fastest runner in the whole museum park.

Trubbish was a little Pokémon that looked like a garbage bag. It liked messy places, and it lived where people threw away their trash.

But Trubbish had a dream. It wanted to help make the town cleaner. So it started collecting trash and sorting it. Paper here. Bottles there. Cans in a pile. The townspeople noticed. "Trubbish is recycling!" they said. They started sorting their trash too. And soon, the whole town was cleaner than ever, thanks to a little garbage bag Pokémon.

Garbodor was a big trash Pokémon with long, droopy arms. It was made of garbage, and it smelled a bit like garbage too.

But Garbodor had a kind heart. It liked to help keep the town clean by gathering trash that people dropped on the ground. Scoop, scoop! It carried the trash to the recycling center and sorted it out. The people of the town were grateful. "Thank you, Garbodor!" And they made sure to always use the bins, so Garbodor didn't have to work so hard.

Zorua was a little fox Pokémon with a red tuft on its head. And it had a magic trick: it could make itself look like anybody else! A Pidove, a little girl, even a teapot.

Zorua loved to play tricks on its friends. It made itself look like a Pikachu and said, "Pika!" Everyone was fooled. It made itself look like a big Snorlax and pretended to snore. Everyone was fooled again! But Zorua always gave itself away in the end, because it couldn't stop giggling. And when it giggled, its fluffy tail popped out.

Zoroark was a big fox Pokémon with a long red mane. It could make illusions, pictures in the air that looked completely real. A forest that wasn't there. A river that wasn't there.

Zoroark used its illusions to protect its family. When the little Zorua were sleeping, Zoroark made an illusion of a big, prickly bush around their den, so nobody would disturb them. Shh. Behind the illusion, the Zorua slept peacefully, curled up together. And Zoroark kept watch until morning.

Minccino was a little gray Pokémon with a big, fluffy tail. It loved everything to be clean and tidy, and it used its tail like a duster!

Minccino dusted the shelves. Swish, swish. It dusted the windowsills. Swish, swish. It dusted its friends' heads. Swish, swish! "Hey!" they giggled. Minccino couldn't help it. If it saw dust, it had to clean it. The family it lived with had the cleanest house in town. And Minccino had the shiniest tail.

When Minccino touched a Shiny Stone, it became Cinccino, a white Pokémon with soft, silky fur like scarves. Its fur was coated in a special oil that kept dust away.

Cinccino was very elegant. It kept its fur clean and fluffy, and it helped keep everyone else clean too. It brushed the little Minccino's tails. It fluffed up the cushions. It even polished the doorknobs until they sparkled. Swish, swish, shine! "Cinccino, you make everything beautiful," said the family. Cinccino twirled its silky scarves and smiled.

Gothita was a little Pokémon with a big bow on its head. It liked to stare at things that nobody else could see. It would look at an empty corner and smile, as if someone were there.

"What are you looking at, Gothita?" asked its friends. Gothita just smiled and kept staring. Some people said it could see invisible things, like dreams floating in the air. Maybe it was watching a happy dream drift by. Maybe it was waving to an invisible friend. Nobody knew. But Gothita always looked very happy about it.

Gothorita was a Pokémon with a pretty dress and bows. It loved to look at the stars, and people said it gathered its power from starlight.

On clear nights, Gothorita stood in the meadow, looking up at the stars. It stood so still, and the stars twinkled down at it. The children sometimes joined it, lying on the grass. "Which one is your favorite, Gothorita?" Gothorita pointed at the brightest one. And from then on, the children called it Gothorita's star.

Gothitelle was a tall, elegant Pokémon that could see the stars move. People said it could read the future in the patterns of the stars.

Gothitelle liked to stargaze with its friends. "Tomorrow will be sunny," it said, looking at the stars. And it was! "Next week, someone will find something they lost." And they did! The townspeople came to ask it questions. "Will it be a good harvest?" Gothitelle looked up and smiled. "The best one yet."

Solosis was a tiny green Pokémon floating inside a bubble of special jelly. The jelly kept it safe, like a little space suit.

Solosis could talk to its friends without saying anything at all. It just thought, and they heard it in their heads! "Hello," it thought to a Pidove. The Pidove jumped. "Did someone say hello?" Solosis giggled inside its bubble. It liked floating around and surprising its friends with friendly thoughts.

Duosion was a Pokémon with a brain that had split into two parts. Sometimes the two parts thought different things at the same time!

One part of Duosion's brain wanted to go to the park. The other part wanted to go to the lake. "Park!" "Lake!" "Park!" "Lake!" Duosion floated in circles, trying to decide. Finally, both parts had the same idea: "The park next to the lake!" And off it floated, happy that both halves agreed.

Reuniclus was a green Pokémon floating inside a jelly body, with big jelly arms. Its brain was very powerful, and it could lift heavy things with its mind.

When two Reuniclus shook their jelly hands, their minds connected, and they could share their thoughts. Shake! "Hello, friend." "Hello, friend." The children at the park tried shaking hands with Reuniclus too. Its jelly arms were cool and squishy. They couldn't read its mind, but they felt a warm, friendly feeling, and that was almost the same.

Ducklett was a little blue duck Pokémon that loved to swim and dive. It could dive deep under the water and stay there for a long time.

Ducklett liked to play diving games with its friends. "Ready? Dive!" Splash! They all dove under the water. Ducklett stayed under the longest. The others popped back up, but Ducklett didn't come up. One second. Two seconds. Then, splash! It popped up right behind them, quacking with laughter. Quack, quack!

Swanna was a beautiful white swan Pokémon with a long, graceful neck. It loved to dance, especially at dawn.

As the sun came up over the lake, the Swanna gathered together and started their morning dance. They bowed their long necks, they spread their wings and they spun gracefully on the water. The lake turned pink and gold with the sunrise. The fishermen stopped rowing to watch. It was the most beautiful dance in the world, and it happened every morning.

Vanillite was a little Pokémon that looked just like an ice cream cone! Its body was made of ice and snow, and it breathed out cold, snowy air.

Vanillite loved cold weather. When the snow fell, it danced around in it, catching snowflakes. When it was too warm, it made its own little snow flurries around itself. Flurry, flurry! The children always wanted to lick it, because it looked so much like ice cream. But Vanillite always said, "No, no, I'm not dessert!" and floated away, giggling.

Vanillish was an icy Pokémon that looked like a big swirl of snow, like soft-serve ice cream. It made little ice crystals and snowy clouds wherever it went.

Vanillish liked to make little snow clouds over its friends' heads, just for fun. Poof! A tiny cloud appeared over a Pidove, and it started to snow on it. "Hey!" The Pidove shook off the snow and laughed. Vanillish made snow clouds over everyone, and soon they were all throwing snowballs in the middle of summer.

Vanilluxe was a big icy Pokémon with two swirly heads, like a double scoop of ice cream. When it was happy, it made a big, sparkly snowstorm.

When both of Vanilluxe's heads were happy, they laughed together, and the air filled with sparkly snow. Snow, snow, snow! The children in the village loved it. They built snowmen and snow forts and snow castles, all thanks to Vanilluxe. And when the two heads got tired, they yawned at the same time and took a nap in the snow.

Deerling was a little deer Pokémon that changed color with the seasons. In spring, it was pink. In summer, it was green. In autumn, it was orange. And in winter, it was white.

The children in the village always knew what season it was by looking at Deerling. "Deerling is pink! It's spring!" they said. And when Deerling turned orange, they knew it was time for leaf piles and warm cocoa. Deerling liked being the village's calendar. It felt very important.

Sawsbuck was a tall, graceful deer Pokémon with antlers that changed with the seasons. In spring, flowers bloomed on them. In summer, green leaves grew. In autumn, the leaves turned red. And in winter, the antlers were bare.

Every spring, the children waited to see Sawsbuck's flowers bloom. When it walked through the village with flowers on its antlers, they ran out to see. "Spring is here!" Sawsbuck bowed its head, and the children gently touched the soft flowers. It was the most beautiful way to welcome spring.

Emolga was a little flying squirrel Pokémon. It had a cape of skin between its arms and legs, and when it jumped from a tree, it glided through the air like a kite. Wheee!

Emolga stored electricity in its cheeks, and when it glided, little sparks crackled around it. Zap, zap! It loved gliding from tree to tree, sparkling through the forest. The children watched it at dusk, when it looked like a little shooting star. "Make a wish!" they said, every time Emolga sparkled by.

Karrablast was a little blue bug Pokémon that wanted a shell more than anything. It saw the Shelmet with their nice, round shells and felt a little bit jealous.

Then one day, Karrablast met a Shelmet, and they became friends. They played together every day. And one day, something amazing happened: they both changed at the same time! Karrablast got a shiny suit of armor, and Shelmet became light and super fast. They looked at each other and laughed. "We helped each other grow!"

Escavalier was a bug Pokémon wearing a shiny suit of armor, like a knight. It had two long lances on its arms, and it was very brave.

Escavalier liked to protect the little Pokémon in its forest. It stood guard at the edge of the forest, shiny and strong. When the wind blew, it stood firm. When the rain fell, it stood firm. And when the little Pokémon came out to play, they always felt safe, knowing their knight was nearby.

Foongus was a little mushroom Pokémon with a cap that looked just like a ball. Red and white, round and shiny. Lots of people thought it was a ball!

Foongus liked to sit in the grass and wait. When someone walked by and said, "Oh, look, a ball!" Foongus jumped up and wiggled. "Surprise!" The children loved this game. They pretended to be fooled every time, and Foongus giggled and wiggled every time. It was the silliest mushroom in the forest.

Amoonguss was a mushroom Pokémon with a cap that looked like a ball. It had two smaller caps on its arms, and it liked to wave them around.

Amoonguss liked to dance. It waved its arm caps back and forth, back and forth, swaying in the breeze. The other Pokémon thought it was a game. They waved their arms too. Wave, wave, sway! Soon, the whole forest was dancing with Amoonguss. And when Amoonguss shook its cap, a little puff of spores floated up, sparkly in the sunlight.

Frillish was a jellyfish Pokémon with frilly tentacles. It floated in the sea, drifting slowly with the waves. Some Frillish were blue and some were pink.

Frillish liked to drift near the surface and look up at the sky. It watched the clouds and the birds and the sun. "I wonder what it's like up there," it thought. One day, a Ducklett landed on the water next to it. "Hello!" said the Ducklett. "Want to hear about the sky?" And Frillish listened happily, bobbing on the waves.

Jellicent was a big jellyfish Pokémon with a crown on its head. It lived at the bottom of the sea, in a palace made from old shipwrecks.

Jellicent was the queen of the deep sea. It floated through its palace, wearing its crown proudly, and the deep-sea Pokémon bowed when it passed by. Jellicent held parties in its palace, with glowing lanterns and seaweed decorations. Everyone was invited: Finneon, Lumineon, Chinchou and even the little Frillish. It was the best party under the sea.

Alomomola was a big pink fish Pokémon shaped like a heart. People called it the nurse of the sea, because it loved to help other Pokémon feel better.

When a sea Pokémon was hurt, Alomomola swam up and wrapped it gently in its soft fins. Its special skin helped hurt places heal. "There, there," it seemed to say. The little Pokémon felt better in no time. Alomomola swam around the ocean all day, helping anyone who needed it. It was the kindest fish in the sea.

Joltik was a tiny yellow bug Pokémon, about the size of a button. It couldn't make electricity on its own, so it climbed onto bigger Pokémon to collect their static.

Joltik climbed onto a fluffy Mareep. Zap! It got a little electricity. It climbed onto an Emolga. Zap! A little more. It climbed onto a fuzzy Lillipup. Zap! "Hey, that tickles!" said the Lillipup. Joltik giggled. Now it had enough electricity to glow all night, like a tiny yellow night-light.

Galvantula was a big yellow spider Pokémon that spun webs full of electricity. When the sun hit the webs, they sparkled and crackled. Zzzt!

Galvantula liked to spin webs between the trees, making beautiful patterns. Circles, spirals, stars! At night, the webs glowed with electricity, lighting up the forest. The forest Pokémon called it the light weaver. And on dark nights, they followed the glowing webs all the way home.

Ferroseed was a little round Pokémon covered in steel spikes. It stuck its spikes into the ceilings of caves and hung there, upside down, soaking up iron from the rocks.

Ferroseed was usually very still and quiet. When something came near, it rattled its spikes, clink, clink, which meant, "Careful, I'm prickly!" The cave explorers learned to say hello from a little distance. And Ferroseed, hanging from the ceiling, rattled its spikes again, just a little, to say hello back.

Ferrothorn was a spiky steel Pokémon with long, thorny vines. It liked to hang from the ceilings of caves, swinging gently on its vines.

Ferrothorn's thorns were very sharp, so it always moved very carefully around its friends. When the little Ferroseed wanted to play, Ferrothorn swung them gently on its vines, like a swing set. Swing, swing! The Ferroseed giggled. "Higher!" And Ferrothorn swung them a little bit higher, very, very carefully.

Klink was two little gears that fit together perfectly. They spun together, click, click, click, and they never, ever came apart.

The two gears were best friends. When one gear turned, the other turned too. Click, click, click! If one gear was tired, the other spun a little faster to help. People liked to watch Klink spin. "How do they always stay together?" they asked. Klink clicked happily. Best friends always fit together, like gears.

Klang was a big gear and a little gear spinning together. The little gear spun very fast, and the big gear spun slowly and steadily. Whirr, click, whirr, click!

Klang helped at the old clock tower. It spun inside the clock, keeping the hands moving round and round. Tick, tock, whirr, click. The whole town knew what time it was, thanks to Klang. And every hour, when the bells rang, Klang spun a little faster, just for fun.

Klinklang was three gears spinning together, with a little red core in the middle. When it spun really fast, its core glowed bright red. Whirrrrr!

Klinklang worked at the big factory, keeping all the machines running. Whirr, click, whirr, click! It spun the conveyor belts. It turned the wheels. And at lunchtime, it spun the big ice cream machine, so all the workers got a cold treat. "Thanks, Klinklang!" they said. Klinklang's core glowed with pride.

Tynamo was a tiny eel Pokémon that could make little sparks of electricity. One Tynamo alone could only make a tiny zap. But Tynamo never swam alone.

The Tynamo swam together in big groups. When they all made sparks at the same time, the electricity was so strong that it lit up the whole river! Zap, zap, ZAP! The fishermen saw the river glowing at night and smiled. "The Tynamo are out," they said. Little by little, together, they were strong.

Eelektrik was a long blue eel Pokémon with yellow circles on its body. The circles made electricity, and they glowed when Eelektrik was full of energy.

Eelektrik swam through the river at night, its circles glowing like little lamps. Glow, glow, glow. The fish followed it, using its light to find their way through the dark water. "Where are we going, Eelektrik?" they asked. "Anywhere you like," said Eelektrik. And they swam together until the moon was high.

Eelektross was a big eel Pokémon with a mouth like a sucker. It could climb out of the water and pull itself up onto rocks using its sucker mouth. Smooch!

Eelektross liked to visit the land. It climbed out of the river, smooch, smooch, and stuck itself to a big rock to bask in the sun. The children on the riverbank giggled. "It's kissing the rock!" Eelektross looked at them and smooched the rock again, just to make them laugh.

Elgyem was a little Pokémon with a big head and big eyes. People said it came from outer space, a long time ago, when something fell from the sky into the desert.

Elgyem was very curious about everything on Earth. It looked at flowers and wondered. It looked at rain and wondered. It looked at children eating ice cream and wondered very, very much. One little boy shared his ice cream with Elgyem. It tasted it with its tiny mouth, and its big eyes went even bigger. "Mmm," it thought. Earth was a wonderful place.

Beheeyem was a Pokémon from space with a big head and three colored lights on each hand. It talked to its friends by flashing the lights. Red, yellow, green!

Nobody knew exactly what the flashing meant. But the children in the village tried to learn. Red, red, green meant "Hello!" they decided. Yellow, yellow, yellow meant "I'm hungry." And all three together meant "Good night." The children flashed their flashlights at Beheeyem every night, and Beheeyem flashed back. Red, yellow, green. Good night!

Litwick was a little candle Pokémon with a purple flame on its head. It glowed softly, like a little night-light, and it liked to light the way in the dark.

When a little girl got lost on her way home one evening, she saw a soft purple glow ahead. It was Litwick, bobbing along. It floated in front of her, lighting the path. Glow, glow, glow. She followed it all the way to her front door. When she turned to say thank you, Litwick gave a little flicker and floated off to help someone else.

Lampent was a ghost Pokémon that looked like an old-fashioned lantern. It floated through the streets at night, glowing with a soft, purple light.

Lampent liked to keep the town company at night. It floated past windows, glowing softly. People who couldn't sleep saw it and felt calm. "Lampent is out," they said. "Everything's all right." And Lampent floated on, lighting up the dark alleys and quiet corners, until the sun came up and it floated home to rest.

Chandelure was a ghost Pokémon that looked like a beautiful chandelier with purple flames. When it waved its arms, its flames swayed and danced.

Chandelure lived in an old mansion, where it hung from the ceiling of the grand ballroom. Every night, it lit up the room with its dancing flames. The flames made shadows that looked like people dancing. Twirl, swirl, flicker! The little ghost Pokémon came to dance in the ballroom, and Chandelure made the most beautiful lights for them.

Axew was a little green dragon Pokémon with two tusks on its face. It used its tusks for all sorts of things, like cutting fruit and marking trees.

Axew's tusks were very important to it. It practiced using them every day, cutting apples and slicing berries. Chop, chop! If a tusk broke, a new one grew back stronger. Axew was very proud when it learned to cut an apple into perfect slices. It shared the slices with all its friends. "Delicious!" they said.

Fraxure was a dragon Pokémon with strong, sharp tusks. Every day, it sharpened its tusks on rocks, scrape, scrape, scrape, to keep them shiny and strong.

Fraxure was very proud of its tusks. It polished them until they shone. When its friends needed help, Fraxure used its tusks to cut through tangled vines and chop branches for firewood. Chop, chop! "Thanks, Fraxure!" they said. Fraxure grinned and gave its tusks one more polish.

Haxorus was a big, strong dragon Pokémon with huge tusks. Its tusks were so strong that they could cut through steel. But Haxorus was gentle with its friends.

Haxorus lived in a cave in the mountains. It was strong and brave, but it was also kind. When a little Axew got lost, Haxorus found it and carried it home on its back. "Thank you, Haxorus," said the Axew's family. Haxorus nodded. Being strong was good. Being kind was even better.

Cubchoo was a little white bear cub Pokémon, and its nose was always running! A drip of icy snot always hung from its nose.

When Cubchoo sneezed, ah... ah... ACHOO! The drip turned into ice crystals that sparkled in the air. The children laughed. "Bless you, Cubchoo!" Cubchoo sniffed and wiped its nose with its paw. Then it laughed too. Being a little drippy wasn't so bad, especially when your sneezes made sparkles.

Beartic was a big white bear Pokémon that lived in the icy north. It could freeze its breath into icy fangs and claws.

Beartic was a very good swimmer, and it swam in the cold northern sea. When the ice broke up in spring, Beartic swam from iceberg to iceberg, looking for its friends. When it found the little Cubchoo, it let them ride on its back. Splash, splash! They swam together across the icy sea, and the little ones squealed with joy.

Cryogonal was a Pokémon shaped like a beautiful snowflake. It floated in the cold air, with little chains of ice dangling from it.

Cryogonal was born in snow clouds, high in the sky. When it got too warm, it turned into a puff of steam and floated back up. When it got cold again, it came back as a snowflake. The children in the snowy village looked up at the falling snow. "Is that Cryogonal?" they wondered. Every snowflake looked a little bit like it.

Shelmet was a little bug Pokémon that lived inside a hard shell, like a snail. It could close its shell up tight when it was scared.

Shelmet liked to stay safe inside its shell, but it wanted to be faster. It watched the other Pokémon running and playing and wished it could join in. Then one day, it met a Karrablast, and they became friends. And when they changed together, Shelmet came out of its shell for good, light and quick as the wind!

Accelgor was a fast bug Pokémon that wore a mask and a scarf. It used to be a Shelmet, but now it had no shell, and it could move very, very fast. Zip, zip!

Accelgor was like a ninja. It darted through the forest so fast that nobody could see it. Zip! It was here. Zip! It was there. It liked to leave little surprises for its friends: a berry on a doorstep, a flower on a windowsill. "Who left this?" they wondered. Accelgor watched from the trees, smiling behind its mask.

Stunfisk was a flat, brown fish Pokémon that liked to lie still in the mud, with only its face showing. It had a big, funny smile.

Stunfisk was so flat and so still that people sometimes stepped on it by accident! Squish! "Oops!" Then Stunfisk gave them a tiny tingle of electricity. Bzzt! "Eek!" The person laughed and looked down at Stunfisk, smiling up at them. "Sorry, Stunfisk!" Stunfisk kept smiling. It always did.

Mienfoo was a little Pokémon that practiced martial arts. It moved like water, flowing from one move to the next. Swish, swoosh, swish!

Mienfoo practiced every morning by the river. It kicked, it chopped and it spun, quick and graceful. The little Pokémon watched and tried to copy it. Swish, swoosh, flop! They fell over. Mienfoo helped them up. "Slow and steady," it said. "Then fast and flowing." And they practiced together until the sun was high.

Mienshao was a graceful Pokémon with long fur on its arms that flowed like ribbons. When it moved, its arm fur swirled around it, like a dancer's sleeves.

Mienshao practiced its moves so fast and so beautifully that people came to watch. Swirl, swish, spin! It looked like dancing. At the village festival, Mienshao performed on the stage, and its arm ribbons swirled through the air like colorful streamers. The crowd clapped and cheered. It was the most graceful show they had ever seen.

Druddigon was a red and blue dragon Pokémon with a rough, bumpy face. It lived in dark caves, and it liked to come out to warm itself in the sunshine.

Every morning, Druddigon climbed out of its cave and spread its wings in the sun. Ahh, warm. When it was nice and toasty, it could run fast and play. But on cold days, it was slow and sleepy. So its friends brought it blankets on chilly mornings. "Here, Druddigon, stay warm." And Druddigon wrapped up and smiled.

Golett was a little Pokémon made of clay, built by ancient people a very long time ago. Nobody knew exactly how it worked, but it had been walking and helping for thousands of years.

Golett was a good helper. It carried things for people, and it did whatever job it was given, slowly and carefully. Step, step, step. The townspeople liked having Golett around. It never complained, and it never got tired. And when the work was done, it sat quietly in the sun, its clay body warming up.

Golurk was a giant clay Pokémon, made long ago to protect people and Pokémon. It had a band across its chest, and it could fly by blasting off from its feet like a rocket!

When someone needed help, Golurk flew to them. Whoosh! It flew over mountains and rivers. When a family's house was flooded, Golurk carried them to safety. When a little Pokémon was lost, Golurk found it. Golurk was very old, but it had never forgotten its job: to protect everyone, always.

Pawniard was a little Pokémon that wore a helmet and stood up very straight, like a little soldier. It was brave and loyal, and it always followed its leader.

Pawniard lived in a group with other Pawniard. They marched together, one, two, one, two, all in a line. When their leader said, "Halt!" they stopped. When their leader said, "March!" they marched. But Pawniard's favorite command was "Snack time!" Then everyone sat down in a circle and shared their berries.

Bisharp was the leader of the Pawniard. It wore a shiny helmet and stood tall and proud. All the Pawniard followed it, and they trusted it completely.

Bisharp took good care of its Pawniard. It taught them to march, to be brave and to always help each other. When one of the Pawniard fell behind, Bisharp waited. "Nobody gets left behind," it said. The Pawniard looked up to Bisharp. Someday, they hoped, they would be just as good a leader.

Bouffalant was a big buffalo Pokémon with a huge, fluffy afro on its head. Its hair was so thick and bouncy that it was like a giant pillow.

Bouffalant was very proud of its hair. It brushed it every morning until it was perfectly fluffy. Fluff, fluff! When the little Pokémon got sleepy, they climbed onto Bouffalant's head and snuggled into its fluffy hair. "It's like sleeping on a cloud," they said. Bouffalant didn't move a muscle. It didn't want to wake them up.

Rufflet was a little eagle Pokémon, and it was very, very brave. It wasn't scared of anything, not even Pokémon much bigger than itself!

Rufflet wanted to be a strong flier like the big eagles. So it practiced every day. Flap, flap, flap! It flew up the hill, then down. Up the cliff, then down. Sometimes it got tired, but it never gave up. "I'm going to be the bravest flier in the sky!" it said. And all its friends believed it.

Braviary was a big, brave eagle Pokémon with red, white and blue feathers. It was the bravest flier in the sky, and it would fly into any storm to help a friend.

When a little Rufflet got caught in a storm, Braviary didn't hesitate. It flew right into the wind and the rain, found the little Rufflet and carried it home under its wing. "Thank you, Braviary!" said the Rufflet, shivering. Braviary fluffed up its feathers to keep the little one warm. "That's what brave is for," it said.

Vullaby was a little bird Pokémon whose wings were still too small to fly. It wore a hard shell around its bottom, like a cozy little diaper, to keep it safe.

Vullaby waddled around the nest, flapping its tiny wings. Flap, flap, waddle! It couldn't fly yet, but it practiced every day. Its mother watched from a nearby branch. "Soon," she said. "Soon you'll fly." Vullaby flapped harder. And one day, it fluttered all the way to the next branch!

Mandibuzz was a big bird Pokémon that took very good care of little ones. It liked to fly over the land and keep an eye on everything.

When Mandibuzz saw a little Vullaby that needed help, it swooped down and gathered it up. It made cozy nests, collected tasty food and taught the young ones how to fly. "Flap your wings like this," it said, showing them. The little Vullaby flapped and flapped. Mandibuzz was the best teacher in the sky.

Heatmor was an anteater Pokémon with a long, hollow nose. It could breathe fire through its nose, like a little torch. Whoosh!

Heatmor used its fiery nose to toast marshmallows. Whoosh! A perfect golden marshmallow. The children at the campfire lined up with their sticks. "Me next, Heatmor!" Whoosh! Whoosh! Heatmor toasted every single marshmallow, golden and gooey. Then it sat by the fire, its nose glowing softly, while everyone ate.

Durant were steel ant Pokémon that lived in big groups. They wore shiny armor, and they worked together to build their nest.

The Durant worked all day long, digging tunnels and carrying food. March, march, march! Each Durant had a job, and they all helped each other. When one Durant found a big berry, it called the others, and they all carried it home together. "Teamwork!" they said. Their nest was the biggest, strongest nest on the whole hill.

Deino was a little dragon Pokémon that couldn't see very well. It had fluffy fur over its eyes, so it found its way by bumping into things and nibbling them.

Deino bumped into a tree. Bonk! "That's a tree." It bumped into a rock. Bonk! "That's a rock." It bumped into its friend. Bonk! "That's... a friend!" Its friend laughed. "Yes, it's me!" Deino wagged its tail. It couldn't see very well, but it always knew its friends.

Zweilous was a dragon Pokémon with two heads. The two heads didn't always get along. They both wanted to eat first, and they both wanted to lead.

"I want to go left!" said one head. "I want to go right!" said the other. They tugged in opposite directions, and Zweilous went nowhere. Then they both got hungry at the same time. "Lunch!" they said together. And they walked straight to the berry bush, finally agreeing on something.

Hydreigon was a big dragon Pokémon with three heads: one in the middle and one on each arm. It flew on six dark wings, and it was very powerful.

Each of Hydreigon's heads had its own personality. The middle head was serious. The left head was curious. The right head was a bit silly. When they flew together, the middle head steered, the left head looked around and the right head sang songs. And sometimes, just sometimes, all three heads laughed together.

Larvesta was a fuzzy white bug Pokémon with five orange horns on its head. It lived near volcanoes, and its horns could make little flames.

People said that Larvesta was a child of the sun. Its horns glowed warm, and its fuzzy body was cozy. When a little Larvesta crawled across the snow, the snow melted in its path, making a little trail. The children followed the trail and found Larvesta, warming itself in a patch of sunlight.

Volcarona was a big moth Pokémon with six fiery wings. When it flapped its wings, sparks of warm light floated down like falling stars.

Long, long ago, there was a winter so dark and so cold that the sun disappeared behind thick, gray clouds. Everyone was cold and scared. Then Volcarona came. It flapped its fiery wings, and warm, golden light filled the sky. It glowed like a second sun, keeping everyone warm until the real sun came back. People still call it the sun Pokémon.

Cobalion was a legendary Pokémon with a body as strong as steel. It was calm and wise, and it was the leader of three friends who protected the Pokémon of the land.

Long ago, when a fire swept through the forest, Cobalion and its friends Terrakion and Virizion rushed in to help. Cobalion led the way, calm and steady, guiding the young Pokémon to safety. "Stay calm," it said. "Follow me." And every single Pokémon made it out safely.

Terrakion was a legendary Pokémon with a body as strong as rock. It was the strongest of three friends who protected the Pokémon of the land.

Terrakion could break through walls of stone with a single push. Long ago, when an old castle wall fell and trapped some little Pokémon, Terrakion pushed through the stones and rescued them all. "Thank you, Terrakion!" they cried. Terrakion just nodded, shook the dust off its back and went off to see if anyone else needed help.

Virizion was a legendary Pokémon with leafy horns, as graceful as the wind. It was the quickest of three friends who protected the Pokémon of the land.

Virizion moved so fast and so lightly that it never even bent a blade of grass. When the young Pokémon of the forest needed help, Virizion was there in a flash. Swish! It guided them through the trees, quick and quiet. The forest Pokémon called it the guardian of the green, and they felt safe whenever it was near.

Tornadus was a legendary Pokémon that flew on the wind. It was green, with a long tail, and wherever it flew, big, swirly winds followed it. Whoosh!

Tornadus loved to fly fast and play with the wind. It blew the leaves around in autumn. It blew the clouds across the sky. And it blew the children's kites high, high, high into the air! "Look how high my kite is!" shouted a little girl. And somewhere up there, Tornadus laughed and blew a little harder.

Thundurus was a legendary Pokémon that flew through the stormy sky, making thunder and lightning. Crash! Boom! It loved a good storm.

Thundurus liked to fly over the farms during the summer, bringing big rumbling thunderstorms. The rain fell on the thirsty crops, and the lightning lit up the sky. Crash! Flash! The children watched from their windows, counting between the flashes and the booms. "One, two, three... BOOM!" They thought Thundurus was putting on a show, just for them.

Reshiram was a legendary white dragon with a tail like a big, glowing fire. People said it stood for truth, and that it helped people who were honest.

People told a story about Reshiram. When someone told the truth, even when it was hard, Reshiram's tail glowed bright and warm, like a sunrise. "Truth is like a light," the grown-ups said to the children. "It helps everyone see." And whenever the children told the truth, they imagined Reshiram's tail glowing, just for them.

Zekrom was a legendary black dragon with a tail that crackled with lightning. People said it stood for ideals, the big dreams that people work hard to make come true.

People told a story about Zekrom. When someone had a big dream and worked hard for it, Zekrom's tail crackled with energy. Zap! "Dream big," said the grown-ups to the children. "And work hard. Zekrom is cheering for you." And when the children had big dreams, they imagined Zekrom, crackling with lightning, cheering them on.

Landorus was a legendary Pokémon that floated on a cloud. Wherever it went, the land became rich and green, and the crops grew big and strong.

The farmers loved Landorus. When it floated over their fields, the plants grew taller, the fruit grew sweeter and the vegetables grew bigger. "Landorus came by!" they said, pointing at their giant pumpkins. Every autumn, the farmers held a harvest festival, and they always saved the biggest pumpkin for Landorus.

Kyurem was a legendary dragon Pokémon made of ice. It lived in a cold, quiet cave, and its body was so cold that the air around it froze into sparkling crystals.

Kyurem had been alone for a very long time. People said it was waiting for something to make it feel whole. One day, a little Cubchoo wandered into its cave, sniffling and shivering. "Are you lonely too?" it asked. Kyurem looked at the little Cubchoo for a long time. Then it made a little ice sculpture of a flower, just for it. It was the first gift Kyurem had ever given.

Keldeo was a young Mythical Pokémon with a horn on its head and a mane like flowing water. It was brave and full of energy, and it could run across the top of the water.

Keldeo was learning to be a hero, just like Cobalion, Terrakion and Virizion. It practiced every day, running across rivers and leaping over rocks. Splash, splash, leap! "I'm going to be the bravest hero ever!" it said. Cobalion smiled. "Being a hero isn't only about being brave," it said. "It's about being kind." Keldeo thought about that. Then it went to help a little Ducklett across the river.

Meloetta was a Mythical Pokémon who loved to sing and dance. Its voice was so beautiful that anyone who heard it felt happy, and its dancing made everyone want to dance too.

Meloetta sang songs that were sweet and gentle. Then it changed into its dancing form, and it danced so fast and so happily that everyone joined in. Twirl, leap, spin! When it was time for bed, Meloetta sang one last song, a lullaby so soft that the stars seemed to lean in to listen. La, la, la... good night.

Genesect was an ancient bug Pokémon from long, long ago. Scientists found it as a fossil, brought it back and gave it a shiny new metal body.

Genesect woke up in a world it didn't know. Everything was strange and new. It missed its old home, from long ago. But then it met some kind Pokémon who showed it the forest, the river and the stars. "This can be your home now," they said. Genesect looked around. The stars were the same ones it remembered. And it felt at home at last.

Chespin was a little green Pokémon with a hood of soft, prickly quills on its head. Usually the quills were soft, but when Chespin flexed, they turned hard and pointy!

Chespin was curious about everything. It poked its nose into flowers, peeked under leaves and chased butterflies all over the meadow. "What's that? Ooh, what's this?" When something surprised it, its quills went stiff. Boing! Then it laughed and let them go soft again. "Just checking," it said, and off it went to find something new.

Quilladin had a hard, spiky shell that protected its body, like a suit of armor. When it was scared, it curled up into a ball, and nothing could get past its spikes.

Quilladin liked to roll down hills in its ball. Roll, roll, bump! It rolled all the way to the bottom and then uncurled, dizzy and giggling. Its friends lined up at the top of the hill to watch. "Again, Quilladin!" So Quilladin climbed back up and rolled again, faster than before.

Chesnaught was a big, strong Pokémon with a spiky shell on its back. Its shell was so strong that it could protect its friends from almost anything.

When a storm came, Chesnaught gathered all the little Pokémon behind it. It curled its arms around them and held up its strong shell. The wind howled and the rain poured, but Chesnaught didn't budge. "Stay close," it said. And everyone stayed safe and dry, snuggled behind their big, strong friend.

Fennekin was a little fox Pokémon with big, fluffy ears. Its ears gave off warm air, and when it was happy, little puffs of heat came out of them. Puff, puff!

Fennekin loved to munch on twigs. Crunch, crunch! The twigs gave it energy, and its ears got even warmer. On chilly days, its friends snuggled up next to its warm ears. "Ahh, cozy," they said. Fennekin's ears puffed with happiness. It liked being the warmest friend in the forest.

Braixen was a fox Pokémon that kept a little stick tucked into its fluffy tail. When it pulled the stick out, the end lit up with a little flame, like a magic wand.

Braixen used its wand for all sorts of things. It lit candles at bedtime. It toasted berries for its friends. And it drew pictures in the air with its glowing flame, swirls and stars and flowers. Swish, swish, sparkle! The little Pokémon clapped and asked for more. "Draw a dragon!" So Braixen drew a dragon, and it glowed in the air for a whole minute.

Delphox was a tall, graceful fox Pokémon with a magic wand made of a burning branch. It could look into the flame on its wand and see pictures of the future.

When the villagers were worried about something, they asked Delphox. Delphox gazed into its flame for a long time. "Tomorrow will be sunny," it said. "And someone will find a lost kitten." And sure enough, the next day was sunny, and a little girl found her lost Espurr hiding in the bakery. Delphox smiled and twirled its wand.

Froakie was a little blue frog Pokémon covered in soft, bubbly foam. The bubbles were called frubbles, and they protected Froakie's skin.

Froakie was always ready for an adventure. It hopped and leaped and bounced through the forest, light as a feather. Hop, hop, LEAP! It could jump so high that it landed on top of trees. Its friends tried to keep up, but Froakie was just too bouncy. So it waited for them at the top, giggling, covered in frubbles.

Frogadier was a quick, nimble frog Pokémon. It could throw pebbles covered in bubbles so accurately that it could hit a target from far, far away. Plink!

Frogadier liked to practice its aim. It knocked a leaf off a branch. Plink! It rang a little bell on a fence post. Plink! It even helped the children get their ball out of a tree. Plink! Down it came. "Wow, Frogadier!" they cheered. Frogadier did a little bow and hopped away, quick as a flash.

Greninja was a ninja frog Pokémon. It moved so fast and so quietly that nobody could see it coming. Swish! One second it was here. The next, it was gone!

Greninja could make spinning stars out of water and throw them far across the lake. Whirr, splash! It liked to skip them across the water, like skipping stones. The children tried to skip stones too. Plop, plop, sink. Greninja showed them how to flick their wrists. And soon, the children's stones were skipping too. Skip, skip, skip!

Bunnelby was a little rabbit Pokémon with big ears that it used like shovels. It could dig deep holes faster than you could say "Bunnelby!"

Bunnelby liked to dig tunnels all over the meadow. Dig, dig, dig! It made little rooms underground, with doors and windows. Its friends came to visit, and Bunnelby gave them a tour. "This is the kitchen. This is the bedroom. And this is the secret room!" Its friends gasped. The secret room was full of berries. Party time!

Diggersby was a big rabbit Pokémon with huge, strong ears. Its ears were so strong that they could dig through rock, and people liked to have Diggersby help with building.

When the town needed to dig a new pond in the park, they asked Diggersby. It dug and dug, scoop, scoop, scoop, all morning long. By lunchtime, there was a big, round pond. The town filled it with water, and the children came to sail their toy boats. Diggersby sat on the edge, dipping its feet in the cool water.

Fletchling was a little red bird Pokémon with a beautiful, clear voice. It sang the most wonderful songs, and its songs were full of happiness.

Every morning, Fletchling sat on the windowsill and sang. Tweet, tweet, tweedle! The family woke up smiling. "Good morning, Fletchling!" they said. Fletchling sang a little louder. It sang until breakfast was ready, and then it got a little crumb of toast as a thank you. Then it flew away to sing to the next house.

Fletchinder was a bird Pokémon with a little fire inside its body. The warmer its fire, the faster it could fly. Zoom!

On sunny days, Fletchinder flew so fast that it was just a streak of orange in the sky. It loved to race the wind. Whoosh! On cold days, it flew a bit slower, so its friends could keep up. "Wait for us, Fletchinder!" Fletchinder slowed down and flew beside them, keeping them warm with its fiery feathers.

Talonflame was a big, fiery bird Pokémon that could fly incredibly fast. When it flew at full speed, its feathers glowed with fire, like a shooting star.

Talonflame was the fastest bird in the sky. It flew from one end of the land to the other in no time at all. Whoosh! The children on the hill saw a streak of fire across the sky. "Make a wish! It's a shooting star!" Then the streak turned around and waved its wing. "That's no star," they laughed. "That's Talonflame!"

Scatterbug was a little bug Pokémon covered in a dark powder. The powder kept it safe and helped it stay warm, even in very cold places.

Scatterbug liked to munch on leaves. Munch, munch, munch. It wasn't fussy at all. It ate leaves in the hot desert and leaves in the snowy mountains. "Don't you get cold, Scatterbug?" asked a friend. "Nope," said Scatterbug. "My powder keeps me cozy." And it went back to munching.

Spewpa was a little bug Pokémon covered in hard, bristly fur. It sat very still and waited, while its body changed on the inside.

Spewpa didn't like to be bothered. If someone poked it, its fur bristled, and it said, "Please let me rest!" Its friends learned to leave it alone. They waved hello from far away. "Bye, Spewpa! See you soon!" Spewpa didn't wave back, but it was secretly happy. Soon, very soon, it would have wings.

Vivillon was a butterfly Pokémon with beautiful patterned wings. And here's the amazing part: the pattern on its wings depended on where in the world it lived!

Vivillon from the sunny islands had bright, flowery wings. Vivillon from the snowy north had icy, sparkly wings. Vivillon from the deserts had sandy, swirly wings. When all the Vivillon met in a big meadow, it looked like a garden full of flying paintings. Every pattern was different, and every one was beautiful.

Litleo was a little lion cub Pokémon with a fiery mane. When it was excited, its mane got hotter and hotter. Sizzle!

Litleo wanted to be strong, just like the big lions in its family. So one day, it set off on an adventure to see the world. It climbed mountains, crossed rivers and made lots of new friends. When it came home, its mane was bigger and brighter. "I'm back!" it called. And its family gave it the biggest welcome-home hug ever.

Pyroar was a big lion Pokémon with a magnificent mane of fire. The Pyroar lived together in a family called a pride, and they took care of each other.

Pyroar watched over the little Litleo as they played. When the cubs got too far away, Pyroar gave a gentle roar. Roooar! The cubs came running back. At night, the whole pride curled up together under the stars, their fiery manes glowing softly, keeping the little ones warm until morning.

Flabébé was a tiny Pokémon that rode on a flower. It held on tight to its flower and never let go, because the flower gave it special power.

Flabébé floated through the garden on its flower, looking for new flowers to visit. It said hello to the roses. It said hello to the tulips. It said hello to the daisies. Each flower was a friend. And when a flower was droopy, Flabébé floated over, held on tight and gave it a little bit of its sparkle. The flower perked right up.

Floette was a little fairy Pokémon that took care of flowers. It held a flower in its hand and floated around the garden, making sure every flower was happy.

When a flower drooped, Floette gave it a drink of water. When a flower was too cold, Floette sang it a warm song. When the flowers bloomed, Floette danced around them, twirling with joy. The garden where Floette lived was the most beautiful garden in the whole town, full of every color you could imagine.

Florges was a fairy Pokémon that owned a big, beautiful flower garden. It took care of the garden for hundreds and hundreds of years.

Florges's garden was full of flowers of every color. It knew the name of every single flower, and it knew exactly what each one needed. When people came to visit, Florges showed them around. "This is the oldest rose. It was here when your great-great-grandmother was a little girl." The visitors gasped. Florges's garden was a treasure, and it would last forever.

Skiddo was a little goat Pokémon with leaves growing on its back. It could soak up sunlight through its leaves, so it hardly ever needed to eat.
